docs.title: Anti-Patterns to Avoid
docs.text: ❌ Don't ✅ Do Instead prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", ...) inline in every node prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions", advanced_mode) yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1]... repeated 5× data = parse_yaml_response(response) try: enc = tiktoken.get_encoding(...) in 3 different methods tokens = count_tokens(text) (model-calibrated) provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER") + if/else in 2 nodes provider, model, endpoint, key = resolve_llm_settings() / max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared) safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95) safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level) thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level") in a node thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "<node_key>") Redefining import re inside functions when it's already imported at the top Use the top-level import

docs.title: When to Create New Helpers
docs.text: If you find yourself writing the same block of code (≥3 lines) in 2+ nodes, extract it as a module-level helper function. Name it descriptively and add a docstring explaining what it does, what it takes, and what it returns.

docs.title: main.py Modular Design
docs.text:
main() is a short orchestrator (~40 lines). All logic is extracted into module-level functions:

Function Signature Returns Description parse_arguments () -> tuple[ArgumentParser, Namespace] (parser, args) All argparse setup; returns parser (for .error()) and parsed args resolve_mode_and_project (args) -> tuple[str, str] (mode, project_name) Handles --advanced legacy flag, derives project name from args build_shared_store (args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name) -> dict shared dict Constructs the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes resolve_thinking_plan (args) -> tuple[str, dict, list[str]] (profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides) Pure (no emit), runs before init_output() so string translation uses the plan's translate_strings level _validate_thinking_args (args, invalid_overrides) -> None — Emits ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE (exit 1), WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED (override names a node not in thinking.MODE_NODES[mode]), and WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE — after init_output() detect_llm_config (args) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int] (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length) resolve_llm_settings() + context length display_config (args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan) -> None — Emits all CFG_* strings to console (startup order) — — parse_arguments → resolve_thinking_plan → init_output(auto_translate=False) → _check_quoting_errors / _validate_thinking_args → standalone --cleanup → check_llm_auth() (exit 1 on failure) → translate_missing_strings() → notice_legacy_cache() → mode/project resolution → flow. Translation is an LLM call, so it runs only after arguments and credentials are checked. _emit_usage_summary () -> None — In finally: one LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY per provider used (llm_common.get_usage_summary(): calls, input incl. cached / cache write, output/thinking, refusals, fallbacks, truncations, cost via token_utils.format_cost), then LLM_USAGE_STEPS_HEADER and one LLM_USAGE_STEP row per step (get_step_summary(): calls, LLM-cache hits, billed vs estimated input with deviation, output/thinking, cost) _run_cleanup () -> None — Removes llm_cache_v2.json (+ .tmp), legacy llm_cache.json, llm_token_calibration.json (+ .tmp), and the logs/ directory

docs.title: Depth-First File Ordering (api-reference mode)
docs.text:
In DeterministicFileMapper.post(), chapter_order is sorted by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical within same depth). This ensures utility/leaf files are processed before orchestration files in WriteChapters, making their summaries available as previous_chapters_summary context when processing higher-level files.

shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
    chapter_order,
    key=lambda idx: (-modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep), modules[idx]["original_path"].lower()),
)

This ordering is language-agnostic — it works for any codebase (Python, C#, C++, Java, etc.) because it exploits the universal convention that utility files live in deeper directories.

docs.title: 17. LLM Providers & Thinking Flows
docs.text: Notes for AI: utils/llm_anthropic.py is the ONLY file that imports the anthropic SDK. utils/thinking.py is the ONLY place that defines per-node effort. Nodes never hard-code a thinking level.

docs.title: Thinking Plan (utils/thinking.py)
docs.text:
Every LLM call site has a NODE key. main.resolve_thinking_plan() builds shared["thinking_plan"] once: --thinking-override NODE=LEVEL > --thinking-level LEVEL (all nodes) > --thinking-profile table (+ per-mode adjustments). Nodes read their level with resolve_thinking_level(shared, "<node_key>") (falls back to shared["thinking_level"] when no plan exists).

NODE key Call site Workload filter_files DeterministicFileMapper Mechanical classification (api-reference) extract_facts ExtractFacts (per file) Extraction with verbatim quotes (api-reference) map_abstractions MapAbstractions (per batch) Extraction reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions Reasoning-heavy synthesis identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions Reasoning-heavy synthesis analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships Reasoning-heavy synthesis order_chapters OrderChapters Planning write_chapters WriteChapters (per chapter) Long-form generation chapter_summary WriteChapters (per chapter, summary_thinking_level) Mechanical summary group_modules CombineTutorial → write_mkdocs_output nav grouping Light structuring translate_strings utils/i18n.auto_translate (via init_output) Mechanical translation

Profiles (auto = balanced on ANTHROPIC, GEMINI and OPENROUTER (thinking.PROFILED_PROVIDERS), off elsewhere; off = every node None → model default):

NODE economy balanced quality max filter_files low low medium medium extract_facts low low medium medium map_abstractions low medium high xhigh reduce_abstractions medium high high max identify_abstractions medium high high max analyze_relationships low medium high xhigh order_chapters low medium high high write_chapters low medium high xhigh chapter_summary low low medium medium group_modules low medium high high translate_strings low low medium medium

Rationale: reasoning-heavy synthesis (identify/reduce) gets the most effort; relationship analysis only feeds the summary, diagram and ordering; chapter writing runs N times (hundreds in api-reference), so shipped profiles stop at high — current Claude 5 models already do strong work at medium (Opus 5.5 at medium beats Opus 5 at high on knowledge work). xhigh/max only in the explicit max profile (use when a gain has been measured).

Per-mode adjustments: economy → write_chapters=medium for advanced (design-rationale chapters, at most max_abstraction_num calls). MODE_NODES lists which nodes can run per mode (api-reference: filter_files, extract_facts, write_chapters, chapter_summary, group_modules, translate_strings; other modes: the analysis nodes + write_chapters, chapter_summary, translate_strings) — used for the config display and WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED.

Provider mapping of a level: ANTHROPIC → output_config.effort (xhigh → high on the 4.6 family; pre-4.6 models such as Haiku 4.5 → budget_tokens 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,000); GEMINI 3.x → thinking_level (per-model set, llm_config.GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS), Gemini 2.5 → thinking_budget (GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS clamped to GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES); OPENROUTER → reasoning.effort clamped to the catalog's supported_efforts, or reasoning.max_tokens for budget-only models; OLLAMA → low/medium/high. The startup display shows it as CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT (llm_config.describe_thinking_support).

docs.title: call_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_anthropic.py)
docs.text:
• Model: ANTHROPIC_MODEL, default claude-sonnet-5 (1M context, 128K output; claude-opus-5-5 for Opus 5.5). Limits from the Models API (client.models.retrieve(model) → max_input_tokens, max_tokens), cached per process; offline fallback 1M/128K (Haiku 4.5: 200K/64K) with WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP.
  • Thinking: adaptive-thinking models (Opus 5.x, Sonnet 5, Fable/Mythos, Opus 4.6–4.8, Sonnet 4.6) get thinking={"type": "adaptive"} and, when a level is set, output_config={"effort": level} (minimal → low). With no level (model default), thinking is omitted on Opus/Sonnet 4.6–4.8, where omission means no thinking; Opus/Sonnet 5.x, Fable and Mythos think adaptively either way. Sonnet 5 (the default) thinks adaptively unless told otherwise and defaults to effort high; Opus 5.5 cannot disable thinking and defaults to medium — so the plan sets effort explicitly. With --debug, display="summarized" and the summaries are written to the log file only.
  • Never sent: temperature/top_p/top_k, assistant prefill, budget_tokens on adaptive models (all 400 on Opus 5.5; Sonnet 5 rejects enabled budget thinking and non-default sampling values).
  • max_tokens (thinking counts toward it): llm_config.anthropic_planned_output(model, level) — adaptive models: ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT (minimal/low 32K, medium/high/None 64K, xhigh 96K, max 128K); Haiku 4.5 and older: ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL + 16K for the reply. input_token_budget reserves the same value. Level → effort normalization (llm_config.anthropic_effort) is shared too. ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is a hard cap: planned max_tokens = min(table, cap), and the truncation retry never exceeds it. Ceiling = min(model output cap, context − count_tokens(prompt) − ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN (2,000), cap), min 4,096; WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED only when the ceiling is < 90% of the plan. The prompt is tokenized once per call.
  • Streaming: every request uses messages.stream(...) + get_final_message() (large max_tokens never hit HTTP timeouts).
  • Refusal fallbacks: ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS=default (Opus 5.x and Fable 5.x only) → beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 + extra_body={"fallbacks": "default"} on client.beta.messages.stream; a comma-separated model list (any model, e.g. Mythos 5.1) → beta server-side-fallback-2026-06-01 + [{"model": ...}]; off disables. A fallback-served answer emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED. Cost with fallbacks sums usage.iterations, each at its own model's price; an attempt with 0 output tokens (declined before output) is unbilled.
  • Prompt caching: ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE=on adds top-level cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"}. Off by default: templates start with per-call content (chapter name, batch files), so only exact retries share a prefix — the 1.25× write cost is not repaid on single-shot calls.
  • Response: text = concatenated text blocks (thinking/fallback blocks ignored). A reply that ends with max_tokens / model_context_window_exceeded is returned as TruncatedResponse (a str subclass with truncated = True), which call_llm never caches. Refusal / truncation handling: Section 13.
  • Usage: one ledger request per billed attempt (_billed_entries: every usage.iterations entry with output under server-side fallbacks, each priced and listed under its own model; otherwise the top-level usage), recording total input (input + cache read + cache write), output, cache read/write and thinking (usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens). A refusal with no output tokens is an unbilled decline (_declined_before_output, same rule for tokens and _message_cost): recorded as one unmeasured $0 request. _billed_tokens sums the billed attempts for the debug line. The attempt that produced the message (top-level usage) feeds token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens unless a fallback model served it; the truncation retry observes once. Per request, ANTHROPIC USAGE | ... (DEBUG, dest BOTH: console with --debug) shows tokens, thinking, cache, est. cost and observed_token_ratio (billed input ÷ tiktoken count); call_llm prints the per-call LLM_CALL_USAGE line and the totals are emitted after the flow as LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY. Prices (USD/MTok in/out/cache-read) live in _PRICING; 5-minute cache writes = 1.25× input.

docs.title: Credentials & preflight (utils/llm_config.check_anthropic_auth)
docs.text:
The anthropic SDK (zero-arg anthropic.Anthropic()) resolves credentials itself: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN → the ant auth login profile (ANTHROPIC_PROFILE or the active one, stored under ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR, default %APPDATA%\Anthropic on Windows / ~/.config/anthropic elsewhere) → Workload Identity Federation. Empty variables count as unset. For OAuth profiles the SDK merges its oauth-2025-04-20 beta header with ours (fallback beta), so betas=[...] is safe.

check_anthropic_auth() -> bool (SDK-free; returns True for every other provider) runs before any LLM call in both entry points — main() (after argument validation, before translate_missing_strings() and the flow) and the utils/call_llm.py self-test (after init_output):

Step Condition Result 1 anthropic package not importable ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING (pip install -r requirements.txt) → False 2 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN non-empty (both → WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK → True 3 Federation vars (ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, _ORGANIZATION_ID, _SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID + _IDENTITY_TOKEN[_FILE]) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK → True 4 ant on PATH run ant auth status (30 s timeout, empty key vars removed from its env). Its exit code is not a health signal, so parse_ant_auth_status() reads the (active) rows of the Credentials / Workspace sections (token prefixes redacted). Active credential → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK (source + workspace) → True; none → ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN + the (redacted) status output + help → False; subprocess error/timeout → WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED → True 5 ant not on PATH stored credentials/*.json in the config dir → WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND → True; otherwise ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS + help (incl. OS-specific ANTHROPIC_AUTH_HELP_INSTALL_ANT_{WIN,MAC,LINUX}: winget install Anthropic.Ant / brew install anthropics/tap/ant / release packages, each with a go install or zip fallback) → False

Help lines: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_HELP_HEADER, _KEY (API key from platform.claude.com/settings/keys), _INSTALL_ANT_* (only when ant is missing), _LOGIN (ant auth login / ant auth status), _NOTE (leave the key unset; billed to the API org, not a Claude.ai plan). Interactive login is for your own machine; CI uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or federation.

utils/call_llm.py adds the repo root to sys.path when run as a script, so the self-test works as both python utils/call_llm.py and python -m utils.call_llm.

docs.title: call_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_gemini.py)
docs.text:
The only module that imports google-genai (>= 1.56: thinking_level MINIMAL/MEDIUM; 1.51 had LOW/HIGH only; older SDKs reject the field).

Model (prefix, longest wins) Thinking control Levels Default when omitted gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.7-flash thinking_level low, medium, high (MINIMAL errors) medium gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash(-lite) thinking_level minimal, low, medium, high medium (Flash-Lite: minimal) gemini-3.1-pro(-preview) thinking_level low, medium, high (cannot turn off) high gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash thinking_level minimal, low, medium, high minimal / high other gemini-3.x, gemini-flash-latest / gemini-pro-latest, newer families thinking_level low, medium, high — gemini-2.5-pro / -flash / -flash-lite thinking_budget 128-32,768 / 1-24,576 / 512-24,576 dynamic gemini-1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants, non-Gemini ids none (WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED) — —

Model ids are normalized first (llm_config.gemini_model_id: models/… and publishers/google/models/… prefixes stripped, lower-cased).

  • thinking_level and thinking_budget are never sent together (400). Levels outside the set clamp (WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED, once per model+level); xhigh/max → high. No level → no thinking_config (model default). include_thoughts=True only with --debug (summaries go to the log).
  • max_output_tokens = llm_config.gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit): minimal/low 32,768, else 65,536 (the 3.x / 2.5 output limit, thinking included), capped by GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Gemini's input and output limits are separate, so output is not reduced for large prompts and input_token_budget reserves only CONTEXT_MARGIN.
  • Limits: models.get (input_token_limit, output_token_limit) on AI Studio, cached; Vertex AI (SDK maps no limits) and failures → GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS (1,048,576 / 65,536; WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP).
  • One client per process: HttpOptions(timeout=GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS×1000 ms (default 1800 s, total deadline), retry_options=HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, 408/429/5xx)); Vertex via vertexai=True, project, location=GEMINI_LOCATION (default global — Gemini 3.x is not served from us-central1); AI Studio via vertexai=False, api_key.
  • Requests stream (generate_content_stream): text = non-thought parts; prompt_feedback from the first chunk; the last usage_metadata and finish_reason win. Never sends temperature/top_p/top_k (deprecated on 3.x).
  • Usage: input = prompt_token_count (incl. cached), output = candidates + thoughts (thinking is billed as output), cost from _PRICING (standard prices, AI Studio = Vertex global; >200K-prompt tier for Pro; 3.6–3.8 Flash at the introductory _INTRO_PRICING through 2026-12-31; Vertex regional endpoints +10%; unknown models → cost n/a).
  • Retired ids (GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS: id → (replacement, still aliased on AI Studio)): gemini-3-pro-preview on AI Studio → WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (served by 3.1 Pro Preview); on Vertex, and gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview anywhere → ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (preflight fails).
  • Vertex locations per model (GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS, longest prefix): 3.1 Pro / 3 Flash / 3 Pro → global; 3.8 Flash Cyber → global, us; 3.5 Flash → any (also single regions); other 3.x → global, us, eu. us / eu use the aiplatform.{us|eu}.rep.googleapis.com endpoints.

docs.title: call_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=None) -> str (utils/llm_openrouter.py)
docs.text:
Catalog-driven (llm_config.openrouter_model_info: exact id, canonical_slug, a dated canonical slug only (anthropic/claude-4.6-opus → …-20260205; looser prefixes are not matched), routing suffixes :nitro/:floor/:online/…, ~…-latest aliases via alias_target). The catalog is fetched from {OPENROUTER_BASE_URL}/v1/models and cached on success; after a failure callers get None and the fetch is retried after a 60 s cooldown (WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE once). Family checks (rejects_sampling_params, get_token_ratio) resolve aliases through the catalog, and _normalize_claude_id maps version-first ids (claude-4.7-opus → claude-opus-4-7).

Catalog reasoning Request supported_efforts list reasoning.effort = level clamped to the list (never none; WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED once) supported_efforts key missing + supports_max_tokens (e.g. Qwen 3.8 Flash) reasoning.max_tokens = 1,024 / 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,000 for minimal…max (kept below max_tokens) supported_efforts null / key missing otherwise (e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5) reasoning.effort = level (OpenRouter converts to a budget) no reasoning and not in supported_parameters no reasoning (WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED once) model not in catalog / catalog unavailable reasoning.effort = level (unverified)
  • reasoning.exclude = not --debug (reasoning is billed either way; with --debug it is logged).
  • max_tokens: openrouter_output_budget(model, level) (shared per-effort table capped by top_provider.max_completion_tokens, 32K when that is unknown, and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), clamped to context − prompt − CONTEXT_MARGIN (min 4,096). Omitted for a model missing from the catalog unless OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is set.
  • temperature (OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE, default 0.7) only when: no reasoning requested, not rejects_sampling_params(model) (Claude 4.7+/5.x, Gemini 3.x), temperature in supported_parameters, and the model is neither mandatory nor default_enabled reasoning.
  • SSE streaming (stream: true; lines split as bytes and decoded per line — str.splitlines() would break JSON containing U+2028; :-prefixed keep-alive lines skipped; read timeout OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS between events). A proxy that answers with one application/json body is parsed as a single chunk. Headers Authorization: Bearer (when a key is set). App attribution is opt-in (llm_openrouter._attribution_headers()): only when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set are HTTP-Referer (that URL), X-OpenRouter-Title and legacy X-Title ("Codebase Knowledge Builder") sent; unset → no attribution headers.
  • Usage from the final chunk: prompt / completion (incl. reasoning) / completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens / prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens/cache_write_tokens / cost (USD, authoritative; with BYOK, cost_details.upstream_inference_cost is added).
  • Claude 4.6+ through OpenRouter: effort → Anthropic output_config.effort (xhigh → high on 4.6, minimal → low); Gemini 3.x: effort → thinkingLevel.

docs.title: Shared helpers (utils/llm_common.py, SDK-free)
docs.text: TruncatedResponse(str) (truncated = True), LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider, retryable=False), the refusal memo (request_key, remember_refusal, previous_refusal), the usage ledger (record_usage(provider, model, *, input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, cache_read, cache_write, cost) — input_tokens is the TOTAL prompt tokens incl. cached for every provider, cache fields are breakdowns, cost=None counts an unpriced call; measured=False (no usage reported, or an unbilled decline) counts the request in unmeasured_calls and keeps it out of estimate-vs-billed comparisons; totals are kept per provider and per step (usage_step(step) context set by call_llm); count_event(provider, "refusals"|"fallbacks"|"truncations"), record_estimate(step, estimate, cache_hit=False), usage_snapshot(provider) / usage_delta, get_usage_summary(), get_step_summary() — entries expose unpriced_calls and cost_known), and warn_once(key, *parts). llm_anthropic re-exports TruncatedResponse / LLMRefusalError.

docs.title: Preflight for every provider (utils/llm_config.check_llm_auth)
docs.text: Called by main() and the utils/call_llm.py self-test before any LLM call; returns False (after printing instructions) when the run cannot work: - ANTHROPIC → check_anthropic_auth() (above). - GEMINI → check_gemini_config(): google-genai installed (ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING) and >= 1.56 (ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED); retired model → WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED (AI Studio alias) or ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED → False; Vertex: location not in gemini_vertex_locations(model) → WARN_GEMINI_LOCATION (lists the allowed locations), google.auth.default() must succeed (ERROR_GEMINI_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS: gcloud auth application-default login); else GEMINI_API_KEY required (ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS). Success → LLM_AUTH_OK. - OPENROUTER → check_openrouter_config(): OPENROUTER_API_KEY when the base URL is an openrouter.ai host (ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_KEY), OPENROUTER_MODEL (ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_MODEL); a catalog that cannot load → WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE (with the URL and error, e.g. a 404 from a proxy without /v1/models); a model missing from a loaded catalog → WARN_OPENROUTER_MODEL_UNKNOWN (continues). Success → LLM_AUTH_OK. - Other providers → True.

docs.text:
flowchart TD S0["Application Setup<br/>main.py"] S1["Workflow Pipeline<br/>nodes.py, flow.py"] S2["Repository Ingestion<br/>crawl_local_files.py, crawl_github_files.py, files.py, exclude_patterns.py"] S3["LLM Infrastructure & Providers<br/>llm_common.py, thinking.py, llm_config.py, token_utils.py, llm_anthropic.py, llm_gemini.py, llm_openrouter.py, call_llm.py"] S4["Documentation Synthesis & Verification<br/>facts.py, prompts.py, chapter_check.py, mkdocs.py"] S5["Console & Localization<br/>output.py, i18n.py"] S0 --> S1 S0 --> S2 S0 --> S3 S0 --> S4 S0 --> S5 S1 --> S2 S1 --> S3 S1 --> S4 S1 --> S5 S2 --> S5 S3 --> S5 S4 --> S3 S4 --> S5 S5 --> S3 classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5 class S2,S3,S4,S5 entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

Arrows point from a section to the sections its modules use. Sections used by two or more others are outlined in red.

docs.title: Application Setup
docs.text: Chapter Description main.py Serves as the primary CLI entry point and operational coordinator, translating command-line options into shared pipeline state via main(). It performs pre-flight authentication checks, invokes the workflow DAG, and guarantees teardown cleanup and telemetry logging.

docs.title: Workflow Pipeline
docs.text: Chapter Description nodes.py Implements the concrete PocketFlow processing nodes for repository ingestion, abstraction mapping, relationship analysis, AST-grounded fact extraction, and chapter drafting. It manages dynamic context-window budget planning and provides fault-tolerant retry and fallback mechanisms. flow.py Defines the directed acyclic graph workflow topology using PocketFlow via create_tutorial_flow(). It orchestrates execution routing across direct single-pass, batch map-reduce, and deterministic AST-grounded pathways with node-level retry policies.

docs.title: Repository Ingestion
docs.text: Chapter Description crawl_local_files.py Recursively traverses a local directory to discover and decode source files into an in-memory dictionary via crawl_local_files(). It prunes directories using .gitignore specifications and glob rules while enforcing maximum file-size limits. crawl_github_files.py Discovers and extracts source code from remote GitHub repositories via REST API traversal or shallow Git clones using crawl_github_files(). It filters binary assets, respects file-size ceilings, and handles API rate limits with adaptive backoff. files.py Formats master file sequences into high-density directory trees with positional indices via build_directory_tree(). It also enables selective source retrieval through get_content_for_indices(), optimizing LLM prompt token consumption. exclude_patterns.py Defines DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, a declarative set of Unix-style glob patterns for pruning irrelevant, third-party, compiled, and sensitive files. It guards downstream crawling pipelines against token waste and secret leakage without runtime side effects.

docs.title: LLM Infrastructure & Providers
docs.text: Chapter Description llm_common.py Provides provider-neutral runtime primitives, error types, and telemetry accounting for LLM calls. It standardizes context-overflow handling with TruncatedResponse, classifies policy blocks with LLMRefusalError, and tracks token usage across pipeline steps using usage_step(). thinking.py Configures and resolves model reasoning effort levels across pipeline nodes using build_thinking_plan(). It normalizes user overrides and maps abstract cognitive tiers to concrete model capabilities via clamp_level() to optimize token budgets. llm_config.py Resolves runtime model parameters, credential validation, and context ceilings across supported LLM providers via resolve_llm_settings(). It performs fail-fast authentication preflight checks using check_llm_auth() before resource-intensive crawling begins. token_utils.py Calculates token counts and dynamic prompt budgets via count_tokens() and input_token_budget(). It combines tiktoken estimation with an empirical Exponential Moving Average feedback loop in observe_prompt_tokens() to prevent context window overflow. llm_anthropic.py Adapts Anthropic Claude models via call_anthropic(), enforcing streamed HTTP transport to prevent gateway timeouts. It negotiates adaptive thinking budgets, dynamic context limits, prompt caching, and server-side fallback headers. llm_gemini.py Adapts Google Gemini models across AI Studio and Vertex AI backends through call_gemini(). It separates streamed thought traces from response text, negotiates reasoning budgets, and automatically recovers when models reject thinking controls. llm_openrouter.py Connects to the OpenRouter gateway via call_openrouter() using Server-Sent Events streaming over HTTP completions. It uses dynamic catalog introspection to negotiate reasoning effort tiers, calibrate context budgets, and classify content moderation refusals. call_llm.py Acts as the unified dispatch facade and disk caching layer for all LLM requests through call_llm(). It normalizes provider routing, memoizes completed generations to prevent redundant API costs, and suppresses repeat calls after model refusals.

docs.title: Documentation Synthesis & Verification
docs.text: Chapter Description facts.py Implements a language-agnostic static verification and symbol-resolution engine via verify_file_claims() and ModuleTable. It verifies quoted evidence against source text lines, resolves cross-module dependencies, and outputs an atomic facts.json artifact. prompts.py Manages prompt template loading, verified AST fact block formatting, and robust YAML/JSON response deserialization. It recovers from truncated or malformed LLM outputs using cascading fallback parsers like parse_yaml_response(). chapter_check.py Audits generated documentation pages using rule-based static verification via run_chapter_check(). It detects broken relative links, malformed Mermaid syntax, unclosed code fences, and undocumented or mismatched code symbols against AST facts. mkdocs.py Compiles generated documentation chapters and verified AST facts into static sites via write_mkdocs_output(). It constructs navigation structures, generates Mermaid dependency graphs, normalizes relative links, and executes automated verification checks.

docs.title: Console & Localization
docs.text: Chapter Description output.py Provides centralized console formatting, diagnostic event dispatching, and file-based logging via emit() and configure_logging(). It normalizes UTF-8 streams, buffers pre-initialization telemetry, and routes localized UI strings from tabular templates. i18n.py Automates localization of UI diagnostic messages through auto_translate(). It scans strings.csv for missing translations, dispatches batch translation requests to an LLM, and persists updated string tables without breaking runtime logging.

docs.title: flow.py
docs.text: Source: flow.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The flow.py module defines the directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflow topology for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. Built on top of the lightweight PocketFlow framework, it serves as the declarative pipeline orchestrator that wires together repository crawling, architectural analysis, factual verification, and document authoring into an executable workflow object. The module decouples the operational sequencing of tasks from their internal node execution logic, allowing individual analysis and generation steps to operate as modular units connected through operator-driven transitions.

The pipeline architecture configured in this file bifurcates repository processing into two primary paradigms governed by context window capacity and execution mode: a dynamic heuristic pipeline and a deterministic fact-based pipeline. When operating under dynamic routing, the workflow branches into either a single-pass abstraction identifier (IdentifyAbstractions) for compact codebases or a distributed map-reduce abstraction pipeline (MapAbstractions and ReduceAbstractions) for larger repositories. In parallel, when deterministic mode is enabled, the graph routes execution through DeterministicFileMapper and ExtractFacts to enforce code-grounded structural accuracy before converging on the chapter generation stages (WriteChapters and CombineTutorial).

At runtime, flow.py exposes a single factory function, create_tutorial_flow(), which instantiates all processing nodes with tailored retry budgets and backoff intervals, links their dependencies using PocketFlow's right-shift (>>) and action-channel (- "action" >>) operators, logs the graph construction event, and returns a unified Flow instance ready for invocation.

flowchart TD subgraph Ingestion["Repository Ingestion and Routing"] fetchRepo["FetchRepo"] contextRouter{"ContextRouter"} end subgraph DynamicBranch["Dynamic LLM Analysis Pipeline"] identifyAbstractions["IdentifyAbstractions"] mapAbstractions["MapAbstractions"] reduceAbstractions["ReduceAbstractions"] analyzeRelationships["AnalyzeRelationships"] orderChapters["OrderChapters"] end subgraph DeterministicBranch["Deterministic Extraction Pipeline"] deterministicMapper["DeterministicFileMapper"] extractFacts["ExtractFacts"] end subgraph Synthesis["Documentation Synthesis and Output"] writeChapters["WriteChapters"] combineTutorial["CombineTutorial"] end fetchRepo --> contextRouter contextRouter -->|"direct"| identifyAbstractions contextRouter -->|"batch"| mapAbstractions contextRouter -->|"deterministic"| deterministicMapper mapAbstractions --> reduceAbstractions identifyAbstractions --> analyzeRelationships reduceAbstractions --> analyzeRelationships analyzeRelationships --> orderChapters orderChapters --> writeChapters deterministicMapper --> extractFacts extractFacts --> writeChapters writeChapters --> combineTutorial classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class fetchRepo,identifyAbstractions,deterministicMapper,writeChapters entryNode; Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow():

Description: Instantiates and configures the complete PocketFlow execution graph responsible for generating documentation. It initializes all operational nodes with specific retry policies, establishes data flow transitions and conditional action routes, logs the graph generation event to internal diagnostic logs, and wraps the entry node into an executable Flow instance.

Parameters: This function takes no parameters.

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow instance configured with FetchRepo as the root entry point.

Raises: This factory function does not explicitly raise exceptions during graph definition; however, failures occurring during node initialization within third-party packages or invalid operator connections will raise standard runtime errors.

docs.title: Node Instantiation and Fault-Tolerance Configuration
docs.text:
fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    extract_facts = ExtractFacts(max_retries=3, wait=10)  # one small call per file; the last attempt keeps what verifies

Every stage of the documentation lifecycle is instantiated as a distinct node object. Nodes interfacing with Large Language Models (map_abstractions, reduce_abstractions, identify_abstractions, analyze_relationships, order_chapters, write_chapters, and deterministic_mapper) are configured with defensive retry policies: max_retries=5 and wait=20. This configuration accounts for upstream provider rate limits, transient connection drops, and API timeouts by enforcing exponential backoff intervals of twenty seconds across five attempts before failing.

In contrast, extract_facts is configured with a leaner retry envelope of max_retries=3 and wait=10. Because ExtractFacts iterates over repository files individually, smaller retry counts and shorter wait times prevent pipeline stalls on edge-case files while the node retains verified claims gathered on final attempts. Non-LLM infrastructure nodes—fetch_repo, context_router, and combine_tutorial—rely on local filesystem I/O and deterministic string assembly, and therefore do not require retry wrappers.

docs.title: Execution Graph Wiring and Conditional Routing
docs.text:
fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> extract_facts >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

PocketFlow overloads the Python bitwise right-shift operator (>>) and subtraction operator (-) to construct directed edges and conditional branching logic between nodes. Execution begins linearly with fetch_repo >> context_router, which ingests the codebase files and analyzes token volume. From context_router, three mutually exclusive transitions are defined: * "direct": Triggered when total repository tokens fit safely within a single context window, routing directly to identify_abstractions. * "batch": Triggered when token counts exceed single-prompt thresholds, routing to the map-reduce cluster where map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions groups files into modular domains. * "deterministic": Triggered when operating in explicit structural documentation modes (e.g., API reference or SDK reference generation), bypassing heuristic abstraction clustering in favor of deterministic_mapper.

Both dynamic abstraction branches converge into analyze_relationships, which correlates dependencies and interfaces across discovered abstractions. The workflow then orders narrative sections (order_chapters) and feeds into write_chapters. In parallel, the deterministic path executes deterministic_mapper >> extract_facts >> write_chapters, extracting ground-truth AST facts and signatures directly into the chapter writer. Finally, write_chapters >> combine_tutorial joins individual markdown files into the completed documentation suite.

docs.title: Telemetry Emission and Flow Construction
docs.text:
emit_raw("DEBUG", "create_tutorial_flow | constructed PocketFlow execution graph", dest="LOG")
    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

Once all node instances and directional transitions are mapped, the factory issues a structured diagnostic trace via emit_raw. The message is assigned the "DEBUG" category and routed specifically to the "LOG" destination, ensuring the internal log file tracks graph initialization without cluttering the interactive terminal interface. Finally, the function returns a pocketflow.Flow object with its root set to start=fetch_repo, providing the caller with an executable pipeline container.

Example: 

# Extracted directly from flow.py: instantiation, wiring, and return
flow = create_tutorial_flow()

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
The primary operational object returned by create_tutorial_flow(), declared in the external pocketflow library. It encapsulates the complete DAG topology starting from the root entry point.

Field Type Description start Node (FetchRepo) The designated entry node where graph execution begins when Flow.run() is invoked.

docs.title: Shared store keys
docs.text:
While flow.py does not declare custom dataclasses, the returned Flow relies on an in-memory dictionary (the PocketFlow shared store) passed across all connected nodes during execution. The following table describes the core schema elements populated, transformed, and read across the nodes orchestrated by this flow:

Field Type Description repo_path str Filesystem directory path or remote Git URL specifying the target codebase. files dict[str, str] Mapping of relative file paths to their UTF-8 decoded text contents, populated by FetchRepo. abstractions list[dict] Core domain abstractions discovered by IdentifyAbstractions or ReduceAbstractions. relationships list[dict] Cross-module dependencies and architectural relationships mapped by AnalyzeRelationships. chapter_order list[str] Reading order and structural chapter outlines resolved by OrderChapters. module_facts dict AST-verified symbols, line numbers, and dependencies produced by ExtractFacts. written_chapters dict[str, str] Map of chapter identifiers to generated Markdown text produced by WriteChapters. final_output str Completed documentation site or combined Markdown output generated by CombineTutorial.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Fault tolerance within flow.py is established declaratively through node parameterization rather than try...except blocks. Because LLM interactions are subject to provider latency spikes, network partition events, and upstream rate limits, the flow embeds defensive recovery directly into the node definitions:

  • Exponential Backoff and Retries: Nodes performing non-deterministic LLM operations (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) are bounded by max_retries=5 and wait=20. If an underlying provider request fails, PocketFlow traps the failure, pauses for twenty seconds, and retries the node up to five times before terminating the workflow.
  • Granular Extraction Safeguards: ExtractFacts receives an isolated retry policy (max_retries=3, wait=10). As noted by the inline comment (# one small call per file; the last attempt keeps what verifies), AST factual extraction operates per file. Setting fewer retries and shorter backoffs prevents single anomalous files from stalling the entire graph, while the node guarantees that all claims verified up to the final attempt are preserved.
  • Deterministic Execution Integrity: The deterministic non-LLM nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) execute without retry loops, allowing local filesystem exceptions, missing permissions, or invalid UTF-8 decodings to fail fast before expensive LLM completions are initiated.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the declarative workflow definitions in flow.py, main.py serves as the primary command-line interface (CLI) entry point and operational coordinator for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It manages the runtime initialization sequence, command-line parameter parsing, environment variable loading via dotenv, and pre-flight validation. Before any network requests or file crawling operations begin, the module enforces configuration consistency across language model providers, reasoning effort profiles, file filtering patterns, and output modes.

The execution lifecycle transitions through distinct operational phases: parsing arguments, resolving reasoning plans, initializing internationalized diagnostic outputs, validating credentials, preparing execution state, invoking the workflow graph, and executing guaranteed teardown. The module instantiates a shared state dictionary (shared_store) and passes it into the PocketFlow graph returned by create_tutorial_flow(). A centralized try...finally block ensures that cumulative token consumption ledgers, estimated dollar costs, and log handles are flushed and emitted even when an unhandled exception or user interrupt terminates the pipeline prematurely.

Additionally, main.py provides standalone maintenance routines. When invoked with --cleanup, it purges persistent LLM response caches, token calibration data, and log directories from disk. docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS = {"*"}

Description: The baseline wildcard pattern applied to codebase crawlers when no explicit inclusion flags (-i or --include) are provided via the CLI. It ensures that crawler adapters ingest all files within the target root directory by default, subject to default exclusion rules.

docs.title: parse_arguments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_arguments():

Description: Configures and executes the argparse.ArgumentParser instance defining the entire CLI surface of Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. It structures command-line flags into functional categories including repository source ingestion (--repo, --dir, --cleanup), documentation generation metadata (--name, --token, --output), file filtering boundaries (--include, --exclude, --max-size), LLM generation constraints (--language, --no-cache, --max-abstractions, --max-tokens), reasoning configuration (--thinking-level, --thinking-profile, --thinking-override), architectural modalities (--mode, --advanced, --mkdocs, --incremental, --force-rebuild), and execution controls (--batch, --force-batch, --debug).

Returns: * tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]: A 2-tuple containing the configured ArgumentParser instance and the parsed command-line argument namespace.

Example: 

def main():
    parser, args = parse_arguments()
    # Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
    thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
    # ...


def parse_arguments():
    """Parse and return command-line arguments."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Source: --repo or --dir (mutually exclusive but not required if --cleanup is used)
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache files. Can be used standalone or after a run.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    # ...
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50, help="Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).")
    parser.add_argument("--force-batch", action="store_true", help="Force map-reduce mode regardless of context size.")
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose debug output.")

    return parser, parser.parse_args()

The function establishes validation invariants across mutually exclusive groups and typed converters. Ingestion targets --repo and --dir are configured inside a mutually exclusive group, though neither is marked mandatory at the parser level to allow standalone --cleanup invocations. Specialized converters like _thinking_level_arg are attached to individual arguments to intercept and normalize values before they enter the runtime pipeline.

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project(args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args):

Description: Resolves documentation generation modes and derives canonical project names. It maintains backward compatibility with the legacy --advanced flag, issuing a localized warning if both --advanced and an explicit --mode are specified. If the user omits an explicit project name (-n/--name), the function extracts the basename of the local directory path or derives the repository slug from a GitHub URL (stripping trailing .git extensions). If no source is specified, it defaults to "project".

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple containing the resolved documentation mode ("tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", or "sdk") and the resolved project name string.

Example: 

def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name

The resolution logic prioritizes explicit command-line input while ensuring deterministic fallbacks. For local directories, os.path.abspath normalizes relative paths before extracting the final path segment via os.path.basename. For remote URLs, trailing slashes are trimmed, and URL segments are split to isolate the Git repository slug. This ensures that downstream file paths, log files, and cache manifests use consistent identifiers.

docs.title: build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):

Description: Assembles and returns the initial state dictionary passed to the PocketFlow workflow engine. It consolidates inputs from the parsed CLI namespace, environment-resolved credentials, normalized file inclusion/exclusion sets, reasoning effort plans, and runtime mode flags. It also initializes placeholder containers (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters) that downstream pipeline nodes populate as processing progresses.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments from parse_arguments(). * github_token (str | None): Authenticated GitHub personal access token, if resolved. * mode (str): Resolved documentation mode string. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of pipeline node keys to normalized thinking effort levels. * project_name (str): Canonical project name resolved via resolve_mode_and_project().

Returns: * dict: The shared store dictionary containing configuration options and empty output slots.

Example: 

def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": project_name,  # Resolved once in main so logs, --force-rebuild and output agree
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities: global level (legacy) + per-node plan (utils/thinking.py)
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        "thinking_plan": thinking_plan,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

The resulting dictionary serves as the single source of truth across all PocketFlow graph operations. File exclusion patterns merge user-provided sequences directly with DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS using set union semantics, ensuring standard build caches, virtual environments, binary files, and media directories are excluded by default. Output slots are initialized to empty collections to allow pipeline nodes to inspect state without encountering KeyError exceptions.

docs.title: detect_llm_config(args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args):

Description: Discovers active LLM provider configurations, models, base endpoints, credentials, and context window limits. It invokes resolve_llm_settings() from utils.llm_config to read environment settings, then determines the token context ceiling by prioritizing the explicit --max-tokens CLI parameter over the model context length returned by get_model_context_length().

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments containing optional context token overrides.

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple consisting of (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length).

Example: 

def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.llm_config import get_model_context_length

    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()
    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length

This function links static CLI parameters with dynamic environment configuration. By deferring the import of get_model_context_length, the module minimizes startup overhead when running standalone commands like --cleanup. If --max-tokens is set, dynamic remote inspection of model limits is skipped, which helps when operating in air-gapped environments or behind custom proxy configurations.

docs.title: resolve_thinking_plan(args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_thinking_plan(args):

Description: Compiles a per-node thinking plan dictionary without triggering side effects or console emissions. It resolves the documentation mode, parses command-line overrides via parse_overrides(), and identifies the active thinking profile using resolve_profile_name(). If a global --thinking-level is set, the profile is labeled "global". The function then calls build_thinking_plan() to compute the final mapping of node keys to thinking effort levels.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments containing thinking flags (--thinking-level, --thinking-profile, --thinking-override, --mode, --advanced).

Returns: * tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]: A 3-tuple containing the resolved profile name (str), the compiled node-to-effort dictionary (dict[str, str | None]), and a list of any invalid override strings encountered (list[str]).

Example: 

def resolve_thinking_plan(args):
    """Build the per-node thinking plan from --thinking-override / --thinking-level / --thinking-profile.

    Pure (no emit): runs before init_output(). Validation messages come from _validate_thinking_args().

    Returns:
        tuple[str, dict, list[str]]: (resolved profile name, {node_key: level | None}, invalid override strings)
    """
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, invalid = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    profile = "global" if args.thinking_level else resolve_profile_name(args.thinking_profile, resolve_llm_settings()[0])
    return profile, build_thinking_plan(profile, mode, args.thinking_level, overrides), invalid

The function remains purely computational with no side effects. This design ensures it can run before utils.output.init() is called, which is necessary because the output subsystem's automated translation routine uses the reasoning effort assigned to translate_strings in the returned plan. Any malformed overrides collected in the invalid list are passed to _validate_thinking_args() for formatted error reporting once the logging system is ready.

docs.title: display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):

Description: Outputs the complete runtime execution configuration to the console and log streams using localized UI message keys. It prints the source target, output language, resolved provider credentials, endpoint URLs, model identifiers, context limits, thinking allocations, tokenizer ratio calibration summaries, batch sizes, execution mode settings, cache statuses, and the active log file path.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments. * mode (str): Resolved documentation mode string. * provider (str): Resolved LLM provider identifier (e.g., "anthropic", "gemini", "openrouter", "openai"). * model_name (str): Resolved model name. * endpoint_url (str): Resolved endpoint URL. * context_length (int): Maximum context token capacity. * log_file (str): Filesystem path to the active log file. * thinking_profile (str): Resolved thinking profile name. * thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Active mapping of node keys to thinking effort levels.

Returns: * None

Example: 

def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_PROFILE", value=thinking_profile)
    if any(thinking_plan.values()):
        emit("CFG_THINKING_PLAN", value=describe_plan(thinking_plan, mode))
    emit("CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT", value=describe_thinking_support(provider, model_name))
    emit("CFG_TOKEN_RATIO", value=describe_token_ratio())
    # ...
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block

The function provides complete visibility into runtime parameters before long-running crawler or LLM operations execute. It uses utils.output.get to resolve localized boolean indicators (CFG_VALUE_ENABLED vs CFG_VALUE_DISABLED), ensuring status messages align with the user's selected language. If mode is set to "api-reference", abstraction limits are formatted using dedicated UI tokens instead of raw integer counts.

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main():

Description: The primary application orchestrator. It manages the full execution lifecycle of Codebase-Knowledge-Builder, coordinating argument parsing, configuration validation, directory preparation, workflow instantiation, and resource cleanup.

Implementation Breakdown:

docs.title: Phase 1: Argument Parsing and Initial Configuration
docs.text:
def main():
    parser, args = parse_arguments()
    # Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
    thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
    # Translation of missing strings is an LLM call: deferred until arguments and credentials are checked.
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=thinking_plan["translate_strings"],
        debug=args.debug,
        auto_translate=False,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
    _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)
The entry point begins by parsing command-line parameters and resolving the reasoning plan. Because init_output handles UI translations via LLM calls, it requires the resolved translate_strings thinking level upfront. Automatic translation is initially disabled (auto_translate=False) so argument syntax errors and quoting problems can be reported without making premature network calls. Quoting errors and invalid thinking overrides are validated immediately.

docs.title: Phase 2: Ingestion Verification and Authentication Preflight
docs.text:
# Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

    # Fail fast (with setup instructions) before crawling if the configured provider cannot authenticate
    if not check_llm_auth():
        sys.exit(1)
    translate_missing_strings()
    notice_legacy_cache()
The orchestrator confirms that an ingestion source (--dir or --repo) was provided before beginning generation, while allowing standalone --cleanup executions to bypass this requirement. It then performs an authentication preflight check via check_llm_auth(). If credentials or SDK dependencies are missing, execution aborts with exit code 1 and outputs provider-specific setup instructions. Once authentication succeeds, missing UI strings are translated and legacy cache files are checked.

docs.title: Phase 3: Token Resolution and Cache Preparation
docs.text:
# Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)
        # The verified-facts cache (ExtractFacts) lives in facts.json: docs/api/ under --mkdocs, else next to the pages
        for facts_file in (facts_path(output_base, project_name, True), facts_path(output_base, project_name, False)):
            if os.path.exists(facts_file):
                os.remove(facts_file)
                emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED_FACTS", path=facts_file)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode
    if mode == "api-reference" and args.force_batch:
        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")
        args.force_batch = False
This phase handles access tokens, project metadata, and caching rules. If --repo is targeted, it reads the access token from -t/--token or the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, logging a warning if neither is found. It validates incremental cache combinations, ensuring --force-rebuild is accompanied by --incremental and that --incremental is restricted to api-reference mode. If --force-rebuild is active, it removes .doc_cache_manifest.json and all variants of facts.json to force fresh document generation.

docs.title: Phase 4: Shared Store Setup, Pipeline Execution, and Resource Teardown
docs.text:
shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)

    # Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    try:
        tutorial_flow.run(shared)

        # Cleanup after run if requested
        if args.cleanup:
            _run_cleanup()
    finally:
        from utils.output import shutdown

        # Report spend even when the run fails — failed runs are often the expensive ones.
        try:
            _emit_usage_summary()
        except Exception as e:
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")
        shutdown()
In the final phase, main() initializes the shared state dictionary, configures persistent file logging, and prints active settings via display_config(). It then instantiates the PocketFlow DAG with create_tutorial_flow() and starts execution via tutorial_flow.run(shared). A surrounding try...finally block ensures that even if a network timeout or user interrupt occurs, _emit_usage_summary() records token spend and shutdown() flushes file loggers and resets terminal streams.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised on argument validation failures, unauthenticated provider preflights, or quoting errors.

Example: 

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: _thinking_level_arg(value)
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_level_arg(value):

Description: Custom validator and type converter for the --thinking-level argument in argparse. It strips leading and trailing whitespace and converts inputs to lowercase. Empty strings or "default" map to None, indicating the provider's default reasoning level should be used. If the value is not in THINKING_LEVELS, it raises an argparse.ArgumentTypeError.

Parameters: * value (str): Raw string value passed on the command line.

Returns: * str | None: Validated thinking level string from THINKING_LEVELS, or None if default behavior was selected.

Raises: * argparse.ArgumentTypeError: If the input does not match "default", an empty string, or an allowed value in THINKING_LEVELS.

Example: 

def _thinking_level_arg(value):
    """argparse type for --thinking-level: a level from THINKING_LEVELS; '' or 'default' → None (model default)."""
    level = value.strip().lower()
    if level in ("", "default"):
        return None
    if level not in THINKING_LEVELS:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid choice: {value!r} (choose from {', '.join(THINKING_LEVELS)}, default)")
    return level

This helper standardizes command-line values before they enter the argument namespace. By mapping empty strings and "default" directly to None, it unifies the handling of model-native default reasoning configurations across Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and OpenRouter backends.

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):

Description: Detects shell quoting errors where values passed to -e/--exclude or -i/--include accidentally swallow subsequent command-line flags. When glob patterns are misquoted in shells (for example, --exclude "dist/* "src/*" --language Vietnamese), unescaped quotes can cause the shell to treat subsequent flags as part of the pattern string. This function extracts all valid option flags directly from the ArgumentParser instance and checks if any pattern contains an embedded flag string. If a collision is detected, it emits an ERROR_QUOTING diagnostic and exits immediately with status code 1.

Parameters: * parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser instance containing all registered option flags. * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments containing exclude and include pattern lists.

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Terminated with status 1 if a swallowed flag is found inside a pattern.

Example: 

def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags.

    When users misquote patterns (e.g., --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese),
    the shell merges subsequent flags into the pattern value. This silently causes ALL following
    arguments to be ignored. We detect this by checking if any pattern value contains a known
    CLI flag string, which no legitimate file/directory pattern would ever contain.

    Flags are extracted dynamically from the argparse parser — no hardcoded list to maintain.
    """
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)

This safety check dynamically inspects the parser's registered option_strings to discover flags without requiring a hardcoded list. By checking for space-delimited flag occurrences or trailing flag suffixes within individual pattern elements, it detects swallowed CLI parameters early and prevents silent misconfigurations during crawling operations.

docs.title: _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):

Description: Audits reasoning effort flags and overrides for syntax errors and configuration conflicts. If any invalid override tokens are detected, it outputs an ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE message and exits with status code 1. It also checks whether per-node overrides target nodes that are not used by the selected documentation mode, and warns if a global --thinking-level is combined with a non-default --thinking-profile.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments. * invalid_overrides (list[str]): List of malformed NODE=LEVEL override strings identified by parse_overrides().

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Terminated with status 1 if invalid_overrides is not empty.

Example: 

def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):
    """Report malformed --thinking-override values (fatal), overrides for nodes the mode never runs,
    and --thinking-level/--thinking-profile conflicts."""
    if invalid_overrides:
        emit("ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE", value=", ".join(invalid_overrides), nodes=", ".join(NODE_KEYS), levels=", ".join(THINKING_LEVELS))
        sys.exit(1)
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, _ = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    unused = [node for node in overrides if node not in MODE_NODES[mode]]
    if unused:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED", nodes=", ".join(unused), mode=mode, active=", ".join(MODE_NODES[mode]))
    if args.thinking_level and args.thinking_profile != "auto":
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE", level=args.thinking_level, profile=args.thinking_profile)

The function runs after output logging is initialized, allowing validation diagnostics to be recorded in persistent log files. It inspects the active mode's registered node sequence via MODE_NODES[mode] to warn users when they override reasoning effort on nodes that will never execute in the selected documentation mode.

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _run_cleanup():

Description: Cleans up persistent cache files, temporary staging files, and log directories. It deletes active and legacy LLM response caches (llm_cache_v2.json, llm_cache.json), tokenizer calibration files (llm_token_calibration.json), and associated .tmp files. It also removes the logging directory configured by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs/).

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Example: 

def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in [cache_file, f"{cache_file}.tmp", LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE, f"{TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE}.tmp"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

The cleanup helper is designed to fail softly: individual file deletion errors are caught and logged using CLEANUP_FAILED without interrupting the broader cleanup process. It handles both standalone cleanup requests (python main.py --cleanup) and post-execution cleanup runs requested via --cleanup alongside generation arguments.

docs.title: _emit_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _emit_usage_summary():

Description: Compiles and outputs token consumption metrics and estimated USD costs across all language model interactions in the run. It retrieves cumulative provider records from get_usage_summary() and step-level records from get_step_summary(). For each provider, it emits total API call counts, input tokens, output tokens, thinking tokens, cache read/write tokens, estimated costs, and failure events (refusals, fallbacks, truncations). It then prints an itemized per-step usage breakdown.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Example: 

def _emit_usage_summary():
    """Emit accumulated token usage and estimated cost per provider, then the per-step breakdown."""
    from utils.llm_common import get_step_summary, get_usage_summary
    from utils.token_utils import emit_step_usage, format_cost

    for name, usage in get_usage_summary().items():
        emit(
            "LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY",
            provider=name,
            models=", ".join(usage["models"]) or "-",
            calls=f"{usage['calls']:,}",
            input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
            output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
            thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
            cache_read=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
            cache_write=f"{usage['cache_write']:,}",
            cost=format_cost(usage),
            refusals=usage["refusals"],
            fallbacks=usage["fallbacks"],
            truncations=usage["truncations"],
        )
    steps = get_step_summary()
    if steps:
        emit("LLM_USAGE_STEPS_HEADER")
        for step, usage in steps.items():
            emit_step_usage("LLM_USAGE_STEP", step, usage)

This reporting helper runs inside the main() function's finally block, ensuring token spend is surfaced even if a run aborts due to an unhandled exception or network failure. By reporting both provider-level summaries and per-step breakdowns, it helps users analyze cost distribution across different pipeline stages.

docs.title: Command-Line Quoting Error Trapping
docs.text:
The _check_quoting_errors() helper mitigates a common shell mistake where missing or unescaped quotes in -e/--exclude or -i/--include patterns cause the shell to treat subsequent CLI flags as glob strings. Because the parser's registered option_strings are dynamically extracted from parser._actions, any occurrence of a known flag string (e.g., " --language") within a pattern triggers an immediate error emission via ERROR_QUOTING and exits execution with code 1:

for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
    if not pattern_list:
        continue
    for pattern in pattern_list:
        for known_flag in known_flags:
            if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                emit(
                    "ERROR_QUOTING",
                    flag=flag_name,
                    pattern=pattern[:120],
                    embedded=known_flag,
                )
                sys.exit(1)

docs.title: Fail-Fast Provider Authentication Verification
docs.text:
To prevent unnecessary file crawling or token budgeting work when credentials are invalid, main() calls check_llm_auth() before starting ingestion:

# Fail fast (with setup instructions) before crawling if the configured provider cannot authenticate
if not check_llm_auth():
    sys.exit(1)

If the active provider's API key, project identity, or SDK installation is missing, check_llm_auth() emits provider-specific setup instructions and returns False, causing main() to exit immediately with status 1.

docs.title: Defensive Argument Validation
docs.text: The _validate_thinking_args() helper guards against invalid thinking level overrides before pipeline execution begins: * Malformed Overrides: If parse_overrides() flags syntax issues (e.g., missing = separators or invalid levels), the function emits ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE listing all valid nodes and thinking tiers, then exits with code 1. * Inactive Node Warnings: If an override targets a node not used by the selected documentation mode (such as specifying reduce_abstractions=high in api-reference mode), the function logs WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED with the list of active nodes for that mode. * Conflicting Settings: If both a global --thinking-level and a non-default --thinking-profile are specified, it logs WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE to explain that the global level takes precedence.

docs.title: Guaranteed Telemetry and Teardown
docs.text:
Workflow execution and post-run cleanup are wrapped in a comprehensive try...finally block inside main(). This guarantees that usage reporting and logging teardown run even if the pipeline encounters network errors or keyboard interrupts:

try:
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)

    # Cleanup after run if requested
    if args.cleanup:
        _run_cleanup()
finally:
    from utils.output import shutdown

    # Report spend even when the run fails — failed runs are often the expensive ones.
    try:
        _emit_usage_summary()
    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")
    shutdown()

If _emit_usage_summary() fails due to an unexpected accounting error, the exception is caught and recorded to the log file via emit_raw, allowing shutdown() to proceed and cleanly close all stream handlers.
