docs.title: nodes.py
docs.text: Source: nodes.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The nodes.py module defines the concrete processing nodes and execution lifecycle logic that power the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder documentation pipeline. Built upon the pocketflow framework's Node and BatchNode abstractions, this module houses the computational, analytical, and generative engines responsible for converting raw source code repositories into navigable, fact-verified, structured Markdown documentation suites. The module handles ingestion, context-window budget planning, abstraction decomposition, architectural relationship discovery, topological chapter ordering, AST-grounded factual extraction, incremental chapter drafting, and static site synthesis.

Architecturally, execution bifurcates into two distinct operating pathways managed by routing logic: 1. Dynamic Heuristic Pathway: Used for narrative modes (tutorial, advanced, and sdk). Repositories are evaluated by ContextRouter against context token limits. Codebases fitting within model context windows follow a single-pass extraction through IdentifyAbstractions, while larger codebases are batched across directory boundaries via MapAbstractions and unified through ReduceAbstractions. Dependencies are inferred by AnalyzeRelationships, sequenced by OrderChapters, drafted sequentially via WriteChapters with rolling context summarization, and compiled by CombineTutorial. 2. Deterministic Ground-Truth Pathway: Used for the api-reference mode. In this mode, DeterministicFileMapper maps every non-empty source file directly to a single chapter page without semantic abstraction grouping, sorting pages by directory depth to document leaf dependencies before orchestrators. Parallel static and LLM verification is executed by ExtractFacts, which validates symbol signatures, line boundaries, and cross-module dependencies against physical source files using utils.facts. These verified claims are injected into WriteChapters prompts to prevent hallucination.

docs.title: safe_exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def safe_exec(func):

Description: A function decorator designed to wrap the exec lifecycle method of any Node or BatchNode subclass with unified error handling, diagnostic telemetry emission, and exception re-raising. When an exception escapes the decorated execution method, safe_exec intercepts the error, emits a localized "NODE_RETRY_ERROR" UI event specifying the calling node's class name and error message, writes a full stack trace to the persistent log file under the "ERROR" severity channel, and re-raises the caught exception. This allows upstream PocketFlow retry policies to trigger without repeating logging boilerplate across every node.

Parameters: * func (callable): The node execution method (exec or exec_fallback) to wrap.

Returns: * callable: The wrapped execution function preserving original signature and metadata via functools.wraps.

Raises: * Exception: Re-raises any exception thrown by the underlying wrapped method after logging.

Example: 

@safe_exec
def exec(self, prep_res):
    prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
    emit("LLM_CALL_FILTER_FILES")
    log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
    response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="filter_files")
    parsed = parse_yaml_response(response)
    # ...

docs.title: emit_step_subtotals()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_step_subtotals(*steps: str) -> None:

Description: Diagnostic utility function invoked inside BatchNode.post() methods to query the runtime usage ledger in utils.llm_common and emit intermediate token consumption and financial subtotal metrics for specified pipeline operational steps. It iterates through the provided step labels, cross-references them with the snapshot returned by get_step_summary(), and formats console and log outputs via emit_step_usage.

Parameters: * *steps (str): Variable length list of pipeline step identifiers (e.g., "extract_facts", "write_chapters", "chapter_summary").

Returns: * None: Dispatches telemetry directly to output channels.

Example: 

def emit_step_subtotals(*steps: str) -> None:
    """Print the running usage subtotal of each step (batch nodes call this from post())."""
    summary = get_step_summary()
    for step in steps:
        if step in summary:
            emit_step_usage("LLM_STEP_SUBTOTAL", step, summary[step])

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):

Description: A deterministic routing and mapping node used exclusively in api-reference mode. Instead of using LLM heuristics to cluster multiple source files into conceptual abstractions, this node establishes a 1:1 mapping between each project source file and a dedicated documentation chapter. It invokes an LLM to distinguish functional source code files from package manifests and build artifacts, filters empty or whitespace-only files, records manifests in shared state, and establishes an optimal documentation order based on directory nesting depth.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Extracts the codebase files and project name from the shared store, constructs a numbered file catalog excluding empty and whitespace-only files, builds a file-filtering prompt via build_code_file_filter_prompt, resolves the reasoning thinking level for "filter_files", and returns the execution parameters.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary containing "files", "project_name", "use_cache", and "max_tokens".

Returns: * tuple: A 4-element tuple containing (prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    project_name = shared["project_name"]

    # Empty/whitespace-only files (e.g. bare __init__.py) are left out: post() skips unlisted indices,
    # so they are never documented instead of flipping in and out with the LLM's answer.
    file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data) if content.strip()])

    prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"DeterministicFileMapper prep | {len(files_data)} candidate files for filtering", dest="LOG")
    return prompt, shared.get("use_cache", True), resolve_thinking_level(shared, "filter_files"), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Dispatches the classification prompt to the LLM via call_llm to categorize project files into valid code modules and build/package manifests. Parses the returned YAML mapping using parse_yaml_response and expands ranges or composite index strings into discrete integer lists via parse_file_indices. Wrapped by @safe_exec.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The 4-element tuple returned by prep().

Returns: * tuple[list[int], list[int]]: A tuple containing (indices, manifest_indices) representing validated code files and manifest files.

Example: 

@safe_exec
def exec(self, prep_res):
    prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
    emit("LLM_CALL_FILTER_FILES")
    log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
    response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="filter_files")
    parsed = parse_yaml_response(response)
    # {code: [...], manifests: [...]}; a bare list (older reply shape) is the code list
    code = parsed.get("code") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else parsed
    manifests = parsed.get("manifests") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else []
    indices = [idx for entry in (code if isinstance(code, list) else []) for idx in parse_file_indices(entry)]
    manifest_indices = [idx for entry in (manifests if isinstance(manifests, list) else []) for idx in parse_file_indices(entry)]
    return indices, manifest_indices

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

Description: Ingests the classified file indices, discards indices for empty files or non-code assets, and registers valid manifest files under shared["manifest_files"]. For every valid code file, it instantiates an abstraction dictionary with the file's basename as its title and its POSIX path as original_path. Crucially, it sets shared["chapter_order"] by sorting chapters by descending directory depth (deepest subdirectories first, then alphabetically). This bottom-up ordering guarantees that leaf modules and utilities are analyzed and summarized before root-level orchestrators, providing rolling context for downstream chapter drafting.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): Output of prep(). * exec_res (tuple): Output of exec().

Returns: * str: The string action "default".

Example: 

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
    files = shared.get("files", [])
    code_indices, manifest_indices = exec_res
    valid_indices = set(code_indices)
    shared["manifest_files"] = sorted(
        {idx for idx in manifest_indices if 0 <= idx < len(files) and idx not in valid_indices and files[idx][1].strip()}
    )
    modules = []
    chapter_order = []
    # ...
    shared["abstractions"] = modules
    shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
        chapter_order,
        key=lambda idx: (
            -modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep),
            modules[idx]["original_path"].lower(),
        ),
    )
    shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
    emit("DONE_DETERMINISTIC_MAPPER", count=len(modules))
    return "default"

docs.title: ExtractFacts
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ExtractFacts(BatchNode):

Description: A parallel, AST-informed verification batch node operating in api-reference mode. For each module and package manifest identified by DeterministicFileMapper, this node extracts physical codebase ground truth—including declared symbols, function signatures, configuration keys, raised/caught exceptions, and cross-module import dependencies. It cross-examines LLM extraction claims against actual source code lines using utils.facts.verify_file_claims, initiates recursive follow-up passes for uncovered lines, validates cross-file import paths using ModuleTable, and compiles an atomic facts.json artifact.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS = 3 # follow-up calls per module at most, each on FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT lines not asked before

Description: Class-level integer constant defining the maximum number of iterative follow-up query rounds executed per module to extract claims from lines missed during initial extraction.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Prepares the batch work payload for code modules and manifest files. Computes a deterministic configuration signature incorporating provider, model name, reasoning effort level, and prompt template MD5 hash. Resolves previous facts from disk using load_facts when --incremental or caching is active. For each file, computes its content-specific facts_hash via utils.facts.facts_hash. If a cache hit occurs, previously validated claims and follow-up states are attached to bypass redundant LLM extraction.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * list[dict]: A collection of item configuration dictionaries prepared for batch execution.

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    template = load_prompt_template("extract_facts", mode="common")
    thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "extract_facts")
    provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    signature = f"{provider}|{model_name}|{thinking_level or 'default'}|{hashlib.md5(template.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}"
    self.facts_file = facts_path(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared["project_name"], shared.get("mkdocs", False))
    reuse = shared.get("incremental") or shared.get("use_cache", True)
    previous = load_facts(self.facts_file) if reuse else {}
    self.previous_manifests = load_facts(self.facts_file, section="manifests") if reuse else {}
    self.best = {}  # path → (found, claims) of the best attempt so far, kept when retries do worse
    # ...
    return items

docs.title: ExtractFacts.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Executes factual claim extraction for a single module item or delegates to _exec_manifest if item["kind"] == "manifest". If cached claims are present and their follow-up state did not fail, the cached record is returned immediately. Otherwise, it formats the prompt template with full source code, queries the LLM, parses claims via parse_facts_response, and checks them against source text using verify_file_claims.

The execution process follows distinct validation and retry phases: 1. Cache Validation: Reuses valid previous claims or executes follow-ups on previously failed incomplete extractions. 2. LLM Extraction & Verification: Submits un-cached modules to the LLM and runs verify_file_claims to check that claimed quote strings match source text. 3. Coverage Guard & Paraphrase Rejection: Tracks the highest claim count in self.best. If a response contains 4 or more claims but fewer than 50% can be verified in the source text, it indicates LLM hallucination or paraphrasing; the node emits "FACTS_LOW_COVERAGE" and raises a ValueError to trigger an uncached retry under PocketFlow. 4. Targeted Follow-up: Calls _follow_up on the best claims to discover symbols or imports on previously missed lines.

Parameters: * item (dict): Module extraction task descriptor from prep().

Returns: * dict: Module verification result containing path, facts hash, verified claims, follow-up metadata, and call counts.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised when verified claim coverage falls below 50% across 4+ claims during initial attempts.

Example: 

@safe_exec
def exec(self, item):
    if item.get("kind") == "manifest":
        return self._exec_manifest(item)
    if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
        emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
        followup = item["cached_followup"] if isinstance(item["cached_followup"], dict) else {"status": "none", "asked": []}
        if followup.get("status") != "failed":
            return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"], "followup": followup}
        claims, followup, calls = self._follow_up(item, item["cached_claims"], followup.get("asked") or [])
        return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": claims, "followup": followup, "followup_calls": calls}
    # ...

docs.title: ExtractFacts.exec_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):

Description: Fail-soft fallback method invoked by PocketFlow when all retry attempts for a module fail. If an earlier attempt successfully parsed and verified a subset of claims, exec_fallback recovers that best attempt from self.best, marking its follow-up status as "failed" so subsequent incremental runs can re-extract missing lines. If no claims were ever verified, it returns empty claim fields without a facts_hash, preventing unverified data from entering the cache while allowing the overall documentation pipeline to continue.

Parameters: * item (dict): The task payload that failed execution. * exc (Exception): The exception that triggered the failure.

Returns: * dict: Fallback extraction structure with partial or empty claims.

Example: 

def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
    """The best earlier attempt if one parsed; else no facts for this module this run (no hash, so the
    next run retries it). The flow goes on either way."""
    emit("WARN_FACTS_FALLBACK", name=item["path"], error=exc)
    if item.get("kind") == "manifest":
        return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": None, "claims": None}
    best = self.best.get(item["path"])
    if best is not None:  # no follow-up ran: the next run asks it
        return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": best[1], "followup": {"status": "failed", "asked": []}}
    return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": None, "claims": None}

docs.title: ExtractFacts.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):

Description: Aggregates batch extraction results across all modules and manifests. Validates manifest declarations via verify_manifest_claims, verifies code claims against file contents via verify_file_claims, instantiates a repository-wide ModuleTable, and reconciles cross-module import paths via verify_dependencies. Populates bidirectional depends_on and used_by dependency links across all modules. Computes completeness metrics (unreported vs. declined lines), constructs a schema-compliant facts document using build_facts_document, and writes it atomically to disk via save_facts. Stores the final map under shared["module_facts"] and emits running usage subtotals for "extract_facts".

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (list[dict]): The input items supplied to exec. * exec_res_list (list[dict]): Results returned across all batch executions.

Returns: * str: The string action "default".

Example: 

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
    manifest_results = [res for res in exec_res_list if res.get("kind") == "manifest"]
    exec_res_list = [res for res in exec_res_list if res.get("kind") != "manifest"]
    manifest_texts = {item["path"]: item["content"] for item in prep_res if item.get("kind") == "manifest"}
    manifests = {
        res["path"]: {
            **verify_manifest_claims(res["claims"], manifest_texts[res["path"]], res["path"]),
            "facts_hash": res["facts_hash"],
            "claims": res["claims"],
        }
        for res in manifest_results
        if res["claims"] is not None
    }
    # ...
    save_facts(self.facts_file, build_facts_document(shared["project_name"], source_commit(shared.get("local_dir")), modules, manifests))
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=self.facts_file)
    shared["module_facts"] = modules
    # ...
    return "default"

docs.title: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ContextRouter(Node):

Description: The context capacity and branching orchestrator of the pipeline. It evaluates the total token volume of the ingested codebase against model context limits, reasoning reserves, and prompt template overhead. Based on these measurements, it routes the workflow along one of three pathways: * "deterministic": Automatically selected when shared["mode"] == "api-reference". * "direct": Selected when the entire codebase fits comfortably within the effective token budget, delegating to IdentifyAbstractions. * "batch": Selected when codebase tokens exceed the effective limit or when --force-batch is specified, organizing files into directory-aligned batches for MapAbstractions.

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Evaluates token capacity and establishes routing limits through three distinct operations: 1. Mode Check: If shared["mode"] == "api-reference", returns "deterministic" immediately without spending tokens calculating capacity. 2. Overhead Calculation: Computes worst-case template token overhead across all prompt files in prompts/, measures directory tree token size, and estimates the chapter listing token load. 3. Budget Partitioning: Measures token counts for all source files in parallel via count_tokens_many. Calculates safe input headroom by subtracting reasoning reserves (for IdentifyAbstractions or MapAbstractions) and fixed prompt overhead from resolve_max_tokens(shared). Returns a decision tuple indicating whether the repository fits within direct limits or requires batching.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * tuple: Route configuration tuple containing route name, files list, effective limit, batch size, pre-calculated token map, token counter reference, and formatted directory tree.

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
    shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
    directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)

    if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
        emit("CAPACITY_API_REF_MODE")
        return ("deterministic", files_data, 0, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)
    # ...
    total_tokens = sum(file_token_map)
    safety_limit = min(
        input_token_budget(max_tokens, resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")),
        input_token_budget(max_tokens, resolve_thinking_level(shared, "map_abstractions")),
    )
    effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
    # ...

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Implements the routing decision. If the route is "direct" or "deterministic", it returns the string route name immediately. If the route is "batch", it groups files by parent directory using a defaultdict(list) and packs files into discrete sub-batches. Files from different directories are never mixed in a single batch to preserve cohesive module context. Sub-batches are split whenever adding a file would exceed effective_limit or batch_size.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The routing parameter tuple prepared by prep().

Returns: * str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]: Returns the string "direct" or "deterministic", or a list of file batches where each batch contains (index, path, content) tuples.

Example: 

def exec(self, prep_res):
    route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, _directory_tree = prep_res
    if route == "direct":
        return "direct"
    if route == "deterministic":
        return "deterministic"

    # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
    dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

    batches = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
        current_batch = []
        current_tokens = 0
        for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
            if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                batches.append(current_batch)
                current_batch = []
                current_tokens = 0
            current_batch.append((i, path, content))
            current_tokens += tokens
        if current_batch:
            batches.append(current_batch)
    return batches

docs.title: ContextRouter.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

Description: Persists the directory tree generated during prep() into shared["directory_tree"] so subsequent nodes (WriteChapters, CombineTutorial) can reference global repository topology. If batch routing was executed, it stores the packed batches in shared["file_batches"] and returns "batch". Otherwise, it returns the string action ("direct" or "deterministic") to control downstream edge traversal in the PocketFlow DAG.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): Output of prep(). * exec_res (str | list): Output of exec().

Returns: * str: Action string ("direct", "deterministic", or "batch").

Example: 

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ContextRouter post | route={'batch' if isinstance(exec_res, list) else exec_res}", dest="LOG")
    shared["directory_tree"] = prep_res[-1]
    if exec_res == "direct":
        return "direct"
    if exec_res == "deterministic":
        return "deterministic"
    shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
    return "batch"

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item):

Emits token estimation diagnostics, executes the LLM completion via call_llm, parses the YAML response, and normalizes file indices using parse_file_index.

def exec(self, item):

docs.title: MapAbstractions.post()

Description: Flattens the lists of partial abstractions returned across all executed batches, stores the aggregated collection under shared["mapped_abstractions"], and emits running token usage subtotals for "map_abstractions".

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions

Visibility: Public Signature: class ReduceAbstractions(Node):

Description: The reduction phase of the Map-Reduce pipeline. It ingests all partial abstractions identified by individual MapAbstractions batches and prompts the LLM to deduplicate, consolidate, and synthesize them into a coherent repository-wide set of primary abstractions capped by max_abstraction_num (default 10).

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Bundles mapped partial abstractions, project metadata, language preferences, cache flags, abstraction limits, and thinking effort levels into an execution tuple.

Returns: * tuple: 9-element configuration tuple.

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):

        shared["mapped_abstractions"],

        shared.get("language", "english"),

docs.title: ReduceAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Formats partial abstractions into a unified prompt using reduce_abstractions.md, dispatches the request through call_llm, parses the YAML response, and validates that every synthesized abstraction contains valid names, descriptions, and resolved file indices.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Tuple supplied by prep().

Returns: * list[dict]: List of consolidated abstraction dictionaries containing "name", "description", and "files".

Example: 

def exec(self, prep_res):
    mapped_abstractions, project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode = prep_res

    context = ""
    for i, abs_obj in enumerate(mapped_abstractions):
        context += f"- Partial Abstraction {i}: {abs_obj['name']}\n  Description: {abs_obj['description']}\n  Files: {abs_obj['files']}\n\n"

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Encapsulates context construction via an internal closure (create_llm_context). The closure iterates across files, encodes numbered file entries, tracks cumulative tokens, and stops packing files if safety_limit (derived from input_token_budget) is reached, emitting "WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED" if necessary. Generates the directory tree and returns a 12-element tuple of execution parameters.

    def create_llm_context(files_data):
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
        safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)
        context = ""

        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
            if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
                break
            context += entry
            current_tokens += entry_tokens
        return context, current_tokens

    context, context_tokens = create_llm_context(files_data)
    directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
    # ...
    return (...)

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class AnalyzeRelationships(Node):

Description: Discovers architectural relationships, data flows, and dependencies between identified abstractions. It uses a budget-aware snippet allocation algorithm to inject relevant source file excerpts into the prompt without exceeding the context window, asks the LLM to analyze interactions, and validates directed relationship edges connecting abstraction indices.

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Implements a two-pass token budget distribution algorithm to provide balanced code context across all abstractions: 1. Budget Calculation & File Sizing: Calculates remaining prompt token budget after subtracting abstraction listings and prompt overhead. Pre-computes token counts for every file referenced by each abstraction, sorting them by size descending (prioritizing major architectural modules). 2. Pass 1 (Equal Allocation): Divides total budget evenly across abstractions (per_abstr_budget = total_budget // num_abstractions). Assigns files greedily within each abstraction's share, tracking deduplicated files and unused token surpluses. 3. Pass 2 (Redistribution): Collects unused budgets from abstractions with few or small files and redistributes the surplus to abstractions with remaining unallocated files. 4. Context Assembly: Formats included files with full contents, tags deduplicated files previously shown, and prints path-only summaries for files omitted due to budget exhaustion.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary.

Returns: * tuple: 10-element parameter tuple containing context strings, abstraction listings, project metadata, and limits.

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):
    abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
    files_data = shared["files"]
    # ...
    # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
    per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
    included_indices = set()
    abstr_results = []
    for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
        budget = per_abstr_budget
        included_files = []
        remaining_files = []
        for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
            if idx in included_indices:
                included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                continue
            if tokens <= budget:
                included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                budget -= tokens
                included_indices.add(idx)
            else:
                remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
        abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))
    # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget ...
    return (...)

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Renders prompts/{mode}/identify_relationships.md with localized instructions, dispatches the prompt through call_llm, parses the YAML response, and performs boundary validation. Verifies that the returned dictionary contains string "summary" and list "relationships" entries. For every relationship, it parses the from_abstraction and to_abstraction fields using regular expressions (\d+), checks that parsed indices fall within [0, num_abstractions - 1], and records directed edges labeled with interaction descriptions. Wrapped by @safe_exec.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): 10-element configuration tuple from prep().

Returns: * dict: Relationship structure containing a high-level architectural "summary" string and a "details" list of directed edges ({"from": int, "to": int, "label": str}).

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the response is malformed, lacks required keys, or contains unparseable abstraction index references.

Example: 

@safe_exec
def exec(self, prep_res):
    # ...
    response = call_llm(
        prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="analyze_relationships"
    )
    relationships_data = parse_yaml_response(response)
    if not isinstance(relationships_data, dict) or not all(k in relationships_data for k in ["summary", "relationships"]):
        raise ValueError("LLM output is not a dict or missing keys ('summary', 'relationships')")
    # ...
    validated_relationships = []
    for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:
        from_nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["from_abstraction"]).split("#")[0].strip())
        to_nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["to_abstraction"]).split("#")[0].strip())
        from_idx, to_idx = int(from_nums[0]), int(to_nums[0])
        if not (0 <= from_idx < num_abstractions and 0 <= to_idx < num_abstractions):
            continue
        validated_relationships.append({"from": from_idx, "to": to_idx, "label": rel["label"]})
    return {"summary": relationships_data["summary"], "details": validated_relationships}

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Executes the chapter-ordering prompt via call_llm, parses the YAML response, and performs validation to verify: 1. Every entry parses to a valid integer index. 2. All indices fall within the range [0, num_abstractions - 1]. 3. No duplicate indices appear in the list. 4. The output list's length exactly matches num_abstractions.

Wrapped by @safe_exec.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Output tuple from prep().

Returns: * list[int]: Permuted list of unique abstraction indices representing the linear chapter reading order.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the output is not a list, contains invalid or duplicate indices, or omits abstractions.

Example: 

@safe_exec
def exec(self, prep_res):
    # ...
    response = call_llm(
        prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="order_chapters"
    )
    ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
    if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
        raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

    ordered_indices = []
    seen_indices = set()
    for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
        # ... index extraction and validation ...
        if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
        if idx in seen_indices:
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
        ordered_indices.append(idx)
        seen_indices.add(idx)

    if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Ordered list length ({len(ordered_indices)}) does not match number of abstractions ({num_abstractions}). Missing indices: {set(range(num_abstractions)) - seen_indices}"
        )
    return ordered_indices

Visibility: Public Signature: class WriteChapters(BatchNode):

Description: The primary chapter generation batch node. Executing sequentially across the ordered abstractions, this node drafts long-form Markdown documentation chapters using draft_chapters.md. To provide narrative continuity without triggering $O(n^2)$ token explosion, each drafted chapter is immediately summarized by the LLM into a technical brief; these briefs are carried forward as rolling context for subsequent chapters. The node supports incremental regeneration, MD5 manifest caching, verified AST fact block injection, and fail-soft fallback pages.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Drafts an individual chapter through four logical stages: 1. Incremental Manifest Cache Check: Computes an MD5 digest over the generation signature, file contents, and verified facts. If .doc_cache_manifest.json contains a matching entry, reads the existing Markdown file directly from disk, strips YAML frontmatter, loads or generates its summary, appends it to rolling state, and skips the LLM call. 2. Context Window Management: Assembles technical summaries of preceding chapters, capping total summary tokens at 50% of the model context limit (max_tokens * 0.50). Drops oldest summaries first when the budget is exceeded, inserting an omission note. 3. Chapter Drafting: Formats draft_chapters.md with file contents, directory trees, previous chapter summaries, and verified AST fact blocks. Dispatches the prompt via call_llm. If the response contains a truncated attribute, invalidates the manifest hash to force regeneration on subsequent runs. Enforces # Chapter N: Title headings. 4. Technical Summarization: Automatically submits the drafted chapter to build_chapter_summary_prompt via call_llm under step "chapter_summary", generating a 3-5 sentence brief for subsequent chapters and navigation grouping.

Returns: * dict: Output record containing "content", "hash", "name", "cache_key", "filename", and "summary".

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):

Description: Fail-soft fallback invoked when a chapter fails all retry attempts. Emits "WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK", appends an unavailability notice to self.chapter_summaries to maintain index alignment, and returns a stub page with hash: None. This guarantees that partial documentation suites can still compile while forcing the missing page to regenerate on future incremental runs.

Parameters: * item (dict): Task descriptor that failed execution. * exc (Exception): Exception that triggered failure.

Returns: * dict: Fallback dictionary with placeholder Markdown and hash: None.

Example: 

def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
    name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
    chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
    emit("WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK", chapter_num=chapter_num, name=name.strip(), error=exc)
    notice = get("UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE")
    summary = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {name.strip()}:\n{notice}"
    self.chapter_summaries.append(summary)
    return {"content": f"# {name.strip()}\n\n{notice}\n", "hash": None, "name": name, "summary": summary}

Atomically writes the pending incremental cache manifest (shared["pending_manifest"]) to .doc_cache_manifest.json by writing to a temporary file (.tmp) and calling os.replace. Emits the completion notification "GEN_COMPLETE".

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (dict): Output of prep(). * exec_res (str): Written output directory path.

Returns: * None

Example: 

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
    shared["final_output_dir"] = exec_res

    manifest = shared.get("pending_manifest")
    if shared.get("incremental") and manifest is not None:
        manifest_path = os.path.join(exec_res, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        tmp_path = f"{manifest_path}.tmp"
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
        os.replace(tmp_path, manifest_path)

    emit("GEN_COMPLETE", path=exec_res)

docs.title: ExtractFacts._exec_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _exec_manifest(self, item):

Description: Private helper method executed by ExtractFacts.exec to extract declared package identifiers, build targets, and path aliases from project configuration manifests (such as Cargo.toml, package.json, go.mod, or pyproject.toml) using prompts/common/extract_manifest.md. It validates returned YAML items against MANIFEST_KEYS. If unparsed items are detected and retries remain, it raises a ValueError to force an uncached retry; on the final retry attempt, readable claims are retained but the facts_hash is stripped so subsequent runs re-evaluate the manifest.

Parameters: * item (dict): Manifest task configuration dictionary.

Returns: * dict: Manifest result dictionary containing "kind": "manifest", "path", "facts_hash", and "claims".

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if manifest YAML parsing yields unparsed entries before the final retry.

Example: 

def _exec_manifest(self, item):
    if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
        emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
        return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"]}
    prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"])
    emit("LLM_CALL_EXTRACT_MANIFEST", name=item["path"])
    log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
    response = call_llm(
        prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="extract_facts"
    )
    claims = parse_facts_response(response, MANIFEST_KEYS)
    if claims["unparsed"] and self.cur_retry < self.max_retries - 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{claims['unparsed']} manifest items are not valid YAML")
    facts_hash = None if claims["unparsed"] else item["facts_hash"]
    return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": facts_hash, "claims": claims}

docs.title: ExtractFacts._follow_up()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):

Description: Targeted follow-up extraction loop executed when source code lines exhibiting declaration-like or import-like syntax remain uncovered by verified claims. It runs up to FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS (3) iterations. In each round, it inspects uncovered lines using completeness_hints, selects lines not previously queried, and constructs a focused note containing at most FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT source lines. Prompts are submitted to the LLM with up to 2 uncached parsing retries. Discovered claims are merged into the existing claim set via merge_claims, while requested line numbers are recorded in asked to prevent duplicate querying.

Parameters: * item (dict): Task dictionary containing source content and project metadata. * claims (dict): Initial dictionary of claims verified during the primary pass. * asked (tuple | list, optional): Collection of 1-based line numbers queried during prior runs or rounds. Defaults to ().

Returns: * tuple[dict, dict, int]: A 3-element tuple containing (merged_claims, followup_status, total_calls) where status is a dictionary structured as {"status": "done" | "none" | "failed", "asked": list[int]}.

Example: 

def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):
    asked, calls, lines = list(asked), 0, split_lines(item["content"])
    for _round in range(self.FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS):
        hints = completeness_hints(item["content"], verify_file_claims(claims, item["content"]), claims)
        already = set(asked)
        pending = [number for number in hints["uncovered"] if number not in already]
        if not pending:
            break
        note = build_facts_focus_note([(number, lines[number - 1]) for number in pending])
        prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"], focus_note=note)
        emit("FACTS_FOLLOWUP", name=item["path"], count=len(pending))
        # ... dispatch call_llm and merge_claims ...
    return claims, {"status": "done" if asked else "none", "asked": asked}, calls

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
nodes.py uses defensive validation and fault-tolerant execution patterns to prevent individual LLM failures or malformed outputs from halting the entire documentation process:

  • Decorator-Driven Logging & Retries (safe_exec): All critical exec methods are wrapped by @safe_exec. When an unhandled error occurs, it emits "NODE_RETRY_ERROR", writes the full traceback to persistent logs under "ERROR", and re-raises the exception so PocketFlow's retry policies (with exponential backoff) can retry the operation.
  • Low Coverage Rejection: In ExtractFacts.exec, if an LLM returns 4 or more claims but fewer than half match physical source lines, the engine treats this as model hallucination or paraphrasing. It emits "FACTS_LOW_COVERAGE" and raises a ValueError to trigger an uncached retry.
  • Resilient Fallback Execution (exec_fallback):
  • In ExtractFacts, if all retries fail, exec_fallback recovers the best historical attempt (the run with the highest verified claim count). If no claims were ever verified, it returns empty structures without a facts_hash, allowing downstream nodes to run while ensuring the next incremental run retries the module.
  • In WriteChapters, if chapter drafting fails across all retries, exec_fallback inserts an unavailable notice placeholder into shared["chapters"] and records a stub summary. This maintains linear chapter indexing and allows the rest of the documentation suite to compile.
  • Truncation & Manifest Invalidation: If an LLM response is tagged with truncated = True (indicating token limit cutoff via TruncatedResponse), WriteChapters retains the partial page for immediate inspection but sets current_hash = None. This excludes the truncated chapter from .doc_cache_manifest.json, guaranteeing that subsequent --incremental executions will regenerate it.
  • Atomic Manifest Updates: The incremental cache manifest is never written during intermediate node execution. Instead, CombineTutorial.post writes to a temporary file (.doc_cache_manifest.json.tmp) and swaps it into place using os.replace only after all documentation pages have been written to disk. This prevents cache poisoning if a run is aborted midway.

docs.title: call_llm.py
docs.text: Source: utils/call_llm.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/call_llm.py serves as the centralized LLM dispatch gateway and persistent caching layer for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. It abstracts multi-provider API interactions behind a unified function interface (call_llm), allowing the indexing and documentation pipelines to query models across Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and generic OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints (such as local Ollama instances) without coupling calling nodes to vendor-specific SDK semantics. The module manages environment initialization, authentication resolution, request routing, usage ledger tracking, and output validation across all LLM operations.

A core responsibility of this module is local response caching via an in-memory singleton backed by an on-disk JSON document (llm_cache_v2.json). Cache entries are keyed by a SHA-256 digest computed across the active provider, model name, normalized reasoning/thinking effort level, and prompt content. This scoped hashing prevents collisions across models and parameter configurations while removing raw prompt text from disk storage. Disk synchronization employs an atomic write-and-replace strategy using a .tmp file swap to prevent corruption during interrupted runs. Furthermore, caching guards prevent saving empty responses or truncated text resulting from output token limits (TruncatedResponse), ensuring that incomplete generations are never permanently recorded.

The module also implements execution telemetry and defensive request handling. Before dispatching remote requests, it interrogates an execution-wide ledger to detect prior unrecoverable errors (LLMRefusalError); previously refused requests are aborted immediately to prevent redundant quota consumption during node-level retry loops. During live calls, the module tracks execution duration, token estimation, prompt token alignment, thinking/reasoning token breakdowns, and ledger deltas. Real-time usage and financial estimates are emitted to diagnostic and console outputs per pipeline execution step.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: cache_file = "llm_cache_v2.json"

Description: Module-level string path defining the target file location for persistent v2 response caching. Cache records within this file map SHA-256 hashes to cached response strings.

docs.title: LEGACY_CACHE_FILE
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: LEGACY_CACHE_FILE = "llm_cache.json"

Description: Module-level string constant defining the file path for the legacy pre-v2 cache. This file keyed cache records directly by raw prompt text. It is never read during pipeline runs, but is referenced for legacy cache warnings and cleanups.

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache():

Description: Loads the persistent cache from disk into the in-memory singleton _cache. If _cache is already populated, it returns immediately to eliminate redundant disk I/O and JSON parsing overhead across repeated LLM queries. If the cache file does not exist, it initializes _cache as an empty dictionary. When I/O or decoding errors occur, it logs a warning via utils.output.emit and returns an empty dictionary.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * dict: In-memory dictionary mapping SHA-256 cache keys to previously generated LLM string responses.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly; FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, and OSError are caught and handled internally.

Example: 

cache = load_cache()
if key in cache:
    cached_response = cache[key]


def load_cache():
    global _cache
    if _cache is not None:
        return _cache
    try:
        with open(cache_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            _cache = json.load(f)
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("CACHE_LOADED", count=f"{len(_cache):,}", file=cache_file)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        _cache = {}
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        emit("WARN_CACHE_LOAD_FAIL")
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache load error: {e}", dest="LOG")
        _cache = {}
    return _cache

The function verifies whether _cache is initialized before opening cache_file using UTF-8 encoding. If successfully loaded, it emits a CACHE_LOADED event with formatted entry counts. Missing files are treated as benign empty caches, whereas deserialization or file permission failures trigger warning logs before initializing an empty dictionary fallback.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache):

Description: Persists the provided cache dictionary to disk atomically. It updates the internal global _cache reference, serializes the JSON structure into an adjacent temporary file (llm_cache_v2.json.tmp), and executes an atomic replacement via os.replace. This atomic file swap ensures that interrupting the process mid-write does not leave a truncated or corrupted cache file on disk.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The full cache dictionary mapping cache keys to LLM response strings.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly; OSError and TypeError exceptions are caught, triggering diagnostic warnings through utils.output.emit.

Example: 

cache = load_cache()
cache[key] = response_text
save_cache(cache)


def save_cache(cache):
    global _cache
    _cache = cache
    # Write to a temp file and atomically replace, so an interrupted run never leaves a truncated cache.
    tmp_path = f"{cache_file}.tmp"
    try:
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
        os.replace(tmp_path, cache_file)
    except (OSError, TypeError) as e:
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        emit("WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL")
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Cache save error: {e}", dest="LOG")

The function assigns cache to the global _cache pointer and writes the serialized dictionary into tmp_path. Upon successful file closure, os.replace atomically updates cache_file. If an I/O failure or serialization error occurs during this process, the failure is caught, and WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL is emitted to prevent terminating active pipeline execution.

docs.title: notice_legacy_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:

Description: Inspects the local filesystem for the existence of LEGACY_CACHE_FILE (llm_cache.json). Because the v2 pipeline uses hash-scoped entries in llm_cache_v2.json, pre-v2 cache files are obsolete and consume disk space without being read. If detected, the function calculates the file size in megabytes and triggers an informational notification suggesting cleanup.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; OSError (e.g., file not found or permission denied) is silently caught and ignored.

Example: 

# Invoked during startup / self-test preflight checks
notice_legacy_cache()


def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:
    """Point out a leftover pre-v2 cache file: it is never read, so it only takes disk space."""
    try:
        size = os.path.getsize(LEGACY_CACHE_FILE)
    except OSError:
        return
    from utils.output import emit

    emit("CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND", file=LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, size=f"{size / 1_048_576:,.1f}", current=cache_file)

The function performs an os.path.getsize query on LEGACY_CACHE_FILE. If the file does not exist, an OSError is raised internally and caught, returning None. If the legacy file exists, emit sends a CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND event displaying the legacy file path, its size in megabytes, and the name of the active cache file.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None, step: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a single prompt string to the currently configured LLM provider, providing persistent disk caching, token tracking, retry-refusal detection, and provider routing. The function serves as the central API entry point for all generation tasks in the system.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt to transmit to the language model. * use_cache (bool, optional): Flag indicating whether to query and write to the local cache. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort or budget (e.g., 'low', 'medium', 'high'). Defaults to None. * step (str | None, optional): Pipeline execution step identifier corresponding to NODE_KEYS in utils/thinking.py for telemetry attribution. Defaults to None (mapped internally to 'other').

Returns: * str: The completion text generated by the model or retrieved from cache. If truncated, an instance of TruncatedResponse (a str subclass) is returned.

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: If the provider rejects the request with an unrecoverable refusal or if the request was previously refused during the same run. * ValueError: If required environment variables are missing or provider configurations are invalid. * RuntimeError: If an API response payload lacks expected completion structures. * ImportError: If provider-specific client libraries (anthropic, google-genai) are missing. * Exception: If communication with the remote provider encounters fatal HTTP, timeout, or transport errors.

Example: 

from utils.call_llm import call_llm

response = call_llm(
    prompt="Explain the architecture of this project.",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level="high",
    step="draft_chapters",
)

docs.title: Phase 1: Context Initialization and Cache Lookup
docs.text:
step = step or "other"
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"{'=' * 80}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}", dest="LOG")

    # Check cache if enabled
    key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if key in cache:
            cached_response = cache[key]
            emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)
            emit("LLM_CALL_CACHED", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}", dest="LOG")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit", dest="LOG")
            return cached_response
        emit("CACHE_MISS")

The function defaults the pipeline step to "other" if unspecified, resolves active LLM credentials and model definitions using utils/llm_config.py, and counts prompt tokens via memoized utilities in utils/token_utils.py. If caching is enabled, it generates a deterministic cache key via _cache_key. When a cache hit occurs, it logs the hit, updates pipeline token estimates with record_estimate, emits cached call notifications, logs full debug payloads to the log destination, and immediately returns the cached text.

docs.title: Phase 2: Refusal Check
docs.text:
# A request the provider already declined this run is declined again: do not re-send it on
    # node retries (rate limits, billed partial output). The node retry still sees the error.
    refusal_key = request_key(provider, model, thinking_level, prompt)
    refused = previous_refusal(refusal_key)
    if refused is not None:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=refused_before (not re-sent)", dest="LOG")
        raise refused

Before dispatching an HTTP request, the function builds a refusal tracking key via request_key from utils/llm_common.py. It checks whether this exact request previously triggered a non-retryable refusal during the current pipeline session. If found, it writes a debug log and re-raises the recorded LLMRefusalError, preventing wasted token quotas or repetitive wait times caused by node-level retry loops.

docs.title: Phase 3: Provider Invocation and Execution Tracking
docs.text:
# Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...", dest="LOG")

    # Usage of this call = ledger delta for the provider: it includes every billed request the call
    # made (Anthropic truncation retry, resend after fallbacks were disabled), even when it raises.
    before = usage_snapshot(provider)
    returned = False
    try:
        with usage_step(step):
            if provider == "GEMINI":
                response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "ANTHROPIC":
                response_text = _call_llm_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "OPENROUTER":
                response_text = _call_llm_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
                response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        returned = True
    except LLMRefusalError as e:
        if not e.retryable:
            remember_refusal(refusal_key, e)
        raise

The function captures a timestamp and takes a snapshot of the provider's token consumption ledger via usage_snapshot. It wraps provider execution within a usage_step context manager to attribute usage accurately. Based on the resolved provider string ("GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC", "OPENROUTER", or generic fallback), it routes the call to the corresponding specialized helper. If an LLMRefusalError is raised and marked as non-retryable, the exception is stored in memory via remember_refusal before being re-raised.

docs.title: Phase 4: Ledger Delta Accounting and Telemetry
docs.text:
finally:
        call_usage = usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider))
        measured = call_usage["calls"] - call_usage["unmeasured_calls"]
        if measured:
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens * measured)
            _emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)
        elif returned:  # answered, but the provider reported no usage
            emit("LLM_CALL_USAGE_MISSING", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}", dest="LOG")

The finally block guarantees that provider ledger deltas are evaluated regardless of whether the call succeeded, failed, or was truncated. It computes call_usage by comparing ledger snapshots taken before and after execution via usage_delta. If measured calls exist, it attributes input estimates and calls _emit_call_usage to print console statistics. If the provider returned a response without reporting usage metrics, an LLM_CALL_USAGE_MISSING warning is emitted. Total elapsed execution time and response character lengths are logged for debugging.

docs.title: Phase 5: Response Persistence and Cache Eviction Guard
docs.text:
# Update cache if enabled. Empty and truncated responses (llm_common.TruncatedResponse)
    # are never cached — they would be replayed on every later run.
    if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[key] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s", dest="LOG")
    return response_text

The final phase evaluates whether the result qualifies for caching. Empty strings and responses tagged with truncated=True (indicating that the model ran out of output tokens before completing) are excluded from the cache to prevent persisting partial generations. Valid responses are added to the cache dictionary and persisted to disk via save_cache.

docs.title: _cache
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: _cache = None

Description: Internal module-level cache singleton holding the in-memory representation of llm_cache_v2.json. Initialized to None, it is loaded lazily on the first invocation of load_cache or call_llm.

docs.title: _cache_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:

Description: Constructs a deterministic SHA-256 hexadecimal digest that uniquely identifies a generation request. The digest scopes the prompt to its operational configuration: provider, model name, and lowercased reasoning level (defaulting to "default" if None). Scoping prevents cache collisions when switching between models, providers, or reasoning levels.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw prompt string. * provider (str): Name of the active LLM provider (e.g., 'GEMINI', 'ANTHROPIC', 'OLLAMA'). * model (str): Specific model identifier (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-5'). * thinking_level (str | None): Desired reasoning effort level.

Returns: * str: A 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 string.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Example: 

key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)


def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The helper formats the prefix scope string by joining the provider name, model identifier, and normalized thinking level, delimited by pipe characters and terminated with a newline. It appends the raw prompt text, encodes the concatenated string to UTF-8, and computes the SHA-256 digest via Python's standard hashlib library.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Implements a generic HTTP client for communicating with OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints (such as Ollama or custom local proxies). It dynamically resolves provider configurations from environment variables, prepares request payloads and headers, handles Ollama reasoning effort parameters, strips unsupported sampling parameters for specific models, and processes JSON responses.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The prompt string to transmit. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The response text generated by the remote API. Returns an instance of TruncatedResponse if the model ceased generation due to token limits (finish_reason == "length").

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, <provider>_MODEL, <provider>_BASE_URL) are missing, or if the server returns non-JSON data. * RuntimeError: If the returned JSON payload is missing the expected choices array. * Exception: If HTTP status codes indicate an error, network connections fail, or the request times out.

Example: 

# Internal invocation from call_llm when provider is OLLAMA or other generic endpoints
response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment and Configuration Resolution
docs.text:
# Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    # Read the provider-specific variables
    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

    # Validate required variables
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    # Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

The function reads the active provider via get_llm_provider(). It builds dynamic environment variable keys based on the provider name (e.g., OLLAMA_MODEL, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_API_KEY) and fetches their values. It verifies that both the model and base URL are non-empty, raising descriptive ValueError exceptions if missing. Finally, it constructs the OpenAI-standard /v1/chat/completions endpoint URL.

docs.title: Phase 2: Request Payload and Parameter Normalization
docs.text:
# Configure headers and payload based on provider
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        # Ollama reasoning models accept low/medium/high; xhigh/max clamp to high.
        # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
        effort = _clamp_level(thinking_level.lower(), ["low", "medium", "high"]) or "medium"
        payload["think"] = effort
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    if rejects_sampling_params(model):
        # Claude Opus 4.7+ / Opus 5.x / Sonnet 5 / Fable reject sampling parameters (400).
        payload.pop("temperature", None)

The function builds the JSON request headers, including an Authorization: Bearer <api_key> header if a key is defined. It initializes the JSON payload with target model name, user message content, and default temperature (0.7). If the provider is "OLLAMA" and a thinking level is requested, it normalizes and clamps the level to low, medium, or high via _clamp_level, assigning both think and reasoning_effort keys and setting temperature to 1.0. For reasoning models that reject sampling parameters according to rejects_sampling_params, it strips the temperature parameter entirely.

docs.title: Phase 3: HTTP Transmission and Error Handling
docs.text:
try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        response.raise_for_status()  # HTTP status first: an HTML 502 page must not look like a JSON bug
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit

            emit(
                "WARN_INVALID_JSON",
                status_code=response.status_code,
                preview=response.text[:200].strip(),
            )
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
// ...
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

Network transmission is executed via requests.post with a connection timeout of 10 seconds and read timeout of 300 seconds. It evaluates HTTP status codes immediately via response.raise_for_status(), ensuring HTML error bodies from load balancers (such as 502 Bad Gateway) are not misdiagnosed as JSON decoding errors. If deserialization fails, diagnostic warnings displaying the HTTP status code and a truncated preview are emitted. Various network and HTTP exception types are caught and transformed into descriptive Exception instances.

docs.title: Phase 4: Response Validation, Token Telemetry, and Truncation Detection
docs.text:
# Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            from utils.output import emit

            emit("WARN_API_NO_CHOICES", detail=str(error_detail))
            raise RuntimeError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        usage = response_json.get("usage") or {}
        from utils.llm_common import record_usage
        from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, observe_prompt_tokens

        prompt_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
        record_usage(
            provider,
            model,
            input_tokens=prompt_tokens,
            output_tokens=usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0,
            thinking_tokens=(usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0,
            cache_read=(usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens") or 0,
            cost=None,
            measured=bool(usage),
        )
        if usage:
            observe_prompt_tokens(provider, model, count_tokens_raw(prompt), prompt_tokens)
        choice = response_json["choices"][0]
        text = (choice.get("message") or {}).get("content") or ""
        if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
            from utils.llm_common import TruncatedResponse

            return TruncatedResponse(text)
        return text

The function validates that choices is present and non-empty in the returned JSON, guarding against HTTP 200 responses that carry embedded rate-limit or quota error bodies. It extracts token usage details (prompt tokens, completion tokens, reasoning tokens, and cache hits) and logs them to the ledger using record_usage and observe_prompt_tokens. It extracts the generated message content from choices[0]. If finish_reason is "length", the text is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse object so callers can detect output exhaustion.

docs.title: _emit_call_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:

Description: Emits a formatted single-line telemetry log to the console and logging systems at the conclusion of an LLM call. It formats billed input tokens against estimated tokens, calculates deviation percentages, logs output and thinking/reasoning token volumes, displays cache read hits, and formats financial costs.

Parameters: * step (str): The pipeline execution step identifier (e.g., 'draft_chapters'). * estimate (int): The estimated input prompt token count. * usage (dict): Ledger delta dictionary containing actual token metrics for the call. * measured (int): Count of underlying HTTP requests that reported concrete token usage.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Example: 

_emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)


def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:
    """One console line per LLM call: billed input vs the estimate, output (thinking), cached, cost.
    `measured` = requests with provider-reported usage (the deviation is per measured request)."""
    from utils.output import emit, get
    from utils.token_utils import format_cost

    per_request = usage["input"] / measured
    deviation = f"{(per_request - estimate) / estimate:+.0%}" if estimate else get("CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN")
    emit(
        "LLM_CALL_USAGE",
        step=step,
        input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
        estimate=f"{estimate:,}",
        deviation=deviation,
        requests=get("LLM_CALL_REQUESTS", count=measured) if measured > 1 else "",
        output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
        thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
        cached=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
        cost=format_cost(usage),
    )

The helper calculates average per-request input tokens by dividing usage["input"] by measured. It calculates percentage deviation between estimated prompt tokens and billed input tokens. Finally, it triggers an LLM_CALL_USAGE event via utils.output.emit, formatting integer values with comma separators and appending formatted financial metrics calculated by format_cost.

docs.title: Usage Ledger Delta Dictionary
docs.text:
Returned by usage_delta in utils/llm_common.py and passed into _emit_call_usage.

Field Type Description input int Total billed input/prompt tokens recorded for the invocation. output int Total billed completion/output tokens generated. thinking int Number of tokens consumed by the model's internal reasoning phase. cache_read int Number of prompt tokens read from provider-side prompt caching. calls int Total number of HTTP/API calls made during this invocation. unmeasured_calls int Number of calls completed without usage metrics reported by the provider. cost float \| None Financial cost incurred for the call, or None if unavailable.

Example structure: 

{
    "input": 12500,
    "output": 1850,
    "thinking": 620,
    "cache_read": 8000,
    "calls": 1,
    "unmeasured_calls": 0,
    "cost": 0.0125
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/call_llm.py enforces structured defensive programming patterns to handle network volatility, provider rate limits, model refusals, and local cache I/O errors:

  • Non-Retryable Refusal Suppression: When a provider rejects an operation due to policy, context overflows, or unsupported parameters, an LLMRefusalError is raised. If e.retryable is False, the error is recorded via remember_refusal using a request hash. Subsequent retries during the same run fail immediately at Phase 2 of call_llm, preventing repeated remote calls.
  • Network & HTTP Error Normalization: In _call_llm_provider, raw requests.exceptions (HTTPError, ConnectionError, Timeout, RequestException) are caught and wrapped in informative Exception instances. Before parsing JSON payloads, response.raise_for_status() is called to intercept HTML error pages (e.g., 502/504 gateway timeouts) and prevent misleading JSON decoding errors.
  • Defensive JSON Payload Validation: Generic endpoints returning HTTP 200 may still include error bodies or omit completion results. If the deserialized JSON lacks the choices attribute or contains an empty choice list, the module emits a WARN_API_NO_CHOICES warning and raises a RuntimeError.
  • Atomic Cache Persistence: Cache writes in save_cache are performed via an intermediary .tmp file and replaced using os.replace. If a serialization or filesystem error (OSError, TypeError) occurs, a WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL event is emitted without interrupting execution.
  • Truncation Protection: Responses marked with finish_reason == "length" return as TruncatedResponse instances. The caching logic inspects getattr(response_text, "truncated", False) and skips writing them to disk, preventing permanent caching of incomplete code or chapter drafts.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/chapter_check.py module provides deterministic, rule-based verification for generated documentation chapters across the codebase. Operating strictly without LLM invocations, it executes static inspection over Markdown pages and reports discrepancies without modifying files on disk. Its primary responsibility is quality assurance: validating that generated documentation adheres to structural constraints, maintains valid navigation links, provides syntax-valid Mermaid diagrams, leaves no code fences open, and faithfully documents verified source code facts extracted by utils.facts.

The verification engine operates at two distinct tiers. The first tier applies universal syntactic checks to every Markdown page, including MkDocs link resolution against the generated file tree, fence balance tracking, and AST-level lexical validation of Mermaid diagram definitions. The second tier activates for pages associated with verified facts extracted from source code (e.g., API references). It validates factual alignment by identifying omitted symbols, detecting signature divergence (such as parameter additions, renamings, or unauthorized embellishments like hallucinated type annotations), flagging fabricated type names in section headings, and comparing See Also links against verified module dependency graphs.

All findings are aggregated at runtime into an uncommitted inspection report (chapter_check.json) and emitted via utils.output as human-readable warnings and CLI summary telemetry.
