Visibility: Private Signature: def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Identifies the primary root or entry module for a package rule.

Parameters: * package (dict): Manifest package rule dictionary. * under (list[str]): Module paths located within the package directory. * source_path (str): Path of the importing file. * source_words (set): Identifier tokens in the importing file.

Returns: * list[str]: Single-item list containing the package root module path, or a list of referenced modules within the package.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

roots = table._package_root(pkg_rule, pkg_files, "app.py", words)
The helper checks for an explicit entry path declared in the manifest. If none is specified, it scans standard source directories (src, lib) for index files or files named after the package.

docs.title: ModuleTable._corroborated()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:

Description: Confirms that a partial path suffix match is supported by contextual evidence, preventing false-positive matches on common filenames.

Parameters: * target (str): Original import target string. * parts (list[str]): Normalized segments of the target. * size (int): Number of trailing segments that matched. * path (str): Matched module path. * source_path (str): Importing module path. * source_words (set): Identifier tokens in the importing file.

Returns: * bool: True if the match is corroborated by aliases, namespaces, directory relationships, or shared symbols, otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

ok = table._corroborated("store.errors", ["store", "errors"], 1, "lib/errors.py", "main.py", words)
When a match drops leading segments of a qualified target (e.g., matching errors from store.errors), this check requires corroboration: the target must match a path alias, the module must declare the dropped namespace, or the caller must use symbols owned by the module. Similarly, bare name matches outside the importing file's directory tree require corroborating symbol usage.

docs.title: _names_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a module name appears within an evidence line as part of a path or qualified reference, rather than as an arbitrary identifier.

Parameters: * evidence (str): Source evidence line. * name (str): Target module stem name. * extension (str): Expected file extension. * extensions (set): Set of all known project extensions.

Returns: * bool: True if the name appears in a path context, otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

is_path = _names_path("const x = require('./utils.js');", "utils", ".js", exts)
The helper scans occurrences of name in the evidence string. It verifies that the occurrence is bounded by path qualifiers (/, \, ., :, quotes, brackets) or followed by its expected extension, avoiding false matches on variable names or parameters (e.g., exclude_patterns=None).

docs.title: _plain_occurrence()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a name appears in an evidence line without being immediately followed by a different documented file extension.

Parameters: * evidence (str): Quoted line of evidence. * name (str): Target module stem name. * extension (str): Expected file extension. * extensions (set): All project file extensions.

Returns: * bool: True if the name appears without referencing a different file, otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

ok = _plain_occurrence("import socket from 'socket.h'", "socket", ".cpp", {".cpp", ".h"})
This check ensures that referencing a header file like socket.h does not count as evidence for a companion implementation file like socket.cpp when both extensions exist in the project.

docs.title: _names_directory()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether an evidence line references a directory by its terminal segments in a path or dotted namespace context.

Parameters: * evidence (str): Quoted evidence line. * directory (str): Candidate directory path.

Returns: * bool: True if the directory's terminal segments appear as a path or namespace in the evidence, otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

matches = _names_directory("import com.acme.billing.*", "src/com/acme/billing")
The helper extracts the last two segments of the directory path and checks for their sequential occurrence joined by path or namespace separators (/, \, ., ::), supporting wildcard and package imports.

docs.title: _import_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether an evidence string begins with an import-related keyword after stripping modifiers and annotations.

Parameters: * evidence (str): Source evidence line.

Returns: * bool: True if the line opens with an import keyword, otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

is_imp = _import_like("pub use crate::store::Repo;") # True
The helper strips leading annotations and visibility modifiers, then checks whether the first remaining word belongs to _IMPORT_WORDS.

docs.title: _without_bindings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:

Description: Strips local alias bindings (as alias, => alias, = alias) from an import line so that only the imported module specifier remains.

Parameters: * line (str): Source import line.

Returns: * str: Cleaned import line with alias bindings removed.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

cleaned = _without_bindings("from app import models as billing")
# "from app import models  "
The helper uses regular expressions to remove import aliases. This ensures that checks in target_written() evaluate the imported target rather than local variable names.

docs.title: _bare_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:

Description: Strips leading relative path notation (./, ../) and root slashes from a path string.

Parameters: * text (str): Path string.

Returns: * str: Path string without leading relative dots or slashes.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

bare = _bare_path("../utils/facts.py") # "utils/facts.py"
The regex ^(?:\.{1,2}/|/|\.+)+ removes relative path navigation tokens, allowing relative and absolute path specifiers to be compared on equal footing.

docs.title: _imports_target()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies that an evidence line imports a target module through an import statement, Go import block, quoted specifier, or inline qualified code reference.

Parameters: * evidence (str): Quoted evidence text. * target (str): Claimed target string.

Returns: * bool: True if the target is genuinely imported or accessed via qualified syntax, otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

valid = _imports_target("const api = require('@acme/api');", "@acme/api")
The function checks whether the line contains an import statement, matches Go import block syntax, or contains the target inside quotes. It also inspects code lines (ignoring comments) for inline qualified access (e.g., shop_core::money::total()), while excluding mentions inside log strings or comments.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module employs defensive, fail-soft error handling patterns designed to keep verification running across imperfect LLM extractions and varied repository structures:

  • Atomic File Replacement: save_facts() writes data to a .tmp sibling file before calling os.replace. This prevents half-written or corrupted JSON artifacts from persisting if the process is terminated mid-write.
  • Tolerant Deserialization: load_facts() catches both OSError and ValueError (which includes json.JSONDecodeError). If reading fails or the schema version does not match FACTS_SCHEMA, it returns an empty dictionary, allowing the pipeline to re-extract facts smoothly.
  • Subprocess Isolation: source_commit() executes git rev-parse HEAD inside a try...except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) block with a 10-second timeout. If Git is not installed, the directory is not a Git repository, or the command times out, it returns None rather than raising an unhandled exception.
  • Malformed LLM Output Tolerance: All extraction helpers (_as_text(), _claim_list(), verify_file_claims(), verify_manifest_claims()) validate data types before accessing dictionary keys. Non-dictionary items in arrays are filtered out, and unparsed YAML/JSON markers are captured as "unparsed" rejections, ensuring that schema-checking continues even when LLM output is malformed.
  • Safe Character Decoding: Text operations use Unicode NFC normalization via unicodedata.normalize("NFC", ...). The module avoids standard str.splitlines() in split_lines() to prevent non-standard Unicode boundary characters (such as form feeds or vertical tabs) from desynchronizing line counts with GitHub and code editors.

docs.title: files.py
docs.text: Source: utils/files.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/files.py module provides foundational in-memory file aggregation, structural layout rendering, and targeted content extraction utilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Operating without internal project dependencies, it serves as a lightweight data presentation layer situated between repository crawlers (such as local directory scanners or remote GitHub extractors) and the pipeline's LLM-driven analysis nodes. Its primary responsibility is to transform flat sequences of ingested file tuples into compact, high-density structural representations and indexed lookup dictionaries tailored for LLM prompt ingestion.

The module provides two public functions: build_directory_tree and get_content_for_indices. build_directory_tree groups individual file paths by their directory containers using os.path.dirname, annotates each file basename with its zero-based positional index (idx:{i}), and formats the entire codebase layout into an alphabetically sorted, indented hierarchy. This enables language models to perceive repository topology, package nesting, and file locations while consuming a fraction of the token budget required by raw path enumerations. Complementing this, get_content_for_indices accepts targeted index selections produced by downstream planning nodes, extracts the corresponding file contents using defensive boundary checks, and returns a key-annotated mapping (f"{i} # {path}") ready for prompt injection.

flowchart TD subgraph DirectoryTreeFlow["Directory Tree Construction"] startTree["files_data: list of path, content tuples"] groupDirs["Group files into defaultdict by os.path.dirname"] tagBasename["Format basenames as basename with idx:i"] sortKeys["Sort directory keys lexicographically"] sortFiles["Sort files within each directory"] assembleTree["Join directory lines and indented file entries"] end subgraph ContentLookupFlow["Content Extraction by Index"] startIdx["indices: sequence of integer targets"] checkBounds{"0 <= index < len files_data?"} extractTuple["Unpack path and content from files_data index"] formatKey["Construct key as index # path"] storeMap["Assign content into content_map"] skipIndex["Skip out-of-bounds index"] returnMap["Return content_map"] end startTree --> groupDirs groupDirs --> tagBasename tagBasename --> sortKeys sortKeys --> sortFiles sortFiles --> assembleTree startIdx --> checkBounds checkBounds -->|"Yes"| extractTuple checkBounds -->|"No"| skipIndex extractTuple --> formatKey formatKey --> storeMap storeMap --> returnMap skipIndex --> returnMap classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class startTree,startIdx entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_directory_tree(files_data):

Description: Constructs a compact, human-readable directory tree string from an ordered sequence of file path and content tuples. For each entry, the directory path is isolated using os.path.dirname, defaulting to "." for root-level files, while the filename is isolated using os.path.basename. Each filename is formatted with its zero-based ordinal index suffix (idx:{i}). The parent directories and their respective file entries are sorted in lexicographical order. The resulting string lists each directory suffixed with a slash (/), followed by its indented constituent files.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Sequence of (path, content) tuples representing the codebase files and their contents.

Returns: * str: A multi-line string representing the hierarchical file tree with directory headings and two-space indented file entries.

Raises: * TypeError: If files_data is not iterable or contains elements that cannot be unpacked into a 2-tuple. * AttributeError: If a file path within files_data is not a valid string or path-like object compatible with os.path.dirname.

Example: 

def build_directory_tree(files_data):
    """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples.

    Groups files by directory and formats as a hierarchical tree with file indices.
    Used by ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions, MapAbstractions, and CombineTutorial
    to give LLMs structural context about the project layout.
    """
    dir_files = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
        basename = os.path.basename(path)
        dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

    lines = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
        lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
        lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
    return "\n".join(lines)

The function iterates over files_data with enumerate() to assign a stable, linear index to each file matching its position in the list. It builds a collections.defaultdict(list) where each unique directory path maps to a list of annotated basename strings. By applying sorted() across both the directory keys and the basename lists, the rendered output remains completely deterministic regardless of the order in which files were crawled. Each directory name is printed with a trailing / header, and member files are indented by two spaces (), minimizing total character count while preserving visual and semantic hierarchy for upstream LLM prompts.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):

Description: Selectively extracts the source code content for a specific subset of file indices from the master files_data collection. For each index in indices, it validates that the index lies within the valid array bounds [0, len(files_data) - 1]. For matching entries, it records the content in a returned dictionary keyed by a composite string combining the index and file path (f"{i} # {path}"). Any index that is negative or exceeds the maximum index of files_data is silently ignored.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Master sequence of (path, content) tuples representing the ingested repository. * indices (iterable[int]): Collection of integer indices identifying which files must be retrieved.

Returns: * dict[str, str]: A dictionary where each key is formatted as "{index} # {path}" and each value is the corresponding file content string.

Raises: * TypeError: If indices contains elements that cannot be compared with integer bounds, or if files_data elements cannot be unpacked.

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    """Get file content for specific indices from files_data list."""
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

This helper performs targeted, selective context extraction, avoiding the memory and token overhead of passing the entire codebase payload into downstream LLM calls. The bound-checking condition 0 <= i < len(files_data) provides fail-soft protection against invalid or hallucinated file indices produced by upstream LLM routing steps. Keying the resulting dictionary by f"{i} # {path}" embeds self-documenting contextual metadata into the prompt dictionary, enabling downstream models and parsers to correlate extracted code blocks directly with the structural tree previously rendered by build_directory_tree.

docs.title: Ingested Codebase Payload
docs.text:
The standard input structure passed to both functions in this module is a sequence of two-element tuples, typically assembled by repository crawling utilities such as crawl_local_files or crawl_github_files.

Element Index Field Name Type Description [0] path str Relative or normalized POSIX file path within the target repository. [1] content str Complete decoded text content of the source file.

docs.title: Directory Tree String Schema
docs.text:
The multi-line string generated by build_directory_tree adheres to a strict two-tier hierarchical layout.

Line Type Format Pattern Description Example Directory Header {dirname}/ Lexicographically sorted directory path, or . for files in the repository root. utils/ File Entry {basename} (idx:{i}) Two-space indented file name paired with its zero-based position in files_data. files.py (idx:7)

docs.title: Index Content Map
docs.text:
The dictionary returned by get_content_for_indices maps composite identifier keys to source code contents.

Field Type Description Example Key Key str Formatted string containing the file index and relative path separated by #. "7 # utils/files.py" Value str The complete text content of the referenced source file. "\"\"\"File and content helpers...\"\"\""

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive data normalization and boundary checks rather than raising custom domain exceptions:

  • Missing Parent Directory Normalization: In build_directory_tree, top-level files that have no parent directory return an empty string from os.path.dirname(path). The expression os.path.dirname(path) or "." normalizes empty directory strings to ".", preventing empty headers or root-path formatting errors.
  • Safe Index Slicing: In get_content_for_indices, the conditional check 0 <= i < len(files_data) protects against negative index lookups (which in standard Python negative slicing would wrap around and select files from the end of the array) and protects against IndexError exceptions caused by out-of-range indices.
  • Empty Input Handling: Passing an empty list ([]) as files_data safely produces an empty string ("") in build_directory_tree and an empty dictionary ({}) in get_content_for_indices without raising errors.

docs.title: i18n.py
docs.text: Source: utils/i18n.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/i18n.py module provides automated internationalization capabilities for UI diagnostic messages, pipeline logs, and user-facing notifications. It acts as an autonomous localization bridge that monitors strings.csv, detects missing localized string entries for target languages, synthesizes translated entries via language model calls, and writes the translated entries directly back to persistent disk storage.

Architecturally, this module was extracted from utils/output.py to decouple the UI notification system from the language model orchestration layer. In earlier iterations, a circular dependency chain existed: output.py depended on call_llm.py, which depended on token_utils.py, which in turn routed back to output.py for diagnostic event reporting. By isolating localization within i18n.py, the core output subsystem can delegate string translation to this module, making i18n.py the sole boundary component that imports call_llm from within the output toolchain.

The translation pipeline operates in four stages: translation deficiency scanning, token consumption pre-flight checks, batch language model translation via prompt templates, and non-destructive CSV persistence using UTF-8 with Byte Order Mark (BOM) encoding.

flowchart TD startCheck["Receive auto_translate request"] langCheck{"Target is English or file missing?"} returnFalseNoOp["Return False"] readCsv["Scan strings.csv for unpopulated keys"] missingCheck{"Missing translations found?"} returnFalseNoMissing["Return False"] prepPrompt["Format translate_strings.md prompt"] estTokens["Estimate token budget via log_token_estimation"] callLlm["Execute call_llm step translate_strings"] parseRegex{"Valid JSON object matched?"} writeCsv["Invoke _write_translations_to_csv"] emitSuccess["Emit SUCCESS status"] returnTrue["Return True"] emitWarning["Emit WARNING status"] returnFalseFail["Return False"] startCheck --> langCheck langCheck -- "Yes" --> returnFalseNoOp langCheck -- "No" --> readCsv readCsv --> missingCheck missingCheck -- "No" --> returnFalseNoMissing missingCheck -- "Yes" --> prepPrompt prepPrompt --> estTokens estTokens --> callLlm callLlm --> parseRegex parseRegex -- "Yes" --> writeCsv writeCsv --> emitSuccess emitSuccess --> returnTrue parseRegex -- "No or Exception" --> emitWarning emitWarning --> returnFalseFail classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class startCheck entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def auto_translate(lang_col, language, csv_path, use_cache, thinking_level):

Description: Inspects the localization CSV table for missing translation keys for a designated target language, compiles an in-memory dictionary of required translations, invokes the configured language model using a dedicated prompt template, parses the structured JSON response, and persists the generated translations to the CSV file. If the designated language column does not yet exist in the CSV, the function dynamically creates the column header.

Parameters: * lang_col (str): Lowercase column identifier representing the target language in strings.csv (e.g., "vietnamese", "spanish"). * language (str): Capitalized display name of the target language passed to the prompt template (e.g., "Vietnamese"). * csv_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to the target strings.csv file. * use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether LLM caching should be utilized for the translation request. * thinking_level (str | None): Model reasoning/thinking budget parameter passed downstream to the provider routing layer.

Returns: * bool: Returns True if new translations were successfully generated and written to disk (notifying the caller to reload its in-memory string lookup table), or False if no translations were needed, the target language was English, the CSV file was missing, or the translation pipeline failed.

Raises: * The function does not propagate exceptions externally. Internal failures (e.g., missing prompt files, network dropouts, malformed model JSON outputs, or file permission issues) are trapped internally, logged as warning events via emit_raw, and fail gracefully by returning False.

docs.title: Phase 1: Input Validation and Translation Deficiency Scan
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit_raw

    if lang_col == "english":
        return False

    if not csv_path or not os.path.exists(csv_path):
        return False

    # Collect strings that have no translation in the target language column
    missing = {}
    is_new_column = False
    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        is_new_column = lang_col not in fieldnames
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue
            # Check if the language column exists and has a value
            lang_text = row.get(lang_col, "").strip() if lang_col in fieldnames else ""
            if lang_text:
                continue  # Already translated

            english_text = row.get("english", "").strip()
            if english_text:
                missing[key] = english_text

    if not missing:
        return False

Phase 1 establishes entry guards and scans the localization storage file. If the requested target column is "english", the operation immediately returns False since English serves as the canonical source language. It verifies that csv_path exists on disk before reading with utf-8-sig decoding to transparently strip any initial UTF-8 BOM markers. Iterating through rows via csv.DictReader, it filters out blank keys and comment rows prefixed with #. It records an entry in the missing dictionary only when a valid STRING_KEY has an associated non-empty english entry and lacks a non-empty string under lang_col. If no entries require translation, execution halts early to prevent redundant downstream network calls.

docs.title: Phase 2: Prompt Templating and Token Estimation
docs.text:
# Report what we found
    if is_new_column:
        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] New language '{language}' — adding column to strings.csv")
    emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] {len(missing)} strings need translation to {language}")

    # Batch translate via LLM
    try:
        from utils.call_llm import call_llm

        entries_json = json.dumps(missing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # Load prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md
        prompt_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "prompts",
            "common",
            "translate_strings.md",
        )
        with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8") as pf:
            prompt_template = pf.read()
        prompt = prompt_template.format(language=language, entries=entries_json)

        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] Calling LLM to translate {len(missing)} strings...")
        from utils.token_utils import log_token_estimation, resolve_max_tokens

        try:
            context_tokens = resolve_max_tokens({})
        except Exception:
            context_tokens = 0
        log_token_estimation("TranslateStrings", prompt, context_tokens)

Phase 2 prepares the prompt payload and logs pre-flight execution telemetry. It emits informational messages indicating whether a new column is being introduced and reporting the volume of strings to be translated. The missing string dictionary is serialized to a JSON formatted string with unicode preservation (ensure_ascii=False). The system resolves the absolute path to prompts/common/translate_strings.md, loads the template file, and substitutes the target language and string payload. Before dispatching the network call, it imports helper functions from utils.token_utils to estimate token consumption and log the telemetry under the "TranslateStrings" operation label, catching and defaulting token resolution errors to zero.

docs.title: Phase 3: LLM Dispatch and JSON Response Extraction
docs.text:
response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=use_cache, thinking_level=thinking_level, step="translate_strings")

        # Extract JSON from response
        json_match = re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)
        if json_match:
            translations = json.loads(json_match.group())
            translated_count = len(translations)

            # Write translations back into strings.csv
            _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations)
            emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] Translated {translated_count}/{len(missing)} strings — saved to strings.csv")
            return True
        emit_raw("WARNING", "[i18n] LLM response did not contain valid JSON — falling back to English")

    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")

    return False

Phase 3 executes the translation request and processes the raw response. It delegates the prompt to call_llm, tagging the pipeline stage with step="translate_strings". Because language models may wrap responses in conversational markdown or chain-of-thought artifacts, the routine executes a regex search (\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}) across line breaks using re.DOTALL to extract the root JSON object. Upon matching, json.loads parses the translated key-value dictionary, which is passed to _write_translations_to_csv. If the JSON regex does not find a match or if an exception occurs during the LLM call or disk write, the module emits a warning and gracefully defaults to returning False.

Example: 

# Actual invocation pattern as implemented in utils/i18n.py
updated = auto_translate(
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    language="Vietnamese",
    csv_path="/workspace/utils/strings.csv",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level="low",
)
if updated:
    # Caller reloads strings from disk
    pass

docs.title: _write_translations_to_csv()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):

Description: Reads existing rows from strings.csv, merges new translation key-value mappings into their corresponding records, dynamically registers new language headers if the target column is missing, and writes the entire updated dataset back to disk using UTF-8 BOM encoding.

Parameters: * csv_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to strings.csv. * lang_col (str): Name of the language column to populate. * fieldnames (list[str]): List of existing CSV column headers passed from the scanner. * translations (dict[str, str]): Dictionary mapping string key identifiers to their translated text.

Returns: * None: Mutates the target CSV file in place on the filesystem.

Raises: * OSError: Propagated if disk access fails during the read or write phases.

def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):
    """Write LLM translations back into strings.csv, persisting them for future runs.

    If the target language column doesn't exist, it is added to the CSV.
    """
    rows = []

    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        # Add language column if it doesn't exist
        if lang_col not in fieldnames:
            fieldnames.append(lang_col)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if key in translations:
                row[lang_col] = translations[key]
            rows.append(row)

    # Write with BOM so Excel opens as UTF-8 without extra import steps
    with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

The function reads the CSV file in its entirety to ensure row preservation. When reading reader.fieldnames, it defensively re-checks if lang_col exists; if not, it appends the new column identifier to the header array. It iterates through the dataset rows, checks whether the record's STRING_KEY is present in the translations dictionary, and assigns the localized string to row[lang_col]. Finally, it opens the target file in write mode using encoding="utf-8-sig" and newline="", invoking DictWriter.writeheader() and DictWriter.writerows(). Using the UTF-8 signature ensures international characters render correctly in standard text editors and spreadsheet applications without requiring manual UTF-8 import wizards.

Example: 

# Internal usage within auto_translate
_write_translations_to_csv(
    csv_path=csv_path,
    lang_col=lang_col,
    fieldnames=fieldnames,
    translations=translations,
)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements a fail-soft strategy designed to keep UI logging and CLI operations functioning even when external translation services encounter problems:

  • Source File Non-Existence: If csv_path is empty or does not exist on disk, auto_translate avoids raising an IOError or FileNotFoundError, immediately returning False.
  • English Short-Circuit: If the caller requests translations for the "english" column, the module immediately exits with False to prevent overwriting canonical source strings.
  • Token Estimation Failures: Exceptions arising during resolve_max_tokens are caught locally in a nested try...except block, defaulting context_tokens to 0 so translation can continue.
  • LLM Output Formatting Anomalies: If the language model fails to return a parseable JSON structure, re.search fails to find a match, prompting auto_translate to emit a WARNING via emit_raw and exit gracefully with False.
  • Transport and Filesystem Exceptions: Broad exceptions occurring during prompt loading, network operations via call_llm, or CSV disk writes are intercepted by except Exception as e. The error is reported as a non-fatal warning using emit_raw("WARNING", ...), allowing callers to fall back to English UI strings without crashing the pipeline.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/llm_anthropic.py module implements the dedicated Anthropic Claude client adapter for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. While utils/call_llm.py acts as a vendor-agnostic dispatch facade, this module encapsulates all Anthropic-specific protocols, configuration quirks, context budgeting algorithms, and response processing. By isolating SDK dependencies and Claude-specific execution mechanics here, the broader codebase avoids direct coupling to the anthropic Python library, allowing runtime environments targeting alternative providers to omit the Anthropic SDK entirely.

The adapter is engineered around the operational requirements of the Claude model family (primarily Claude 5 and 4.6+, alongside legacy support for Haiku 4.5). It natively configures adaptive thinking budgets, enforces strict token context limits using calibrated ratios, handles ephemeral prompt caching, and negotiates server-side refusal fallbacks via experimental Anthropic beta headers. Because long-running model generations and deep reasoning traces can trigger HTTP gateway timeouts, the module executes all chat completions using streamed HTTP transport via client.messages.stream, extracting the synthesized message aggregate only after transmission concludes.

Furthermore, the module integrates directly with the pipeline's telemetry and caching contracts. It tracks multi-tier token usage across input tokens, output tokens, thinking budgets, and ephemeral cache read/write tiers, recording operational costs into the shared ledger. When requests encounter context exhaustion or safety refusals, it enforces specialized fail-soft protocols: output truncation triggers a one-time dynamic retry with expanded ceilings before yielding a TruncatedResponse, while classifier declinations are mapped directly to LLMRefusalError exceptions to prevent upstream caching.

docs.title: uses_adaptive_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def uses_adaptive_thinking(model: str) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a given model identifier belongs to the model families that natively support adaptive thinking and variable effort levels rather than legacy fixed token budgets.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string to evaluate.

Returns: * bool: True if the model matches prefixes defined in _ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES, False otherwise.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
    if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
        thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
        if is_debug():
            thinking["display"] = "summarized"
        params["thinking"] = thinking

Under the hood, this function performs prefix matching against ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES. Models matching these prefixes use Anthropic's output configuration schema rather than legacy token budget allocations.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the maximum context window capacity and maximum generation limit for a specified model. It queries the Anthropic Models API via the SDK client, caches the result in an in-memory dictionary, and falls back to hardcoded defaults if network or API errors occur.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier string.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple of (context_window, max_output_tokens).

Raises: * Catches anthropic.APIError internally and falls back to static limits.

Example: 

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (context_window, max_output_tokens) from the Models API, with offline fallback."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    fallback = next((v for k, v in _MODEL_LIMITS.items() if model.startswith(k)), _DEFAULT_LIMITS)
    try:
        info = _get_client().models.retrieve(model)
        limits = (getattr(info, "max_input_tokens", None) or fallback[0], getattr(info, "max_tokens", None) or fallback[1])
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Anthropic Models API | model={model} | context={limits[0]:,} | max_output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
    except anthropic.APIError as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e))
        limits = fallback
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits

The function checks _model_limits_cache to eliminate redundant remote calls over the process lifetime. If the remote API endpoint is unreachable or returns an error, the function captures anthropic.APIError, emits a diagnostic warning via emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP", ...), and falls back to hardcoded prefix matches in _MODEL_LIMITS or the global default _DEFAULT_LIMITS (1_000_000, 128_000).

docs.title: normalize_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Normalizes an abstract reasoning effort string (such as "low", "medium", or "high") into a parameter value accepted by the target Claude model, emitting a diagnostic warning if the provided effort level cannot be mapped.

Parameters: * model (str): The target model identifier. * level (str | None): The requested effort level, or None.

Returns: * str | None: The normalized effort string accepted by the Anthropic SDK, or None if unconfigured or unsupported.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Map a thinking level to an effort value the model accepts (None = model default)."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, level)  # minimal → low; xhigh → high on the 4.6 family
    if level and effort is None:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID", level=level.lower(), model=model, supported=str(list(EFFORT_LEVELS)))
    return effort

This method delegates to llm_config.anthropic_effort() to map conceptual tiers (e.g., mapping "minimal" to "low", or capping "xhigh" to "high" on Claude 4.6 family models). If an explicit non-empty level was supplied but failed validation, it logs a warning event containing the valid options before returning None.

docs.title: call_anthropic()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_anthropic(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary public interface for executing completions against the Anthropic API. It resolves model parameters, checks token margins, streams the generation, records telemetry, and validates stop criteria. The function operates across three distinct logical phases: Request Configuration and Sizing, Stream Execution and Truncation Retry, and Usage Accounting and Result Extraction.

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Configuration and Sizing
docs.text:
model = get_model()
    effort = normalize_effort(model, thinking_level)
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
    max_tokens, ceiling = _resolve_max_tokens(int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()), model, effort)
    params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, max_tokens)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Anthropic request | model={model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | max_tokens={max_tokens:,} | "
        f"fallbacks={'on' if betas else 'off'} | prompt_cache={'on' if 'cache_control' in params else 'off'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

In this initial phase, the function determines the active model and normalized thinking effort. It estimates the prompt's raw token count via count_tokens_raw(prompt) and scales it using token_ratio() (calibrated against real Claude tokenizers). It then calls _resolve_max_tokens to calculate an output budget and hard ceiling, ensuring that the combined prompt, margin, and output fit inside the model context window. Finally, it constructs the Anthropic API parameter dictionary and beta header list.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Truncation Retry
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    message = _send(params, betas)

    if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling:
        # Thinking + reply outgrew the budget: retry once at the largest budget that fits.
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}", cap=f"{ceiling:,}")
        _record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model, observe=False)  # same prompt: observe once
        params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, ceiling)
        start = time.time()
        message = _send(params, betas)

The second phase executes the streamed request via _send(). If the generation cuts off with a stop_reason of "max_tokens" and the initial budget was smaller than the allowable ceiling (max_tokens < ceiling), the function triggers an automated retry. It logs a warning, records usage for the partial first attempt without contaminating token calibration (observe=False), rebuilds the request parameters allocated to the absolute ceiling limit, and executes the stream a second time.

docs.title: Phase 3: Usage Accounting and Result Extraction
docs.text:
_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model)
    if is_debug():
        _log_thinking(message)

    if _served_by_fallback(message) and message.stop_reason != "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "fallbacks")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED", model=model, served_by=getattr(message, "model", "unknown"))

    if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
        details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
        category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

    text = _extract_text(message)
    if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(text)
    if not text:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Anthropic response contained no text blocks (stop_reason={message.stop_reason})", dest="LOG")
    return text

In the final phase, the function registers the completed request metrics with the ledger via _record_usage. If debug logging is active, any reasoning blocks in the response are extracted and logged to disk. If the request was fulfilled by a fallback model, telemetry counters are updated. If the generation terminated due to safety classifier refusal, an LLMRefusalError is raised. Finally, it aggregates all text blocks; if the response remained truncated despite retries, it wraps the output in a TruncatedResponse to prevent persistent disk caching.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt sent to Claude. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The synthesized output text, or a TruncatedResponse instance if generation was cut short by context limits.

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: Raised when the Anthropic API refuses the prompt due to safety classifier policies (stop_reason == "refusal").

Example: 

# Real usage from call_llm.py delegating to call_anthropic
from utils.llm_anthropic import call_anthropic

response = call_anthropic("Identify architectural abstractions in this codebase.", thinking_level="high")

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily instantiates and returns the module-level Anthropic client singleton (_client), configuring internal retry handling for transient HTTP errors.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * anthropic.Anthropic: The configured Anthropic SDK client instance.

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly.

Example: 

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        # SDK resolves credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / AUTH_TOKEN / ant profile) and
        # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL itself. SDK retries 408/409/429/5xx with backoff;
        # PocketFlow node retries sit on top of this.
        _client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=3)
    return _client

The helper relies on standard Anthropic SDK resolution order to locate authentication credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or local ant auth login tokens). It configures max_retries=3 for transient gateway errors (HTTP 408, 409, 429, and 5xx), establishing a defensive baseline beneath upstream node retry logic.

docs.title: _matches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a given model string begins with any prefix in a provided collection of strings.

Parameters: * model (str): The model name string. * prefixes (Iterable[str]): A sequence of prefix strings to compare against.

Returns: * bool: True if model starts with any of the prefixes; otherwise False.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:
    return any(model.startswith(p) for p in prefixes)

This helper standardizes prefix matching across the module. It powers model capability detection, determining whether a model supports adaptive thinking, defaults to active reasoning, or supports server-side refusal fallbacks.

docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Determines the appropriate Anthropic beta headers and extra_body payload required to activate server-side fallback routing based on environment settings and model eligibility.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier.

Returns: * tuple[list[str], dict]: A tuple of (betas, extra_body). If fallbacks are disabled or inapplicable, returns ([], {}).

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}

This function inspects ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS. When set to "default", it checks whether the model matches _FALLBACK_PREFIXES (e.g., Opus 5.x, Fable 5.x) and assigns _FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA. If explicit target models are provided as a comma-delimited string, it maps them into a list structure using _FALLBACK_LIST_BETA. If fallbacks are disabled via runtime flags or set to "off", it returns empty structures.

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Assembles the complete parameter payload dictionary and required beta header list for an Anthropic API call, configuring thinking profiles, ephemeral prompt caching, and fallback structures.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The input prompt string. * model (str): The target model identifier. * effort (str | None): The normalized thinking effort setting. * max_tokens (int): The maximum output token allocation.

Returns: * tuple[dict, list[str]]: A tuple containing the params dictionary and the list of betas headers.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas

The function handles variations in thinking across model generations. For models supporting adaptive thinking, it injects {"type": "adaptive"} along with output_config.effort. For legacy models, it calculates fixed budget_tokens from _BUDGET_BY_LEVEL. Additionally, it checks ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE to inject ephemeral cache control breakpoints and merges any fallback settings generated by _fallback_config().

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Calculates the requested output token budget alongside the maximum allowable ceiling that fits safely within the model's physical context window.

Parameters: * prompt_tokens (int): Calibrated prompt token count. * model (str): Target model identifier. * effort (str | None): Normalized thinking effort level.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A tuple of (wanted, ceiling). wanted is the planned token budget; ceiling is the upper limit allowed by context margins and configured caps.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling

The function computes the available context margin using ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN to ensure input prompts do not crowd out output headroom. If ceiling restricts the planned budget by more than 10% (ceiling < wanted * 0.9), it emits a diagnostic warning (WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED) before clamping wanted to ceiling.

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Dispatches a streaming request through the Anthropic client and blocks until the stream completes, returning the aggregated final message object.

Parameters: * params (dict): Keyword parameters for the Messages API. * betas (list[str]): List of beta feature headers.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The fully assembled final response message object.

Raises: * anthropic.APIError: If the API request fails during transmission.

Example: 

def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()

By consuming responses through stream.get_final_message(), this function eliminates the risk of HTTP read timeouts on large reasoning models generating long thinking chains (which can exceed 64K to 128K tokens). If betas are active, it routes execution through the client.beta.messages.stream interface.

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Inspects HTTP 400 Bad Request error messages to determine whether the rejection was caused by unsupported server-side fallback headers rather than invalid user parameters.

Parameters: * error_text (str): The error message string returned by the Anthropic SDK. * params (dict): The request parameter dictionary that triggered the failure.

Returns: * bool: True if the error reflects rejected beta fallback headers; False otherwise.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text

This verification helper inspects error payloads for occurrences of "anthropic-beta" and "server-side-fallback", or notifications indicating that "fallbacks": "default" is unsupported on the invoking account. This distinction allows the client to fall back gracefully instead of crashing on beta header rejections.

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Wraps message streaming with automatic fallback error recovery. If the API rejects fallback headers, it disables fallbacks globally for the rest of the run and immediately retries the request without them.

Parameters: * params (dict): Request parameters. * betas (list[str]): Beta feature header strings.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The completed response message.

Raises: * anthropic.BadRequestError: Re-raised if the 400 error is unrelated to fallback headers. * anthropic.APIError: On general API failures.

Example: 

def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise

When an anthropic.BadRequestError is intercepted, _send invokes _fallback_rejected(). If verified, it sets the global flag _fallbacks_disabled = True, logs a warning (WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED), strips extra_body from the request parameters, clears the betas list, and dispatches an unadorned retry.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated USD cost of an API call using token counts and the pricing rates configured in _PRICING.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier. * tokens_in (int): Count of non-cached input tokens. * tokens_out (int): Count of generated output tokens. * cache_read (int): Count of prompt tokens read from cache. * cache_write (int): Count of prompt tokens written to cache.

Returns: * float | None: Total cost in USD, or None if the model does not match any prefix in _PRICING.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000

The matching algorithm sorts the keys of _PRICING by string length descending to ensure specific model versions (e.g., "claude-opus-5-5") match before broader base prefixes (e.g., "claude-opus-5"). Cache creation is billed at 1.25× the base input token rate, conforming to Anthropic's pricing structure for 5-minute ephemeral cache writes.

docs.title: _tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:

Description: Extracts standard input, output, cache-read, and cache-write token counts from an Anthropic SDK usage object, normalizing None values to 0.

Parameters: * usage: An Anthropic API usage structure or dictionary.

Returns: * tuple[int, int, int, int]: A 4-tuple of (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens).

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return (
        getattr(usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
    )

This helper insulates the adapter against schema variations in usage objects across standard responses, streamed final messages, and nested iteration entries.

docs.title: _thinking_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:

Description: Extracts the count of reasoning tokens generated during adaptive or budgeted thinking from the usage details block.

Parameters: * usage: The Anthropic usage data object.

Returns: * int: Total thinking tokens generated, or 0 if not present.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:
    details = getattr(usage, "output_tokens_details", None)
    return getattr(details, "thinking_tokens", 0) or 0

The function inspects the nested output_tokens_details attribute on the usage payload. This separates reasoning tokens from the visible output tokens returned to the user.

docs.title: _declined_before_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether an API request was declined by safety classifiers prior to generating any billable output tokens.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message response object.

Returns: * bool: True if stop_reason is "refusal" and output token usage is zero; otherwise False.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:
    """A refusal with no output tokens at all is not billed (the same rule as for fallback iterations)."""
    return getattr(message, "stop_reason", None) == "refusal" and not (getattr(message.usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0)

Anthropic billing rules do not bill requests rejected by safety classifiers before token generation begins. This function identifies those unbilled refusals to keep financial accounting accurate.

docs.title: _billed_entries()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _billed_entries(message) -> list:

Description: Identifies and returns all billable usage entries associated with a message response, accounting for server-side fallback attempts and unbilled early refusals.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message object.

Returns: * list: A list of billable usage objects.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _billed_entries(message) -> list:
    """Usage entries of the billed attempts: every usage.iterations entry with output (server-side
    fallbacks), else the top-level usage unless the request was declined before any output."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        return [entry for entry in iterations if (getattr(entry, "output_tokens", 0) or 0) > 0]
    return [] if _declined_before_output(message) else [message.usage]

When server-side fallbacks occur, Anthropic returns per-attempt records in message.usage.iterations. This helper filters out attempts that produced zero output tokens (such as early refusals on the primary model) while retaining billable attempts. If iterations are absent, it returns the top-level usage object unless the request was declined before output.

docs.title: _billed_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:

Description: Computes the aggregated token totals across all billable attempts associated with a response.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message object.

Returns: * tuple[int, int, int, int, int]: A 5-tuple containing (total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking).

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    """(total input incl. cache read/write, output, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) summed over the
    billed attempts (_billed_entries), so token totals match _message_cost."""
    total_in = out = cache_read = cache_write = thinking = 0
    for entry in _billed_entries(message):
        tokens_in, tokens_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        total_in += tokens_in + read + write
        out += tokens_out
        cache_read += read
        cache_write += write
        thinking += _thinking_tokens(entry)
    return total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking

By summing tokens strictly across _billed_entries(message), this function ensures token counts match financial charges calculated by _message_cost. Non-cached input tokens, cache reads, and cache writes are combined to report the total input token footprint.

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the overall USD cost of a response. When server-side fallbacks occur, it prices each attempt using its respective model rates.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message object. * served_model (str): The default model identifier that served the final message.

Returns: * float | None: Total cost in USD, or None if pricing data is missing for any involved model.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if _declined_before_output(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))

This helper handles composite billing when server-side fallbacks switch models during a request. It iterates over message.usage.iterations, checks the model assigned to each attempt, skips unbilled early declinations, and accumulates charges using per-model rates.

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Records token metrics, thinking allocations, and estimated costs into the central pipeline ledger, while updating prompt token calibration ratios.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic response Message object. * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Pre-call prompt token count estimated via tiktoken. * effort (str | None): The normalized thinking effort level. * elapsed (float): Request duration in seconds. * model (str, optional): Configured model identifier. Defaults to "". * observe (bool, optional): Whether to feed observed token ratios into runtime calibration. Defaults to True.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    has_iterations = bool(getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None))
    entries = _billed_entries(message)
    if not entries:
        record_usage("ANTHROPIC", served_model, cost=0.0, measured=False)  # declined before any output: not billed
    for entry in entries:
        t_in, t_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        entry_model = (getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model) if has_iterations else served_model
        record_usage(
            "ANTHROPIC",
            entry_model,
            input_tokens=t_in + read + write,
            output_tokens=t_out,
            thinking_tokens=_thinking_tokens(entry),
            cache_read=read,
            cache_write=write,
            cost=_price(entry_model, t_in, t_out, read, write) if has_iterations else _message_cost(message, served_model),
        )
    total_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking = _billed_tokens(message)
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)
    # ... calculates ratio, calls observe_prompt_tokens and emit_raw ...

The function writes individual ledger records for each billable attempt via utils.llm_common.record_usage(). When observe=True and the request was served directly rather than by a fallback model, it passes the observed input token ratio to observe_prompt_tokens(), dynamically refining tiktoken-to-Claude token conversion multipliers for future requests.

docs.title: _log_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _log_thinking(message) -> None:

Description: Extracts reasoning text from thinking content blocks and logs them to the diagnostics log file when debug logging is active.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message object.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _log_thinking(message) -> None:
    for block in message.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "thinking" and getattr(block, "thinking", ""):
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{block.thinking}", dest="LOG")

The helper iterates through message.content, isolates blocks where type == "thinking", and outputs the raw thought process using emit_raw(). Writing directly to dest="LOG" keeps thinking traces in the debug log file without cluttering standard console output.

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the returned message was generated by a fallback model rather than the primary requested model.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message object.

Returns: * bool: True if fallback blocks or iteration records are detected; otherwise False.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)

The function checks both the message content array for fallback blocks and the usage.iterations log for entries with type == "fallback_message". This allows the adapter to identify server-side model substitutions and emit appropriate diagnostic events.

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _extract_text(message) -> str:

Description: Extracts and concatenates text from all standard text blocks within the message content array.

Parameters: * message: The Anthropic Message object.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text content.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")

This helper ignores non-text blocks (such as thinking summaries, fallback notices, or tool call structures), returning a clean string representing the model's actual response.

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: The module defines and manipulates several internal data structures and configuration schemas.

docs.title: Pricing Rates Schema (_PRICING)
docs.text:
Represents token pricing rates across supported Anthropic models. Keys are matched against the beginning of model name strings using longest-prefix matching.

Field Index Tuple Type Name Description 0 float input_cost_per_m Cost in USD per 1,000,000 standard input tokens. 1 float output_cost_per_m Cost in USD per 1,000,000 generated output tokens. 2 float cache_read_per_m Cost in USD per 1,000,000 tokens read from ephemeral cache.

Note: Ephemeral cache creation (writes) is dynamically computed as input_cost_per_m * 1.25.

Example mapping entry: 

"claude-sonnet-5": (2.00, 10.00, 0.20)

docs.title: Model Limits Tuple
docs.text:
Returned by get_model_limits() and cached within _model_limits_cache.

Element Type Description context_window int Total physical context capacity (input + output headroom) in tokens. max_output int Maximum generation token cap supported by the model architecture.

Example structure: 

(1_000_000, 128_000)

docs.title: Anthropic Request Parameters (params)
docs.text:
The dictionary constructed by _build_request() and dispatched to messages.stream.

Key Type Description "model" str Model identifier string (e.g., "claude-sonnet-5"). "max_tokens" int Allocated output ceiling for this request attempt. "messages" list[dict] Payload containing user input: [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. "thinking" dict (optional) Thinking config ({"type": "adaptive"} or {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": int}). "output_config" dict (optional) Adaptive effort setting: {"effort": effort}. "cache_control" dict (optional) Set to {"type": "ephemeral"} when prompt caching is enabled. "extra_body" dict (optional) Fallback specifications passed via beta headers.

docs.title: Billed Tokens Breakdown
docs.text:
The 5-tuple returned by _billed_tokens() summarizing token consumption across all billable attempts.

Index Field Type Description 0 total_in int Total input volume including regular input, cache reads, and cache writes. 1 out int Total generated output tokens. 2 cache_read int Subset of input tokens served from prompt cache. 3 cache_write int Subset of input tokens written to prompt cache. 4 thinking int Output tokens used for internal model reasoning.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive strategies to manage network errors, feature incompatibilities, safety refusals, and context exhaustion:

  • API Model Lookup Failures: In get_model_limits(), if _get_client().models.retrieve() fails due to an anthropic.APIError, the error is caught, logged via WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP, and safely resolved using _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS (1_000_000, 128_000).
  • Beta Feature Rejection: If an account or model rejects fallback headers (server-side-fallback-*), the API responds with an HTTP 400 BadRequestError. The _send() helper catches this, invokes _fallback_rejected(), disables the feature globally for the run (_fallbacks_disabled = True), emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED, and retries without fallback headers.
  • Safety Classifier Refusals: If Claude's safety filters decline a prompt (message.stop_reason == "refusal"), the adapter logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL, updates refusal event counters via count_event(), and raises an LLMRefusalError. This prevents call_llm.py from caching the refusal and allows calling pipelines to handle the failure cleanly.
  • Context Window Truncation and Retry: When generation is cut off with a stop reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS ("max_tokens" or "model_context_window_exceeded"), call_anthropic() checks if the initial budget was smaller than the available context ceiling. If headroom exists, it logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY and retries once using the full ceiling. If the response is still truncated, it wraps the output in a TruncatedResponse object, signaling upstream callers to avoid caching incomplete text.

docs.text:

  • utils/llm_config.py — Supplies model family constants, prefix configurations, default model IDs, output caps, and thinking effort mapping logic.

docs.title: llm_common.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_common.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/llm_common.py module establishes a provider-neutral operational foundation and shared runtime substrate for all Large Language Model (LLM) client interactions across the codebase. It operates completely independently of vendor-specific software development kits (SDKs) such as Anthropic, Google GenAI, or OpenAI, isolating core coordination logic, accounting primitives, and operational state from third-party transport layers. By providing a decoupled core, it standardizes error semantics, truncation flagging, execution-step attribution, telemetry accumulation, and warning deduplication across disparate model backends.

The architecture of the module centers on three primary mechanisms: a refusal memoization cache, a context-aware usage ledger, and sentinel response typing. Refusal memoization deterministically intercepts repeat requests for prompts that models have rejected on policy grounds, preventing redundant network overhead and unnecessary billing. The usage ledger leverages thread-safe and asynchronous task-safe context variables (contextvars.ContextVar) to transparently attribute prompt tokens, completion tokens, reasoning tokens, cache read/write operations, and estimated USD costs to specific workflow nodes without requiring invasive parameter passing through intermediate layers. Sentinel wrapping through TruncatedResponse enables downstream consumers to detect context window exhaustion while maintaining backward compatibility with standard string APIs.
