docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized string subclass used to represent model outputs that were abruptly terminated prior to natural completion due to maximum token boundaries or context window ceilings. Because it inherits directly from str, instances can be passed transparently through text-processing filters, regex evaluators, and string formatting routines without runtime type mismatches. However, the presence of the class attribute truncated = True allows callers such as call_llm to detect incomplete outputs, suppress local persistent caching, and signal upstream orchestrators to initiate retries or resize token allocations.

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True

The TruncatedResponse class provides an in-band failure signaling mechanism that avoids the overhead and control-flow disruptions of exception unwinding. When an LLM provider indicates that output generation ceased because of a limit cutoff (such as stop_reason == "max_tokens"), the raw text payload is wrapped within this type. Downstream pipeline stages check getattr(response, "truncated", False) to determine whether the response is partial, ensuring that incomplete JSON or truncated YAML payloads do not corrupt persistent caches or trigger malformed parsing errors downstream.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse.truncated
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: truncated = True

Description: A class-level boolean constant set to True on all TruncatedResponse instances, providing a direct discriminator for truncated response detection.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):

Description: A specialized runtime exception indicating that a model provider declined to process or complete an inference request. The error encapsulates diagnostic metadata including the originating model name, refusal category, provider identifier, and a critical retryable boolean flag. This flag differentiates between deterministic prompt-level policy rejections (which must not be retried) and transient, sampling-dependent candidate generation blocks (which can be retried with fresh random seeds).

class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the provider (and any configured fallback) declines a request.

    retryable=False: the same request is declined again (Claude refusal, blocked prompt,
    prohibited content) — call_llm remembers it and does not re-send it on node retries.
    retryable=True: an output-side block that a new sample can pass (Gemini RECITATION / OTHER /
    SAFETY on the candidate, OpenRouter content_filter) — node retries re-sample normally.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")

The LLMRefusalError standardizes error reporting across diverse provider rejection formats, including Anthropic refusal blocks, Google Gemini safety/recitation candidate suppressions, and OpenRouter moderation content filters. By default, retryable is set to False, signaling to callers like call_llm that the prompt itself triggered the refusal and that repeated submissions will consume rate limits without succeeding. When set to True, the calling pipeline recognizes that the refusal occurred on the generated candidate tokens rather than the input prompt, permitting standard retry mechanisms to attempt a new generation pass.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):

Description: Initializes the exception instance with contextual operational metadata, constructing a descriptive diagnostic message passed to the underlying RuntimeError base class.

Parameters: * model (str): Identifier of the specific model that refused generation (e.g., "claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219", "gemini-2.5-pro"). * category (str | None): Provider-specific classification code or reason for the refusal (e.g., "prohibited_content", "RECITATION"), or None if unspecified. * provider (str): Model provider identifier, defaulting to "ANTHROPIC". * retryable (bool): Whether the failure is transient and candidate-dependent (True) or deterministic and prompt-dependent (False). Defaults to False.

Returns: * None: Constructor returns nothing.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a deterministic SHA-256 hexadecimal hash string uniquely identifying an inference request configuration. The input parameters are concatenated into a structured scope string followed by the raw prompt body before hashing.

Parameters: * provider (str): The target provider identifier (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER"). * model (str): The specific model name string. * thinking_level (str | None): Normalized reasoning or thinking effort level (e.g., "low", "high"), falling back to "default" if None. * prompt (str): The complete raw prompt text sent to the model.

Returns: * str: A 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal hash representing the request identity.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The hashing routine ensures that variations in case sensitivity for thinking_level do not lead to key divergence by converting the value to lowercase. A newline character separates the prefix metadata scope from the prompt text, preventing concatenation collisions between model names and prompt prefixes. This hash serves as the uniform primary key for tracking non-retryable refusal events in the memoization table.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Caches a deterministic refusal exception in the module-level refusal dictionary, indexed by the request's unique hash key.

Parameters: * key (str): The SHA-256 hexadecimal digest generated by request_key(). * error (LLMRefusalError): The refusal exception instance to store for subsequent short-circuiting.

Returns: * None: No return value.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error

This function records permanent declinations directly into the in-memory _refused registry. Once registered, any subsequent attempt by pipeline retry loops or concurrent workers to execute the exact same prompt against the same model and thinking configuration can be immediately short-circuited before reaching network sockets or incurring vendor rate-limit penalties.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Queries the refusal registry for a previously recorded declination matching the provided request key.

Parameters: * key (str): The SHA-256 hexadecimal digest generated by request_key().

Returns: * LLMRefusalError | None: The previously cached exception if one exists; otherwise None.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)

The lookup performs an $O(1)$ dictionary lookup against the module-level _refused map. If a match is found, the dispatching engine can re-raise the existing LLMRefusalError immediately without issuing external API calls. If the key has not been recorded, the function returns None, permitting normal request processing.

docs.title: usage_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def usage_step(step: str | None):

Description: A context manager that scopes LLM usage metrics to a specified logical pipeline step. It sets the execution context variable _current_step upon entering the context block and resets it to its previous token state upon exit.

Parameters: * step (str | None): Logical identifier of the execution phase or pipeline node (e.g., "IdentifyAbstractions", "DraftChapters"). If None or empty, defaults to "other".

Returns: * Generator context manager yielding control to the enclosing block.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised; context resetting is guaranteed via a try...finally construct.

Example: 

@contextlib.contextmanager
def usage_step(step: str | None):
    """Attribute every record_usage / count_event inside the block to `step`."""
    token = _current_step.set(step or "other")
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _current_step.reset(token)

By leveraging contextvars.ContextVar, usage_step provides concurrency-safe attribution across synchronous and asynchronous execution boundaries. When nested within multiple workflows or execution blocks, the context manager preserves stack state using context tokens. Any invocation of record_usage() or count_event() within the scope of the context automatically maps token and monetary consumption directly to the designated step.

docs.title: current_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def current_step() -> str:

Description: Retrieves the active pipeline step identifier currently bound to the execution context.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: The name of the currently active step, or "other" if no step context has been established.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def current_step() -> str:
    return _current_step.get()

The function reads directly from the module's _current_step context variable. It is primarily consumed internally by record_usage() and count_event() to determine which ledger entry in _steps should receive incremental telemetry updates.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def record_usage(provider: str, model: str, *, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0, thinking_tokens: int = 0, cache_read: int = 0, cache_write: int = 0, cost: float | None = None, measured: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Records metrics from a completed API invocation into the usage ledger. Updates are applied concurrently to both the provider-level bucket and the current step-level bucket.

Parameters: * provider (str): Vendor identifier for the API provider (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI"). * model (str): Name of the model invoked (e.g., "claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219"). * input_tokens (int): Total prompt tokens counted by the provider, including cached tokens. Defaults to 0. * output_tokens (int): Total completion tokens generated, including reasoning tokens. Defaults to 0. * thinking_tokens (int): Subset of output tokens dedicated to internal reasoning/thinking. Defaults to 0. * cache_read (int): Number of prompt tokens served from provider-side prompt caches. Defaults to 0. * cache_write (int): Number of prompt tokens written to provider-side prompt caches. Defaults to 0. * cost (float | None): Monetary cost in USD for the transaction. If None, the call is flagged as unpriced. Defaults to None. * measured (bool): Flag indicating whether the provider reported actual token counts (True) or if usage went unmeasured/unbilled (False). Defaults to True.

Returns: * None: No return value.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Accumulate one API request. `input_tokens` = total prompt tokens (cached included);
    `output_tokens` includes thinking. `cost` is USD; None = unknown price (counted as unpriced).
    measured=False: the provider reported no usage, or the request was an unbilled decline — it counts
    as a request but is left out of estimate-vs-billed comparisons (`unmeasured_calls`)."""
    for entry in (_usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry()), _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())):
        if model:
            entry["models"].add(model)
        entry["calls"] += 1
        if not measured:
            entry["unmeasured_calls"] += 1
        entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
        entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
        entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
        entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
        entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
        if cost is None:
            entry["unpriced_calls"] += 1
        else:
            entry["cost"] += cost

The method uses a single unified loop over both the provider entry in _usage and the current step entry in _steps, guaranteeing synchronized updates across both dimensions. If the cost argument is None, the unpriced_calls counter increments while the total cost remains unchanged, indicating that cost calculation must be treated as incomplete. Unmeasured or unbilled requests (such as early refusals where no billable tokens were reported) increment unmeasured_calls, which allows auditing routines to discount those requests during token estimation discrepancy checks.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments a named operational event counter across both the provider-level bucket and the currently active step bucket.

Parameters: * provider (str): Provider identifier (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI"). * event (str): Specific counter attribute key to increment; expected to be one of "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations".

Returns: * None: No return value.

Raises: * KeyError: If event does not match an existing key initialized in _new_entry().

Example: 

def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider (and the current step)."""
    _usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry())[event] += 1
    _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())[event] += 1

This helper centralizes tracking for anomalous or non-standard execution paths. When an adapter catches a server-side fallback, records a refusal, or encounters an output truncation, it dispatches count_event to update diagnostic counters without altering token or pricing fields.

docs.title: record_estimate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:

Description: Records pre-flight token estimations and local cache hits for a specific pipeline step.

Parameters: * step (str): Logical step identifier. If empty or None, falls back to "other". * estimated_input (int): Number of input tokens estimated prior to network dispatch (e.g., via tiktoken). * cache_hit (bool): Whether the request was served directly from the persistent local cache (True) or dispatched to an API provider (False). Defaults to False.

Returns: * None: No return value.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:
    """Add call_llm's input estimate for a call (billed or served from the LLM cache) to a step."""
    entry = _steps.setdefault(step or "other", _new_entry())
    if cache_hit:
        entry["cache_hits"] += 1
    else:
        entry["estimated_input"] += estimated_input or 0

This function allows the pipeline to maintain accurate operational tracking even when network calls are avoided entirely due to cache hits. When cache_hit is True, the cache_hits counter increments, isolating cache performance per step. When cache_hit is False, the estimated input tokens accumulate under estimated_input, enabling telemetry summaries to compare predicted token budgets against final provider-measured tokens.

docs.title: usage_snapshot()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:

Description: Creates a point-in-time copy of a provider's running metrics dictionary, excluding non-numeric collection fields like "models".

Parameters: * provider (str): Provider identifier to snapshot.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing scalar copies of all tracking fields for the provider, or an initialized zero-state dictionary if the provider has not yet been registered.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:
    """Copy of a provider's running totals (diff two snapshots to get one call's usage)."""
    entry = _usage.get(provider)
    return {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "models"} if entry else {k: v for k, v in _new_entry().items() if k != "models"}

Snapshots isolate scalar accounting values before and after individual API requests. By excluding the mutable "models" set from the returned structure, the snapshot contains only numeric values that can be cleanly compared and subtracted across points in time.

docs.title: usage_delta()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:

Description: Computes the arithmetic difference between two usage snapshot dictionaries, producing the net usage incurred between the two snapshots.

Parameters: * before (dict): Baseline metric dictionary captured via usage_snapshot(). * after (dict): Later metric dictionary captured via usage_snapshot().

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing the arithmetic difference (after[key] - before[key]) for each key present in after.

Raises: * KeyError: If after contains keys missing from before without a fallback default (safeguarded internally via before.get(k, 0)).

Example: 

def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: after[k] - before.get(k, 0) for k in after}

The function computes delta metrics across individual API requests. Callers capture a baseline snapshot prior to dispatch, execute the LLM invocation, capture a terminal snapshot, and pass both into usage_delta(). This isolates the exact token consumption, cache activity, and monetary cost of a single call even when concurrent or background activity is present.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a comprehensive usage report covering all providers that completed at least one API call during the current execution.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping provider strings to serialized public usage records formatted by _public().

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: _public(entry) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}

The resulting dictionary excludes providers that were registered but made zero actual API calls. The internal records are converted using _public(), which transforms internal sets into sorted lists and appends boolean completeness flags, making the output suitable for JSON serialization and diagnostic logging.

docs.title: get_step_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_step_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles an ordered dictionary of usage metrics grouped by execution step for all steps that incurred either active API calls or cache hits.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping step name strings to their serialized public usage records formatted by _public().

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def get_step_summary() -> dict:
    """{step: totals} in first-use order, including steps answered only from the LLM cache."""
    return {step: _public(entry) for step, entry in _steps.items() if entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]}

Because Python 3.7+ preserves dictionary insertion order, get_step_summary() returns steps in their exact sequence of first encounter during pipeline execution. Steps that executed entirely out of local disk cache (where calls == 0 but cache_hits > 0) are retained in the summary, ensuring visibility into all active phases of the pipeline.

docs.title: reset_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def reset_usage() -> None:

Description: Flushes all internal runtime state, clearing the provider usage registry, the step breakdown registry, and the refusal memoization table.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None: No return value.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def reset_usage() -> None:
    _usage.clear()
    _steps.clear()
    _refused.clear()

This utility resets all tracking state between distinct testing sessions or multi-pass execution runs. Calling reset_usage() prevents metric leakage across pipeline boundaries and purges cached refusals, allowing subsequent executions to start from a clean state.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a warning signature has already been registered during the current process run. If the signature is new, it records it and returns True; otherwise, it returns False.

Parameters: * key (str): Primary category identifier or format template string for the warning. * *parts: Variable length positional arguments forming the unique context tuple (e.g., model name, error code).

Returns: * bool: True if this is the first time the specific (key, *parts) marker has been encountered; False if it was previously recorded.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

Example: 

def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True

The function deduplicates repetitive warning logs that can occur during tight loops or extensive batch operations. By verifying warnings against the internal _warned set, callers ensure that transient conditions (such as missing pricing tables or deprecated model headers) are logged only once per run, preventing terminal log spam.

docs.title: _new_entry()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _new_entry() -> dict:

Description: Factory function that creates a new usage ledger record initialized with zeroed counters and an empty model tracking set.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: An initialized usage metrics dictionary.

Raises: * No internal exceptions are raised.

def _new_entry() -> dict:
    return {
        "models": set(),
        "calls": 0,
        "input": 0,
        "output": 0,
        "thinking": 0,
        "cache_read": 0,
        "cache_write": 0,
        "cost": 0.0,
        "unpriced_calls": 0,
        "unmeasured_calls": 0,
        "refusals": 0,
        "fallbacks": 0,
        "truncations": 0,
        "estimated_input": 0,
        "cache_hits": 0,
    }

The dictionary returned by _new_entry() acts as the standard data container for tracking both provider-level and step-level operations. Initializing integer counters to 0, cost to 0.0, and models to an empty set ensures that accumulation operations can execute without defensive existence checks.

docs.title: _public()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:

Description: Prepares an internal usage ledger dictionary for external consumption by sorting set fields and calculating derivative status flags.

Parameters: * entry (dict): An internal usage record matching the structure generated by _new_entry().

Returns: * dict: A copy of entry with "models" converted to a sorted list and an additional "cost_known" boolean indicating whether all calls were priced.

Raises: * KeyError: If required fields ("models", "unpriced_calls") are missing from entry.

def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:
    return dict(entry, models=sorted(entry["models"]), cost_known=entry["unpriced_calls"] == 0)

The helper ensures internal mutable sets are converted into deterministic, JSON-serializable sorted lists. Additionally, it computes the boolean flag cost_known, which indicates whether all recorded calls had associated pricing data (unpriced_calls == 0). This allows consumers to quickly determine whether monetary totals are authoritative or incomplete.

docs.title: _refused
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Type: dict[str, LLMRefusalError]

_refused = {}

Module-level dictionary storing memoized refusal exceptions indexed by the SHA-256 digest generated by request_key(). It prevents duplicate requests for previously declined prompts from being dispatched over the network.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
An extension of the built-in str class that includes a boolean attribute indicating output truncation.

Attribute Type Description truncated bool Class-level constant, always True. Indicates that response text was cut off by token limits.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The module provides specialized mechanisms for handling two distinct categories of model failure: policy-driven declinations and token-limit truncations.

docs.title: Policy Refusals and Memoization
docs.text:
When an LLM provider explicitly rejects an inference prompt on safety, compliance, or moderation grounds, it signals that the request cannot be fulfilled under the requested parameters. The module manages this via LLMRefusalError, differentiating between two operational modes:

  1. Non-Retryable Declinations (retryable=False): Used when the refusal is triggered deterministically by the prompt content (such as Claude safety refusals or blocked input keywords). The error is cached in _refused via remember_refusal(), indexed by the SHA-256 digest from request_key(). When subsequent attempts or pipeline retry loops encounter the same prompt and parameters, previous_refusal() matches the cached entry and short-circuits execution immediately, preventing repeated rate-limit consumption and billed partial generations.
  2. Retryable Output Blocks (retryable=True): Used when the refusal is non-deterministic and triggered by the generated candidate content rather than the input prompt (such as Gemini recitation checks or dynamic safety blocks on output tokens). These errors are not stored in the memoization table, allowing downstream retry handlers to resubmit the prompt with different sampling parameters or random seeds.

docs.title: Context and Output Truncation
docs.text: When an API provider indicates that generation stopped due to context window or output token limits (e.g., stop_reason == "max_tokens"), raising an exception would disrupt operations where partial output may still be inspectable or repairable. Instead, the module returns a TruncatedResponse instance. This sentinel string allows downstream parsers to check for truncation flags, avoid caching incomplete responses in persistent disk caches, and handle retries or context expansion gracefully.

docs.title: llm_config.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_config.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the runtime ledger, refusal tracking, and truncated response abstractions established in utils/llm_common.py, utils/llm_config.py serves as the centralized configuration, credential preflight, and model parameter resolution engine for the codebase analysis pipeline. Originally extracted from call_llm.py to eliminate circular import dependencies with token_utils.py, this module acts as the authoritative single source of truth for runtime provider selection, model catalog limits, context window calculations, token estimation scaling, and thinking effort budgets.

The architecture isolates upstream pipeline orchestrators from vendor-specific configuration schemas across Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and generic OpenAI-compatible gateways. It models complex model-family behaviors: dynamic reasoning effort translation, token ratio compensation for tiktoken undercounting across various Claude and Gemini tokenizers, Vertex AI regional endpoint routing, and OpenRouter dynamic catalog introspection with transient failure circuit-breaking.

Additionally, the module implements fail-fast credential preflights for all supported providers prior to executing intensive repository crawls or planning nodes. For Anthropic, it performs multi-tier authentication resolution across environment API keys, auth tokens, Workload Identity Federation attributes, native ant auth CLI status scraping with credential masking, and cached filesystem OAuth tokens. For Gemini, it enforces minimum Google GenAI SDK version thresholds (>= 1.56.0) to avoid runtime Pydantic validation failures when handling structured thinking configurations, while intercepting deprecated preview identifiers.

docs.title: anthropic_output_cap()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:

Description: Resolves the user-configured ceiling for Anthropic token generations from the environment variable ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. The value is parsed as a positive integer; if unset, non-numeric, or non-positive, it returns None.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * int | None: The parsed positive token limit, or None if not specified.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Sizing prompt budget in token_utils.py or planned output
cap = anthropic_output_cap()
if cap:
    budget = min(budget, cap)


def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:
    """ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS as an int, or None when unset/invalid."""
    return _env_int("ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
The helper invokes _env_int against ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. It sanitizes input whitespace, ensures pure digit composition, and enforces strict positivity, shielding downstream budgeting formulas from syntax crashes.

docs.title: anthropic_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Calculates the target output token allocation for an Anthropic adaptive thinking model given an abstract reasoning level. It retrieves baseline requirements from ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT and bounds the result using anthropic_output_cap() if an environment override is configured.

Parameters: * thinking_level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort tier ("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "minimal", or None).

Returns: * int: Safe maximum token count to allocate for the request.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

planned = anthropic_output_budget("high")
# Output: 64000 (or capped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS)


def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-effort table value capped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (adaptive models)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget
The implementation lower-cases the input string to match normalized keys in ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT. If thinking_level is absent or unmapped, it defaults to the None key entry (64_000 tokens). Finally, anthropic_output_cap() restricts the value to prevent cost overruns when constrained by administrator environments.

docs.title: anthropic_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Normalizes an abstract reasoning tier into a valid Claude output_config.effort parameter compatible with the target model. It translates "minimal" to "low", validates membership within ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS, and downgrades "xhigh" to "high" on legacy Claude 4.6 architectures.

Parameters: * model (str): The target Claude model name. * level (str | None): The abstract reasoning level string.

Returns: * str | None: The vendor-compliant effort string, or None if thinking is disabled or unmapped.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

effort = anthropic_effort("claude-sonnet-4-6", "xhigh")
# Returns: "high"


def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Thinking level → effort the model accepts: minimal → low, xhigh → high on the 4.6 family,
    unknown values → None (model default)."""
    if not level:
        return None
    level = level.lower()
    if level == "minimal":
        level = "low"
    if level not in ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS:
        return None
    if level == "xhigh" and (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES):
        return "high"
    return level
This function protects API requests from runtime rejections caused by incompatible effort parameters. Models such as claude-opus-4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6 reject the xhigh tier introduced in newer versions with an HTTP 400 error. The helper maps incoming requests down to "high" while ignoring casing differences.

docs.title: anthropic_planned_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Determines the output token headroom that must be reserved for an Anthropic request before checking model and context boundaries. For adaptive models, it queries anthropic_output_budget(). For pre-adaptive models, it calculates ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL.get(effort, 0) + ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS, capping the outcome via anthropic_output_cap().

Parameters: * model (str): Claude model identifier. * thinking_level (str | None): Reasoning effort string.

Returns: * int: Total output token headroom planned for the generation.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Shared by llm_anthropic and token_utils.input_token_budget
output_reservation = anthropic_planned_output("claude-haiku-4-5", "medium")
# Output: 8192 + 16000 = 24192


def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, thinking_level)
    if (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
        return anthropic_output_budget(effort)
    planned = ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL.get(effort, 0) + ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(planned, cap) if cap else planned
The implementation evaluates whether the requested model matches ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES. For adaptive architectures, output allocations match the unified per-effort table. For older models, the explicit thinking budget is added to the minimum reply allowance (16_000 tokens) and bounded by any user-configured token cap.

docs.title: gemini_thinking_mode()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:

Description: Inspects a Gemini model name to resolve its thinking configuration protocol. It returns a tuple classifying the mechanism into categorical levels ("level"), numeric token budgets ("budget"), or unsupported ("none"), along with the relevant configuration bounds.

Parameters: * model (str): Gemini model string or resource name.

Returns: * tuple[str, object]: A tuple structured as either ("level", tuple_of_levels), ("budget", (min, max, can_disable)), or ("none", None).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode("gemini-3.8-flash")
# mode == "level", spec == ("low", "medium", "high")

mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode("gemini-2.5-pro")
# mode == "budget", spec == (128, 32768, False)


def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, low, high, can_disable in GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "budget", (low, high, can_disable)
    if not name.startswith("gemini-") or name.startswith(("gemini-1", "gemini-2")):
        return "none", None  # 1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants (image, live, TTS) and non-Gemini ids
    for prefix, levels in GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "level", levels
    return "level", GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS
The function normalizes the input using gemini_model_id() to strip path prefixes. It executes longest-prefix matching against GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES to isolate legacy 2.5 models requiring integer budgets. If the model is an older release (Gemini 1.x or 2.0) or an unmapped variant, it flags thinking as unsupported ("none"). For Gemini 3.x models, it matches specific levels from GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS or falls back to GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS.

docs.title: gemini_model_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:

Description: Strips Google API and Vertex AI resource path prefixes from fully qualified model identifiers (e.g., transforming "models/gemini-3.8-flash" or "publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash" into "gemini-3.8-flash").

Parameters: * model (str): Raw model identifier or Vertex resource path.

Returns: * str: Stripped, lower-case model name.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

name = gemini_model_id("publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash")
# Returns: "gemini-3.8-flash"


def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:
    """'models/gemini-3.8-flash' / 'publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash' → 'gemini-3.8-flash'."""
    return (model or "").strip().lower().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
The logic performs defensive string cleanup, lower-casing all characters and taking the last segment after any forward slashes (/). This ensures consistent catalog lookups regardless of whether the identifier originated from Google AI Studio, Vertex AI, or OpenRouter.

docs.title: gemini_vertex_locations()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:

Description: Identifies valid Vertex AI deployment locations that serve the given Gemini 3.x model.

Parameters: * model (str): Target Gemini model identifier.

Returns: * tuple | None: A tuple of valid region strings (e.g., ("global", "us")), or None if the model is served across all regional endpoints.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

locations = gemini_vertex_locations("gemini-3.8-flash-cyber")
# Returns: ("global", "us")


def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:
    """Vertex AI locations that serve a Gemini 3.x model (None = any, including regional endpoints)."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, locations in GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return locations
    return GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS if name.startswith("gemini-3") else None
The helper walks GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS using prefix checks. If no specific entry matches but the model belongs to the Gemini 3 family, it returns the standard multi-region tuple GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS ("global", "us", "eu"). For older architectures or unmapped models, it returns None.

docs.title: gemini_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:

Description: Computes the planned completion token allocation for Gemini models. It references GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT, bounds the value by the model's structural limit, and applies the GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment override if defined.

Parameters: * thinking_level (str | None): Desired reasoning effort. * output_limit (int | None): Maximum generation limit supported by the target model (defaults to GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1] = 65_536).

Returns: * int: Bounded output token budget.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

tokens = gemini_output_budget("low")
# Returns: 32768


def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    budget = min(budget, output_limit or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1])
    cap = _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget
The function normalizes the thinking tier and resolves the base output allocation. It ensures the value does not exceed the model's generation limit (65_536 tokens). Finally, it checks _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS") and clamps the budget if an administrator cap is present.

docs.title: openrouter_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Computes the planned generation budget for an OpenRouter model. It cross-references OpenRouter catalog specifications to cap allocations using top_provider.max_completion_tokens and applies any OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment setting.

Parameters: * model (str): Target OpenRouter model identifier. * thinking_level (str | None): Requested thinking effort.

Returns: * int | None: Resolved token cap, or None if the model is absent from the catalog and no explicit environment cap was configured.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

budget = openrouter_output_budget("openai/gpt-4o", "medium")


def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    if info is None:
        return _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    model_cap = (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("max_completion_tokens")
    budget = min(budget, model_cap) if model_cap else min(budget, 32_000)
    cap = _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget
If the catalog entry cannot be found (e.g., when routing through a local or non-OpenRouter OpenAI proxy), the function defers to _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS") (which returns None if unset). When metadata is available, it pulls top_provider.max_completion_tokens, defaulting to 32_000 tokens if omitted, and applies any user-defined ceiling.

docs.title: context_output_reserve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Determines how many tokens must be reserved out of the shared context window for the completion payload under the active provider. For Anthropic and OpenRouter, completion and reasoning tokens consume shared context space, requiring a planned deduction. For Gemini, input and output limits are separate, so the reserve is 0.

Parameters: * thinking_level (str | None): Requested reasoning effort level.

Returns: * int | None: Token count to reserve from context capacity, or None if the active provider does not support explicit output reservations.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

reserve = context_output_reserve("high")
# GEMINI -> 0
# ANTHROPIC -> anthropic_planned_output(model, "high")


def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return anthropic_planned_output(model, thinking_level)
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return 0
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return openrouter_output_budget(model, thinking_level)
    return None
This function is called by token_utils.input_token_budget when sizing source code file batches. Returning 0 for Gemini ensures that prompts can fully utilize the entire 1,048,576-token input window without being penalized by the 65,536-token output capacity.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Identifies the operational LLM backend from environment variables. If LLM_PROVIDER is set, its uppercase value takes precedence. Otherwise, it detects GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY to default to "GEMINI". Anthropic is intentionally never auto-selected without an explicit LLM_PROVIDER declaration to prevent inadvertent billable runs when users have ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY variables set for local CLI agents.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str | None: Canonical provider name ("GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC", "OPENROUTER", or a custom identifier), or None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

provider = get_llm_provider()
if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
    check_anthropic_auth()


def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        return provider.strip().upper()
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        return "GEMINI"
    return None
The selection hierarchy prevents accidental cost exposure. Because tools like Claude Code routinely export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in user shell profiles, auto-detecting Anthropic would silently override local or default configurations. Hence, Gemini credentials serve as the fallback, while Anthropic requires explicit opt-in via LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC.

docs.title: gemini_location()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_location() -> str:

Description: Normalizes the Vertex AI region configured via GEMINI_LOCATION to lowercase, defaulting to DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION ("global").

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: Lowercase location identifier.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

loc = gemini_location()
# Returns: "global"


def gemini_location() -> str:
    """GEMINI_LOCATION lower-cased: google-genai matches 'global' / 'us' / 'eu' case-sensitively."""
    return (os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION).strip().lower()
The google-genai SDK performs case-sensitive matching on endpoint location strings. This utility strips surrounding whitespace and forces lowercase formatting to prevent connection initialization errors.

docs.title: openrouter_base_url()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_base_url() -> str:

Description: Retrieves and normalizes OPENROUTER_BASE_URL. Strips trailing slashes and removes any trailing /v1 suffix so that downstream API path constructors can append /v1/chat/completions or /v1/models consistently.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: Clean base URL without trailing slashes or /v1.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

url = f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models"


def openrouter_base_url() -> str:
    """OPENROUTER_BASE_URL without a trailing '/' or '/v1' (OpenAI SDK style); paths add '/v1/...'."""
    base = (os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL).strip().rstrip("/")
    return base.removesuffix("/v1")
Users often configure base URLs with or without trailing /v1 designations depending on whether their tooling conforms to OpenAI SDK standards or raw HTTP formats. Stripping the suffix guarantees deterministic URL construction.

docs.title: is_openrouter_host()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def is_openrouter_host() -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether openrouter_base_url() resolves to the official OpenRouter service (openrouter.ai) as opposed to a custom, self-hosted, or local proxy.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * bool: True if the base URL contains "openrouter.ai", False otherwise.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if not _env_set("OPENROUTER_API_KEY") and is_openrouter_host():
    emit("ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_KEY")


def is_openrouter_host() -> bool:
    return "openrouter.ai" in openrouter_base_url().lower()
This check gates OpenRouter authentication requirements. If a developer redirects OPENROUTER_BASE_URL to a local Ollama or vLLM proxy running without authentication, the system bypasses API key validation checks.

docs.title: resolve_llm_settings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:

Description: The primary source of truth across the pipeline for active LLM parameters. Resolves the active provider, target model identifier, network endpoint URL, and API authentication key by reading provider-specific environment variables.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str]: A 4-tuple containing (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

provider, model, endpoint, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()

docs.title: Multi-Provider Resolution Logic
docs.text:
def resolve_llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
    """Return (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key) for the active provider."""
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            location = gemini_location().lower()
            if location == "global":
                host = "aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            elif location in ("us", "eu"):
                host = f"aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com"  # multi-region endpoints
            else:
                host = f"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            return provider, model, host, ""
        return provider, model, "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        endpoint = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_ENDPOINT
        return provider, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_MODEL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL, endpoint, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "")
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return provider, os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "unknown"), openrouter_base_url(), os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")
    if provider:
        return (
            provider,
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_API_KEY", ""),
        )
    return "UNKNOWN", "unknown", "unknown", ""
For Google Gemini, the function checks for GEMINI_PROJECT_ID to determine whether Vertex AI or Google AI Studio is targeted. For Vertex AI, it generates the appropriate regional host (e.g., aiplatform.googleapis.com, aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com, or regional prefixes) and clears the API key in favor of Google Application Default Credentials. For Anthropic and OpenRouter, it retrieves the model, endpoint, and key. Unrecognized providers fall back to checking dynamic {PROVIDER}_MODEL, {PROVIDER}_BASE_URL, and {PROVIDER}_API_KEY variables.

docs.title: is_claude_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def is_claude_model(provider: str | None, model_name: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the active request targets an Anthropic Claude model. Returns True for native Anthropic provider executions as well as Claude models routed through third-party gateways (e.g., OpenRouter or AWS Bedrock).

Parameters: * provider (str | None): Active provider identifier. * model_name (str): Target model name.

Returns: * bool: True if the configuration routes to a Claude model.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if is_claude_model(provider, model_name):
    ratio = get_token_ratio()


def is_claude_model(provider: str | None, model_name: str) -> bool:
    """True for native Anthropic calls and Claude models reached through a gateway (e.g. OpenRouter)."""
    return provider == "ANTHROPIC" or _normalize_claude_id(model_name).startswith("claude-")
The implementation checks if provider equals "ANTHROPIC" directly. If routed via another provider (such as OpenRouter), it normalizes the model identifier via _normalize_claude_id() to detect if the underlying model is a Claude variant.

docs.title: is_gemini_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def is_gemini_model(provider: str | None, model_name: str) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether the configuration targets a Google Gemini model, either natively or via an external gateway.

Parameters: * provider (str | None): Active provider identifier. * model_name (str): Target model name.

Returns: * bool: True if provider is "GEMINI" or the model name contains "gemini-".

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if is_gemini_model(provider, model_name):
    return _ratio_from_env("GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)


def is_gemini_model(provider: str | None, model_name: str) -> bool:
    return provider == "GEMINI" or "gemini-" in (model_name or "").lower()
This utility provides unified model detection across gateways, ensuring Gemini-specific token calculations and thinking configurations apply even when routing through OpenRouter (google/gemini-3.8-flash).

docs.title: rejects_sampling_params()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:

Description: Identifies models that trigger HTTP 400 errors or emit runtime deprecation warnings if sampling hyperparameters (temperature, top_p, top_k) are provided. This includes modern Claude thinking architectures (Opus 4.7+, Opus/Sonnet 5, Fable, Mythos) and Gemini 3.x models.

Parameters: * model_name (str): Target model identifier.

Returns: * bool: True if sampling parameters must be omitted from API payloads.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# In call_llm.py dispatch
if not rejects_sampling_params(model):
    payload["temperature"] = 0.2


def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:
    name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    return _normalize_claude_id(name).startswith(_NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES) or "gemini-3" in name.lower()
The helper resolves gateway aliases through _catalog_model_id() and normalizes Claude identifiers. It evaluates the model against _NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES and checks for "gemini-3", allowing upstream request dispatchers to strip sampling parameters before sending network payloads.

docs.title: get_token_ratio()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_token_ratio() -> float:

Description: Returns the static prior multiplier that translates tiktoken (cl100k_base) counts into the target model's actual token volume. Accounts for token undercounting on source code and tokenizer revisions. The value is clamped to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS (0.5 to 3.0).

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * float: Clamped token estimation ratio.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

ratio = get_token_ratio()
estimated_tokens = int(tiktoken_count * ratio)


def get_token_ratio() -> float:
    provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    model_name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    if is_claude_model(provider, model_name):
        claude_id = _normalize_claude_id(model_name)  # also handles gateway ids on the native provider
        default = CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_NEW_TOKENIZER if claude_id.startswith(_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES) else CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_OLD_TOKENIZER
        return max(_ratio_from_env("ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO", default), 1.0)
    if is_gemini_model(provider, model_name):
        return _ratio_from_env("GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)
    return _ratio_from_env("LLM_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)
The function checks the active model family. For Claude models, it differentiates between the tokenizer introduced in Opus 4.7 (1.55 prior) and older tokenizers (1.2 prior), allowing overrides via ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO. Gemini models default to 1.0 (overridden by GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO), and all other endpoints defer to LLM_TOKEN_RATIO.

docs.title: openrouter_catalog_cached()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_catalog_cached() -> bool:

Description: Indicates whether the OpenRouter model catalog JSON payload has been successfully fetched and cached in memory.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * bool: True if _openrouter_models_cache contains data, False otherwise.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if openrouter_catalog_cached():
    # Cache hit guaranteed without network request
    info = openrouter_model_info(model_id)

    """True once the OpenRouter catalog has loaded (catalog-derived values may then be cached)."""

Used by caching layers to verify whether catalog-derived metadata can be trusted as stable and initialized.

docs.title: openrouter_catalog()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:

Description: Fetches and caches the list of available models from the OpenRouter /v1/models endpoint. Employs a 60-second cooldown on network or decoding failures to prevent continuous request retries during startup.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * list | None: A list of model specification dictionaries, or None if the fetch failed or cooldown is active.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

catalog = openrouter_catalog()
if catalog:
    print(f"Loaded {len(catalog)} models from OpenRouter")

docs.title: Cache and Circuit-Breaker Lifecycle
docs.text:
def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:
    global _openrouter_models_cache, _openrouter_last_failure
    if _openrouter_models_cache is not None:
        return _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_last_failure and time.time() - _openrouter_last_failure < _OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN:
        return None
    url = f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models"
    try:
        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=20)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json().get("data")
        if not isinstance(data, list):
            raise ValueError("OpenRouter model catalog response has no 'data' list")
        _openrouter_models_cache = data
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.llm_common import warn_once
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        _openrouter_last_failure = time.time()
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Failed to fetch OpenRouter model info from {url}: {e}", dest="LOG")
        if warn_once("openrouter_catalog_unavailable"):
            emit("WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE", url=url, error=str(e)[:200])
        return None
The implementation provides resilience against transient network outages. When requests.get() throws an exception or the payload lacks a valid data array, _openrouter_last_failure records the current timestamp. Any subsequent calls within the 60-second window return None immediately without blocking the event loop or flooding network logs. Warnings are logged once via warn_once().

docs.title: openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Searches the cached OpenRouter catalog for a given model ID. Handles exact matches, routing suffixes (e.g., :nitro, :floor, :thinking), dated canonical slugs, and alias redirects (alias_target).

Parameters: * model_id (str): Requested model name or slug.

Returns: * dict | None: The resolved catalog metadata dictionary, or None if unmapped.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

info = openrouter_model_info("anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet:nitro")
if info:
    context_limit = info.get("context_length")


def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:
    catalog = openrouter_catalog()
    if not catalog or not model_id:
        return None
    wanted = model_id.strip()
    candidates = [wanted, *(wanted[: -len(suffix)] for suffix in _OPENROUTER_ROUTING_SUFFIXES if wanted.endswith(suffix))]
    for name in candidates:
        entry = next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == name or m.get("canonical_slug") == name), None)
        if entry is None:
            dated = re.compile(re.escape(name) + r"-\d{8}")
            entry = next((m for m in catalog if dated.fullmatch(str(m.get("canonical_slug", "")))), None)
        if entry is not None:
            target = (entry.get("alias_target") or {}).get("slug")
            if target and target != entry.get("id"):
                return next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == target or m.get("canonical_slug") == target), entry)
            return entry
    return None
The search candidate list strips recognized OpenRouter routing suffixes (:nitro, :floor, :online, :thinking, :extended, :exacto). For each candidate, it checks id and canonical_slug. If an initial match is missing, it tests for dated variants (...-YYYYMMDD). Once an entry is found, it inspects alias_target to dereference aliases to their canonical target specifications.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Resolves the maximum input context length (in tokens) for the active model. Dispatches to the Anthropic Models API (with offline fallbacks), Google AI Studio / Vertex limits, or OpenRouter catalog metadata. Falls back to 100_000 tokens if resolution fails.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): Active provider endpoint. * model_name (str): Model identifier. * api_key (str, optional): Provider credentials (defaults to "").

Returns: * int: Maximum context input window.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

ctx_len = get_model_context_length("https://api.anthropic.com", "claude-sonnet-5")
# Returns: 200000


def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    default_limit = 100000
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    try:
        if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
            from utils.llm_anthropic import get_model_limits

            return get_model_limits(model_name)[0]

        if provider == "OPENROUTER" or "openrouter.ai" in (endpoint_url or ""):
            info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
            if info:
                return (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or info.get("context_length") or default_limit
            return default_limit

        if provider == "GEMINI":
            try:
                from utils.llm_gemini import get_model_limits as gemini_limits
            except ImportError:
                return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
            return gemini_limits(model_name)[0]

        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit
        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("WARN_CONTEXT_LENGTH_FETCH", model=model_name, endpoint=endpoint_url, error=str(e))

    return default_limit
The dispatch routes to utils.llm_anthropic.get_model_limits for Anthropic models and utils.llm_gemini.get_model_limits for Gemini models. For OpenRouter, it reads top_provider.context_length or context_length from catalog metadata. Any raised exceptions emit a diagnostic WARN_CONTEXT_LENGTH_FETCH event and safely return the fallback limit of 100_000 tokens.

docs.title: describe_thinking_support()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a single-line human-readable summary of how thinking or reasoning parameters apply to the configured model. Used in CLI startup banners.

Parameters: * provider (str): Target provider string. * model (str): Model identifier.

Returns: * str: Formatted description string.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

summary = describe_thinking_support("ANTHROPIC", "claude-sonnet-5")
# Returns: "adaptive thinking + output_config.effort ∈ {low, medium, high, xhigh, max}"


def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:
    """One-line description of how thinking levels are applied for the startup display."""
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        name = (model or "").lower()
        if not name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
            return "thinking.budget_tokens (low…max → 2,048…32,000)"
        levels = "low, medium, high, max" if name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES) else "low, medium, high, xhigh, max"
        return f"adaptive thinking + output_config.effort ∈ {{{levels}}}"
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
        if mode == "level":
            return f"thinking_level ∈ {{{', '.join(spec)}}}"
        if mode == "budget":
            low, high, can_disable = spec
            return f"thinking_budget {low:,}-{high:,}" + (f" ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_BUDGET_OFF')})" if can_disable else "")
        return "—"
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model)
        if info is None:
            return f"reasoning.effort ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE')})" if not openrouter_catalog() else "—"
        reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
        if not isinstance(reasoning, dict):
            return "reasoning.effort" if "reasoning" in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []) else "—"
        efforts = reasoning.get("supported_efforts")
        if "supported_efforts" not in reasoning and reasoning.get("supports_max_tokens"):
            text = "reasoning.max_tokens (minimal…max → 1,024…32,000)"  # llm_openrouter._REASONING_BUDGETS
        elif efforts:
            text = f"reasoning.effort ∈ {{{', '.join(e for e in efforts if e != 'none')}}}"
        else:
            text = "reasoning.effort"
        extras = [_ui("CFG_THINKING_DEFAULT_EFFORT", effort=reasoning["default_effort"])] if reasoning.get("default_effort") else []
        if reasoning.get("mandatory"):
            extras.append(_ui("CFG_THINKING_MANDATORY"))
        return text + (f" · {' · '.join(extras)}" if extras else "")
    return "—"
The logic checks the provider type and constructs a localized string using _ui(). For Anthropic, it distinguishes adaptive models from token-budget models. For Gemini, it notes whether categorical levels or integer budgets apply. For OpenRouter, it reflects whether reasoning is mandatory, effort-driven, or max-token-driven.

docs.title: parse_ant_auth_status()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:

Description: Parses the raw stdout and stderr output of ant auth status to locate active authentication profiles and workspaces. Redacts token prefixes using _redact() to ensure secret strings are not exposed.

Parameters: * output (str): Raw terminal text emitted by the ant CLI tool.

Returns: * tuple[str | None, str | None]: A tuple of (active_credential, active_workspace).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

cred, wrk = parse_ant_auth_status(cli_output)
# cred == "Profile (user_oauth) [via active_config] sk-ant-***"


def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    section, credential, workspace = None, None, None
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if not line[0].isspace():
            header = line.strip().lower()
            section = header if header in ("credentials", "workspace") else None
            continue
        if "(active)" not in line:
            continue
        text = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", _redact(re.sub(r"^\s*\(active\)\s*\*?\s*", "", line))).strip()
        if section == "workspace":
            workspace = workspace or text
        else:
            credential = credential or text
    return credential, workspace
The parsing routine ignores CLI exit codes, as the ant command can return non-zero codes while still outputting valid profile data. It tracks current sections (credentials vs workspace), scans indented lines for the (active) marker, strips out asterisks and excess whitespace, and runs _redact() to scrub sensitive token strings.

docs.title: check_anthropic_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def check_anthropic_auth() -> bool:

Description: Performs preflight credential verification when LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC. Verifies package installation, environment variables, Workload Identity Federation settings, and local ant auth login profiles.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * bool: True if valid credentials are confirmed; False if unauthenticated.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if not check_anthropic_auth():
    sys.exit(1)

docs.title: Phase 1: SDK and Direct Environment Validation
docs.text:
if get_llm_provider() != "ANTHROPIC":
        return True
    if not _anthropic_sdk_installed():
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING")
        return False

    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") and _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN")
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        return True
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN")
        return True
    if all(_env_set(v) for v in _FEDERATION_VARS) and (_env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE") or _env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN")):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="Workload Identity Federation")
        return True
The preflight verifies that the anthropic Python package can be imported. It then checks for direct credentials: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or Workload Identity Federation variables (ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID, ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID, plus token parameters). If any are valid, the preflight completes successfully.

docs.title: Phase 2: CLI Subprocess and Profile Auditing
docs.text:
ant = shutil.which("ant")
    if not ant:
        stored = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(_anthropic_config_dir(), "credentials", "*.json")))
        if stored:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND", path=stored[0])
            return True
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS")
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=False)
        return False

    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not (k in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN") and not v.strip())}
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([ant, "auth", "status"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=30, env=env)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED", error=str(e))
        return True

    output = f"{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}"
    credential, workspace = parse_ant_auth_status(output)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ant auth status | exit={result.returncode}\n{_redact(output).strip()}", dest="LOG")
    if not credential:
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN")
        details = _redact(output).strip()
        if details:
            emit_raw("INFO", "\n".join(f"    {line}" for line in details.splitlines()))
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=True)
        return False

    source = _ui("AUTH_SOURCE_ANT_LOGIN", credential=credential)
    if workspace:
        source += f" | {_ui('AUTH_SOURCE_WORKSPACE', workspace=workspace)}"
    emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source=source)
    return True
If environment keys are absent, the check looks for the ant CLI tool via shutil.which(). If missing, it checks for stored JSON profiles in _anthropic_config_dir(). If ant is available, it executes ant auth status under a sanitized environment. The output is processed by parse_ant_auth_status(); if an active credential row is present, authentication is confirmed. Otherwise, detailed setup instructions are emitted.

docs.title: check_gemini_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def check_gemini_config() -> bool:

Description: Validates configuration and credentials for Google Gemini (both Vertex AI and Google AI Studio). Enforces SDK version constraints (google-genai >= 1.56.0), detects retired model names, and validates credentials.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * bool: True if Gemini is configured correctly; False otherwise.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if not check_gemini_config():
    sys.exit(1)


def check_gemini_config() -> bool:
    from utils.output import emit

    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
    version = _installed_version("google-genai")
    if version is None:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING")
        return False
    if version < GEMINI_MIN_SDK:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED", version=".".join(map(str, version)), required=".".join(map(str, GEMINI_MIN_SDK)))
        return False

    retired = GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS.get(gemini_model_id(model))
    if retired:
        replacement, aliased_on_ai_studio = retired
        if aliased_on_ai_studio and not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
        else:
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
            return False

    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        location = gemini_location()
        allowed = gemini_vertex_locations(model)
        if allowed is not None and location.lower() not in allowed:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_LOCATION", location=location, model=model, allowed=", ".join(allowed))
        try:
            import google.auth

            google.auth.default()
        except Exception as e:
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS", error=str(e).splitlines()[0][:200])
            return False
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_VERTEX", project=os.environ["GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"], location=location))
        return True
    if _env_set("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_AI_STUDIO"))
        return True
    emit("ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS")
    return False
The preflight verifies that google-genai is installed and meets the 1.56.0 version threshold (older versions fail on thinking_level Pydantic models). It flags deprecated model names in GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS, failing if used on Vertex AI. For Vertex AI configurations (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID set), it validates the selected region against gemini_vertex_locations() and verifies Google Application Default Credentials via google.auth.default(). For AI Studio, it verifies that GEMINI_API_KEY is populated.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def check_openrouter_config() -> bool:

Description: Validates environment variables for OpenRouter runs. Ensures OPENROUTER_API_KEY is present (when targeting openrouter.ai) and verifies that OPENROUTER_MODEL is declared.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * bool: True if configuration is valid; False otherwise.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

if not check_openrouter_config():
    sys.exit(1)


def check_openrouter_config() -> bool:
    from utils.output import emit

    if not _env_set("OPENROUTER_API_KEY") and is_openrouter_host():
        emit("ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_KEY")
        return False
    model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "").strip()
    if not model:
        emit("ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_MODEL")
        return False
    if openrouter_catalog() and openrouter_model_info(model) is None:
        emit("WARN_OPENROUTER_MODEL_UNKNOWN", model=model)
    emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="OpenRouter", source=f"OPENROUTER_API_KEY | {model} | {openrouter_base_url()}")
    return True
The check verifies OPENROUTER_API_KEY when targeting the official host, allowing unauthenticated connections for local proxies. It ensures OPENROUTER_MODEL is not empty. If the OpenRouter catalog is accessible, it checks whether the model exists and warns if the model ID is unrecognized.

docs.title: check_llm_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def check_llm_auth() -> bool:

Description: Main authentication preflight dispatcher. Identifies the active provider via get_llm_provider() and routes execution to check_anthropic_auth(), check_gemini_config(), or check_openrouter_config().

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * bool: True if the active provider passes preflight validation; False otherwise.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# In main.py before crawling begins
if not check_llm_auth():
    sys.exit(1)


def check_llm_auth() -> bool:
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return check_anthropic_auth()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return check_gemini_config()
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return check_openrouter_config()
    return True
This function serves as the central entry point called by main.py and diagnostic testing scripts. Unrecognized or custom providers default to returning True, bypassing vendor-specific checks.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _env_int(name: str) -> int | None:

Description: Parses an environment variable as a strictly positive integer. Non-numeric, empty, or negative values evaluate to None.

Parameters: * name (str): Target environment variable name.

Returns: * int | None: Positive integer, or None.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

cap = _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")


def _env_int(name: str) -> int | None:

docs.title: _normalize_claude_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes heterogeneous Claude identifiers (from OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, or legacy aliases) into a canonical format (e.g., mapping "anthropic/claude-4.7-opus-20260416" to "claude-opus-4-7-20260416").

Parameters: * model_name (str): Raw model identifier.

Returns: * str: Canonical normalized Claude model identifier.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

clean_id = _normalize_claude_id("bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1:0")
# Returns: "claude-opus-4-7-v1:0"


def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    name = (model_name or "").lower().replace(".", "-")
    start = name.find("claude-")
    name = name[start:] if start >= 0 else name
    match = _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST.match(name)
    if match:
        major, minor, family = match.groups()
        name = f"claude-{family}-{major}" + (f"-{minor}" if minor else "") + name[match.end() :]
    return name
The normalization replaces periods with hyphens, extracts the claude- substring, and applies _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST to flip version-first patterns into family-first representations.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _catalog_model_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Resolves OpenRouter model aliases (e.g., ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest) to canonical catalog IDs so downstream model family checks can evaluate the actual underlying model.

Parameters: * model_name (str): Model name or alias.

Returns: * str: Resolved canonical model ID.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)


def _catalog_model_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    if get_llm_provider() == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
        if info and info.get("id"):
            return info["id"]
    return model_name or ""
Queries openrouter_model_info() when OpenRouter is active, dereferencing aliases to their target models. For other providers, it returns the input unchanged.

docs.title: _ratio_from_env()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:

Description: Parses a float ratio from an environment variable and clamps it within TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS. Defaults to default if the value is unparsable or non-finite.

Parameters: * name (str): Target environment variable. * default (float): Fallback multiplier.

Returns: * float: Clamped token ratio.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

ratio = _ratio_from_env("ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.55)


def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    try:
        ratio = float(os.getenv(name, default))
    except ValueError:
        ratio = default
    if not math.isfinite(ratio):
        ratio = default
    low, high = TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS
    return min(max(ratio, low), high)
Catches ValueError exceptions and checks math.isfinite() to ignore NaN or Infinity. It then clamps the ratio between 0.5 and 3.0 to keep token budgeting stable.
