docs.title: COLORS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: COLORS = { ... }

Description: Module-level mapping linking discrete operational logging levels (PROGRESS, SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, INFO, DEBUG, FILE_WRITE, UI) to standard ANSI 16-color escape sequences.

COLORS = {
    "PROGRESS": "\033[96m",  # Cyan — LLM calls, active steps
    "SUCCESS": "\033[92m",  # Green — completions, cache hits
    "WARNING": "\033[93m",  # Yellow — warnings, capacity alerts
    "ERROR": "\033[91m",  # Red — errors, failures
    "INFO": "",  # Plain — config, counts, labels
    "DEBUG": "\033[90m",  # Gray — skipped files, debug
    "FILE_WRITE": "",  # Plain — "  - Wrote {path}" messages
    "UI": "",  # N/A — used in generated docs, never printed
}

The COLORS dictionary defines visual hierarchy across terminal outputs. Active operational steps and LLM dispatches use high-intensity cyan, while success indicators and cache reconciliations are colored green. Warning and error conditions trigger yellow and red highlights respectively. Informational labels, documentation writes, and UI markdown strings remain uncolored to maintain clean piping.

docs.title: RESET
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: RESET = "\033[0m"

Description: The standard ANSI reset sequence used to terminate active terminal color formatting and return standard output streams to default terminal styling.

RESET = "\033[0m"

This constant is conditionally concatenated to the end of colored log messages whenever COLORS.get(level) yields a non-empty string. It guarantees that subsequent console output retains default terminal styling across interactive shells.

docs.title: PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES = 5_000

Description: The maximum upper boundary for the in-memory log buffer (_pending_log) before physical log file instantiation.

PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES = 5_000

PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES defines a bounded memory guard preventing unbounded growth of unpersisted log messages during pre-execution phases. When pipeline initialization runs without active disk file handlers, oldest lines are dropped using FIFO eviction once this threshold is crossed.

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):

Description: Initializes the output subsystem by setting target localization variables, configuring stream encodings, loading strings.csv into memory, and optionally triggering missing string translations.

Parameters: * language (str): Target language name for UI and console display (e.g., "Vietnamese", "english"). Defaults to "english". * use_cache (bool): Whether upstream LLM caching is active for automated translation passes. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None): Model reasoning effort tier passed to background translation requests. Defaults to None. * debug (bool): Boolean flag enabling verbose debug diagnostics across console streams. Defaults to False. * auto_translate (bool): Flag indicating whether missing string translations should be resolved immediately upon initialization. Defaults to True.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None. File and stream configuration errors are trapped or normalized internally.

Example: 

# Initializing output system with custom language and debug logging
init(language="english")


def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):
    """Initialize the output system: load strings.csv, set language, auto-translate missing.

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments but before any emit() calls.

    Args:
        language: Target language name (e.g., "Vietnamese").
        use_cache: Whether LLM caching is enabled (passed to translation calls).
        thinking_level: LLM thinking level (passed to translation calls).
        auto_translate: Translate missing strings now. main() passes False and calls
            translate_missing_strings() after argument validation and the LLM auth preflight,
            because translation is itself an LLM call.
    """
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level, _debug
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _debug = debug
    _ensure_utf8_streams()
    _load_strings()
    if auto_translate:
        _auto_translate()

The initialization routine configures the global module state. It normalizes language identifiers into capitalized presentation labels (_language) and lowercase column headers (_lang_col). It computes the absolute path to strings.csv, saves LLM translation parameters, invokes UTF-8 terminal encoding verification, and parses the CSV into memory. If auto_translate is set to True, it initiates translation of missing localized strings before returning control to the caller.

docs.title: translate_missing_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def translate_missing_strings():

Description: Dispatches an explicit request to scan for and auto-translate missing strings for the configured target language via an LLM.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * None. Exceptions occurring during network transport or CSV persistence are handled inside the translation module.

Example: 

# Executed in main pipeline after authentication preflight succeeds
translate_missing_strings()


def translate_missing_strings():
    """Auto-translate strings missing for the configured language (LLM call); see init(auto_translate=False)."""
    _auto_translate()

This function allows the caller to decouple initialization from translation calls. In standard pipeline workflows, init() is called with auto_translate=False before CLI parsing and API authentication checks run. Once model credentials and network configurations are validated, translate_missing_strings() is explicitly invoked to perform required translations without risking early authentication failures.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):

Description: Retrieves a localized template by key from the in-memory translation table, interpolates runtime keyword variables, applies ANSI color styling, and dispatches formatted output to designated targets (terminal, log file, or both).

Parameters: * key (str): Unique string identifier corresponding to a STRING_KEY in strings.csv. * suffix (str): Optional string appended to the formatted template text prior to terminal emission or file logging. Defaults to "". * **kwargs (Any): Keyword substitutions mapped to placeholders within the message template.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None. Unrecognized keys trigger a defensive console fallback message without interrupting program flow.

Example: 

# Usage from source code docstring
emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", chapter_num=1, name="flow")


def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    """Emit a translatable string to stdout and/or log file.

    Args:
        key: String key from strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER").
        suffix: Optional extra text appended after the main message (e.g., token breakdown).
        **kwargs: Variables to substitute into the string template.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]

    # D-prefixed destinations (DBOTH, DSTDOUT): debug-gated console output.
    # Without --debug, suppress console but always log. Preserves original color from LEVEL.
    if dest.startswith("D"):
        if _debug:
            dest = dest[1:]  # DBOTH → BOTH, DSTDOUT → STDOUT
        else:
            dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)

The emit function coordinates message retrieval, formatting, and routing. When an unknown key is encountered, it logs an [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] notice to sys.stdout and exits cleanly. For valid entries, dynamic parameters are interpolated using _format_safe, and the optional suffix is appended. Destinations with a D prefix (DBOTH, DSTDOUT) are evaluated against _debug: if debugging is disabled, console output is suppressed and the destination becomes LOG. Finally, messages routed to BOTH or STDOUT are printed with ANSI styling, while destinations matching BOTH or LOG are passed to _write_log.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):

Description: Emits pre-formatted strings directly to console or log streams under a specified logging level without performing table lookups or variable substitution.

Parameters: * level (str): Logging level identifier matching keys in COLORS (e.g., "INFO", "WARNING", "DEBUG", "SUCCESS"). * text (str): The pre-formatted text payload to emit. * dest (str): Destination routing specifier ("BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG"). Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Direct emission of pre-formatted run banners
sep = "=" * 80
emit_raw("INFO", sep, dest="LOG")


def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    """Emit a pre-formatted string with explicit level styling.

    Use for dynamic/structural output that doesn't come from strings.csv
    (e.g., numbered file lists, batch details, crawl summary tables).
    """
    # DEBUG-level: suppress console unless --debug is active
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug:
        dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)

emit_raw outputs dynamic and structural payloads that cannot be defined as static templates in strings.csv, such as file trees, batch tables, and crawling summaries. It checks if the specified level is "DEBUG": when debugging is disabled, console dispatch is silenced by forcing dest = "LOG". The text is styled using the ANSI escape codes mapped in COLORS and routed to the requested targets.

docs.text:

# Used by external modules to gate complex diagnostic generation
if is_debug():

This function acts as a public accessor for the module's internal _debug state. It allows external components to check whether debug mode is active before running expensive diagnostic routines, token tracing, or formatting verbose debug strings.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get(key, **kwargs):

Description: Resolves and returns a translated string template with keyword variables substituted, without printing to standard output or writing to log files.

Parameters: * key (str): Target string identifier defined in strings.csv. * **kwargs (Any): Keyword substitutions mapped to placeholders within the string template.

Returns: * str: The translated and interpolated string, or the raw key if no matching record is found.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Retrieve raw translated UI string for markdown generation
label = get("UI_TUTORIAL")


def get(key, **kwargs):
    """Get a translated string without printing or logging.

    Use for UI strings embedded in generated markdown (index.md headings, etc.).
    Returns the raw translated text with variable substitution applied.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)

get extracts translated text for programmatic use, such as generating Markdown headers, table labels, and documentation metadata, where console emission or log persistence is undesirable. If the requested key is absent from the in-memory string cache, it returns the raw key string as a fallback.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):

Description: Establishes a dedicated run-level log file on disk, writes execution metadata headers, and flushes buffered startup log records into the file.

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the codebase project being processed. Sanitized for filesystem safety. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): Documentation generation mode (e.g., "tutorial", "api-reference"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The relative filesystem path to the newly created log file.

Raises: * OSError: If the target directory cannot be created or the file cannot be opened.

Example: 

# Invoked after parsing CLI options
log_path = configure_logging(project_name="my_repo", mode="tutorial")


def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    """Configure file-based logging for this run.

    Creates a new log file per invocation:
        logs/{project_name}_{mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments.
    """
    global _log_file

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_path = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Close any existing log file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()

    _log_file = open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8")  # noqa: SIM115

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    sep = "=" * 80
    emit_raw("INFO", sep, dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"Log file: {log_path}", dest="LOG")
    if _pending_log:
        _log_file.write("".join(_pending_log))
        _log_file.flush()
        _pending_log.clear()

    return log_path

configure_logging initializes the file-based logging system. It resolves the output directory using the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to "logs") and creates the directory if needed. Project and mode strings are sanitized to prevent invalid path characters, and a timestamped filename is generated. Any open log handles are closed before opening the new file with UTF-8 encoding. Initial header metadata is written directly to the log, and any pre-configuration messages stored in _pending_log are written to disk and flushed, clearing the buffer.

docs.title: shutdown()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def shutdown():

Description: Closes the active log file handle and resets internal log state to release underlying filesystem resources.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Executed within a finally block in the application entrypoint
try:
    pass # Run pipeline
finally:
    shutdown()


def shutdown():
    """Close the log file handle and release resources.

    Should be called at the end of main() in a finally block to ensure
    the log file is properly flushed and closed.
    """
    global _log_file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()
        _log_file = None

shutdown cleans up persistent file handles when the pipeline exits. Designed to be called from a finally block in main(), it closes _log_file if open and resets the handle to None. This guarantees that buffered output streams are flushed and file locks are released across execution environments.

docs.title: _write_log()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_log(level, text):

Description: Formats a single timestamped log record and writes it to the active log file, or buffers it in memory if the file handle is not yet open.

Parameters: * level (str): Logging severity identifier (e.g., "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR"). * text (str): Payload text to write.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Internal call site from emit()
_write_log("INFO", "Execution step initiated")


def _write_log(level, text):
    """Write a timestamped line to the log file (buffered until configure_logging opens it)."""
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f")[:-3]
    line = f"{ts} - {level} - {text}\n"
    if _log_file is None:
        _pending_log.append(line)
        if len(_pending_log) > PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES:
            del _pending_log[0]
        return
    _log_file.write(line)
    _log_file.flush()

_write_log handles file logging operations. It formats log entries with a millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm), the logging level, and the message text. If _log_file is uninitialized, the entry is appended to _pending_log. When _pending_log exceeds PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES (5,000 entries), the oldest entry is removed via FIFO eviction. Once _log_file is active, entries are written directly to disk and flushed immediately.

docs.title: _ensure_utf8_streams()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _ensure_utf8_streams():

Description: Reconfigures redirected or piped sys.stdout and sys.stderr streams to use UTF-8 encoding on platforms where non-UTF-8 defaults could cause encoding errors.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * None.

Example: 

# Internal invocation within init()
_ensure_utf8_streams()


def _ensure_utf8_streams():
    """Write UTF-8 when stdout/stderr are piped or redirected.

    On Windows a redirected stream uses the ANSI code page (e.g. cp1252) and any
    non-English CLI string (Vietnamese, CJK, ...) raises UnicodeEncodeError. Interactive
    consoles already use UTF-8 (PEP 528), so only non-TTY streams are reconfigured.
    """
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        encoding = (getattr(stream, "encoding", "") or "").lower().replace("-", "")
        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure") and encoding != "utf8" and not stream.isatty():
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

_ensure_utf8_streams guards against stream encoding failures when output is piped or redirected on platforms like Windows, where non-interactive streams may default to legacy ANSI code pages (such as cp1252). It iterates over sys.stdout and sys.stderr, inspecting their declared encodings. If a stream is not a TTY terminal and its encoding is not UTF-8, it calls reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") to prevent UnicodeEncodeError exceptions when outputting localized or non-ASCII characters.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _format_safe(template, kwargs):

Description: Interpolates keyword variables into a template string, returning the raw template unmodified if substitution fails due to mismatched or missing keys.

Parameters: * template (str): Template string containing {placeholder} variables. * kwargs (dict): Dictionary of keyword arguments to substitute.

Returns: * str: The formatted string, or the raw template if formatting raises an exception.

Raises: * None. KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError are caught internally.

Example: 

# Safe keyword substitution
formatted = _format_safe("Wrote {path}", {"path": "docs/index.md"})


def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    """Apply .format(**kwargs) with graceful fallback on missing keys."""
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template

_format_safe wraps Python's standard str.format() in a fail-soft boundary. If the template contains malformed brace patterns or references keys not present in kwargs, it catches KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError and returns the unformatted template string. This prevents formatting errors from interrupting pipeline execution.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings():

Description: Parses strings.csv into the internal _strings cache, selecting localized column values when available and falling back to English defaults.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If reading strings.csv fails unexpectedly.

Example: 

# Invoked during init() and after auto-translation updates
_load_strings()


def _load_strings():
    """Load all strings from strings.csv."""
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")

_load_strings reads strings.csv using the utf-8-sig encoding to handle optional Byte Order Marks. It iterates over the CSV rows using csv.DictReader, skipping blank lines and comments prefixed with #. For each entry, it parses LEVEL and DEST, then checks the column for the active language (_lang_col); if empty, it falls back to the "english" column. The parsed record is stored in _strings. When a non-English language is fully translated, it emits a SUCCESS message confirming that all strings were loaded.

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _auto_translate():

Description: Invokes the utils.i18n.auto_translate module to scan for missing translations, query an LLM for translated values, update strings.csv, and reload updated strings into memory.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * None

Raises: * None. Upstream exceptions are caught and logged inside the i18n subsystem.

Example: 

# Internal invocation from translate_missing_strings()
_auto_translate()


def _auto_translate():
    """Auto-translate missing strings via LLM and write back into strings.csv."""
    from utils.i18n import auto_translate

    if auto_translate(_lang_col, _language, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level):
        # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
        _load_strings()

_auto_translate handles missing string translations. To avoid circular imports between output.py and call_llm.py, it imports auto_translate locally within the function body. It passes the current language identifiers, CSV filesystem path, caching preferences, and reasoning effort configuration. If auto_translate returns True (indicating that new translations were written to disk), _auto_translate invokes _load_strings() to refresh the in-memory cache with the new translations.

docs.title: In-Memory String Entry Shape
docs.text:
Represents the structural value schema stored for each key inside the _strings dictionary:

Field Type Description Example text str The localized or fallback English string template, with optional {name} format tokens. "Writing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}..." level str Operational logging severity level matching keys in COLORS. "PROGRESS" dest str Destination identifier determining whether output routes to terminal, log file, or both. "BOTH"

docs.title: strings.csv Record Layout
docs.text:
Defines the schema expected when parsing entries from utils/strings.csv:

Column Presence Description STRING_KEY Mandatory Unique programmatic string identifier queried by emit() and get(). Rows starting with # are treated as comments. LEVEL Mandatory Logging severity tier (PROGRESS, SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, INFO, DEBUG, FILE_WRITE, UI). DEST Mandatory Target routing channel (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT, UI). english Mandatory The canonical English fallback text template. <lang_col> Dynamic One or more dynamic language columns (e.g., vietnamese, japanese) matched against _lang_col.

docs.title: Destination Routing Codes
docs.text:
Routing behavior for strings emitted via emit and emit_raw:

Destination Code Console Output (STDOUT) File Logging (LOG) Debug Behavior BOTH Yes Yes Unconditionally active STDOUT Yes No Unconditionally active LOG No Yes Unconditionally active DBOTH Conditional Yes Emits to BOTH if --debug is active; otherwise routes to LOG only DSTDOUT Conditional No Emits to STDOUT if --debug is active; otherwise discarded UI No No Never printed or logged; reserved for get() calls in markdown documents

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Missing Translation Template Keys: If emit(key) is invoked with an unknown identifier, it avoids raising KeyError by printing a fallback message ([UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]) directly to sys.stdout. Similarly, get(key) returns the un-interpolated key string itself.
  • Variable Interpolation Errors: In _format_safe, string template substitution catches KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError. If placeholders do not match the provided keyword arguments, the unformatted template is returned intact rather than raising an exception.
  • Redirected Stream Encoding Collisions: On Windows systems, non-TTY streams (such as redirected files or pipes) can cause UnicodeEncodeError when emitting non-ASCII characters. The private helper _ensure_utf8_streams inspects sys.stdout and sys.stderr and reconfigures them to utf-8 with replacement error handling (errors="replace").
  • Early Run Buffer Eviction: Log messages generated before configure_logging() initializes a file handle are stored in _pending_log. If this list exceeds PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES (5,000 lines), the oldest lines are dropped using FIFO eviction to prevent unbounded memory growth.
  • Path Sanitization in File Logging: In configure_logging, the project_name parameter is sanitized by filtering out any characters that are not alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores, or periods. The mode parameter replaces hyphens with underscores, ensuring the generated log filename is safe across operating systems.
  • Circular Import Defense: The _auto_translate() function uses a local deferred import (from utils.i18n import auto_translate) to avoid circular import cycles between output.py, i18n.py, and upstream LLM dispatch modules.

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text: Source: utils/prompts.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building directly upon the centralized logging and diagnostic output infrastructure of output.py (doc: utils/output.py.md), prompts.py provides template loading, string compilation, and resilient response-parsing routines that mediate interactions between pipeline nodes and language models. The module acts as the core prompt engineering and deserialization substrate across tutorial, advanced, SDK, and API-reference documentation generation modes. It encapsulates prompt asset resolution from the filesystem (prompts/{mode}/), generates contextual prompt segments such as verified AST facts blocks and focus notes, and provides specialized inline prompt generators for file filtering and chapter summarization.

A primary technical challenge addressed by this module is the fragility of structured data extraction from large language models. LLMs frequently emit invalid YAML due to unquoted colons in code signatures, syntax indicators (@, #, *, &) at the beginning of identifiers, unescaped quote marks in extracted evidence, and conversational Markdown fences. Furthermore, responses truncated by context or generation token limits can result in syntactically complete prefixes that silently omit critical data. prompts.py solves this through a multi-tiered, fail-soft parsing pipeline that pairs truncation detection with progressive normalization, regex-based block scalar conversion, and granular list item salvage routines.

The module also prepares grounded contextual blocks for code documentation generation. Through build_verified_facts_block, it synthesizes source-verified symbol signatures, cross-module import targets, configuration keys, and error definitions into prompt context blocks. This ensures that downstream chapter drafting agents remain strictly aligned with physical source code facts extracted by upstream analysis stages.

docs.title: parse_file_index()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_file_index(idx_value):

Description: Extracts the first integer match found in an index representation returned by an LLM. It accommodates various scalar and string formats emitted by models, including raw integers, annotated index strings (e.g., "3 # path/to/file.py"), and range notation (e.g., "0-3"). When encountering a range, it yields the initial integer; caller logic is expected to handle full interval expansions.

Parameters: * idx_value (Any): The raw index value returned by the model (integer, string, or arbitrary object).

Returns: * int | None: The extracted non-negative integer, or None if no numerical digits are present in the string representation.

Raises: * No exceptions raised; non-matching formats return None.

Example: 

def parse_file_index(idx_value):
    """Extract the first integer from an LLM-returned file index value.

    Handles multiple formats the LLM may produce:
    - Plain int: 3
    - Annotated string: "3 # path/to/file.py"
    - Range notation: "0-3" → returns first number only (caller handles ranges)

    Returns:
        int or None if no digits found.
    """
    nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_value))
    return int(nums[0]) if nums else None

The function executes a coarse regular expression scan r"\d+" over the stringified input representation. By selecting index [0] of the matched numeric sequences, it strips trailing comments, path annotations, and trailing delimiter bounds. If no numeric digits exist in the stringified value, the method gracefully returns None.

docs.title: parse_file_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_file_indices(idx_value) -> list[int]:

Description: Strictly parses an LLM-returned index item into a list of constituent file indices. Unlike parse_file_index(), which aggressively takes the first numeric match from any arbitrary string, this function enforces strict syntactic validation to prevent file paths containing digits (e.g., src/v2/api.py) or negative numbers from being incorrectly mapped to index slots. It handles explicit booleans, integers, single annotated index entries, and contiguous index ranges up to an interval length of 10,000.

Parameters: * idx_value (Any): A single entry from a model-generated index list.

Returns: * list[int]: A list containing the parsed integer index, the expanded range of indices, or an empty list if validation fails.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def parse_file_indices(idx_value) -> list[int]:
    """Strictly parse one entry of an index list the LLM returned → the indices it names.

    An int, an annotated number (``"3 # path"``) or an ascending range (``"0-3"``, ``"4..7"``, expanded). Anything
    else — a negative number, a path with a digit in it (``src/v2/api.py``), prose — names no index, instead
    of the first digit run picking an unrelated file."""
    if isinstance(idx_value, bool):
        return []
    if isinstance(idx_value, int):
        return [idx_value] if idx_value >= 0 else []
    text = str(idx_value) if isinstance(idx_value, str) else ""
    single = _INDEX_RE.match(text)
    if single:
        return [int(single.group(1))]
    span = _INDEX_RANGE_RE.match(text)
    if span and int(span.group(1)) <= int(span.group(2)) and int(span.group(2)) - int(span.group(1)) < 10000:
        return list(range(int(span.group(1)), int(span.group(2)) + 1))
    return []

The parsing sequence enforces short-circuit guards: booleans are rejected immediately to prevent Python's bool subclassing behavior from treating True/False as 1/0. Non-negative integers are wrapped directly. For string inputs, _INDEX_RE checks for solitary numbers optionally followed by hash-delimited comments. If that does not match, _INDEX_RANGE_RE evaluates range expressions supporting hyphen (-), double-dot (..), en-dash (\u2013), or "to" delimiters. If the interval is non-inverted and spans fewer than 10,000 items, range() generates the full index list; otherwise, an empty list is returned.

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):

Description: Loads a Markdown prompt template from the project's prompts/ subdirectories. It resolves directory routing based on mode flags, reads the target file using utf-8-sig encoding to handle potential Byte Order Marks transparently, logs a debug tracing message via utils.output.emit_raw, and returns the raw template contents.

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the prompt template file (without the .md extension). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Legacy flag indicating whether to use prompts/advanced/ instead of prompts/tutorial/ when mode is None. Defaults to False. * mode (str | None, optional): The execution mode directory (e.g., "api-reference", "sdk", "advanced", "tutorial", "common"). Overrides advanced_mode when supplied. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw string content of the prompt template file.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the constructed prompt path does not resolve to an existing file on disk. * IOError: If reading the file encounters filesystem access failures.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        content = f.read()
    from utils.output import emit_raw

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"load_prompt_template | loaded '{template_name}.md' from prompts/{prompt_dir}/", dest="LOG")
    return content

Path resolution computes the absolute root by taking the parent directory of utils/ and appending prompts, the selected prompt_dir, and {template_name}.md. File reading is executed within a context manager using encoding="utf-8-sig". A deferred import of emit_raw from utils.output is utilized to emit a localized debug trace to the log channel without triggering circular module-level imports.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response):

Description: Extracts and deserializes YAML data enclosed within Markdown code fences (yaml ...) from an LLM response. It enforces truncation detection: if the response object has its truncated attribute set to True, the function raises an explicit ValueError to force the calling orchestration node to retry rather than operating on incomplete data structures.

Parameters: * response (str | Any): The raw text response or response object (e.g., TruncatedResponse) returned by the LLM client.

Returns: * Any: The deserialized Python data structure (typically a dict or list) parsed from the YAML block.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the response is flagged as truncated, if no ```yaml fence exists, or if yaml.safe_load() fails due to syntax errors.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    # A reply cut off at max tokens (llm_common.TruncatedResponse) can still contain a parseable
    # fenced prefix that silently drops items — raise so the node retries instead.
    if getattr(response, "truncated", False):
        raise ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed")
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

The function checks getattr(response, "truncated", False) upfront to prevent processing partial outputs where token limits severed the payload. It extracts the YAML substring by splitting on ```yaml and subsequently on the closing ``` fence. The extracted string is parsed via yaml.safe_load(). Any parsing exception or indexing failure is wrapped and raised as a ValueError with contextual details.

docs.title: parse_grouping_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_grouping_response(response):

Description: Parses the multi-section YAML output returned by the group_modules.md prompt, which defines documentation sections, descriptions, and inter-module dependencies. Because models frequently introduce syntax errors in long structural YAML blocks—such as wrapping section roles in backticks or misformatting single description entries—this function incorporates a multi-phase recovery mechanism. If full-block parsing fails, it strips backticks from role fields and splits the YAML into independent top-level key blocks (sections:, descriptions:, dependencies:), parsing each independently and aggregating valid components.

Parameters: * response (str | Any): The raw response string or response object from the LLM.

Returns: * dict: Deserialized grouping payload containing at least a "sections" list, alongside any recovered "descriptions" and "dependencies" mappings.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the response is truncated, lacks a ```yaml block, or if the "sections" block cannot be recovered.

docs.title: Standard YAML Evaluation
docs.text:
try:
        return parse_yaml_response(response)
    except ValueError:
        if getattr(response, "truncated", False) or "```yaml" not in response:
            raise
The execution begins by attempting a strict parse through parse_yaml_response(). If this succeeds, the deserialized dictionary is returned immediately. If it raises a ValueError, the function evaluates whether recovery is viable; if the input is marked as truncated or completely lacks a ```yaml marker, recovery is skipped and the exception is re-raised.

docs.title: Section-Wise Chunk Recovery
docs.text:
yaml_str = response.split("```yaml", 1)[1].split("```", 1)[0]
        yaml_str = re.sub(r"(?m)^(\s*(?:-\s+)?role\s*:\s*)`([^`\n]*)`", r"\1\2", yaml_str)
        parsed = {}
        for chunk in re.split(r"(?m)^(?=(?:sections|descriptions|dependencies)\s*:)", yaml_str):
            try:
                part = yaml.safe_load(chunk)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if isinstance(part, dict):
                parsed.update(part)
        if not isinstance(parsed.get("sections"), list):
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse YAML: no sections list in the grouping reply") from None
        return parsed
During the recovery phase, the function extracts the raw YAML substring and uses re.sub to unwrap invalid backtick annotations on role: keys (e.g., role:core` ->role: core). It splits the text along top-level section boundaries using lookahead assertions forsections:,descriptions:, ordependencies:. Each chunk is parsed independently viayaml.safe_load(). Any chunk that fails does not invalidate others. Finally, the function validates that a valid"sections"list was recovered; if missing, it raises a terminalValueError`.

docs.title: build_verified_facts_block()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_verified_facts_block(facts: dict | None, doc_paths: dict) -> str:

Description: Constructs the {verified_facts} context block for draft_chapters.md prompts in API-reference documentation mode. It formats verified code facts—such as symbols, signatures, module dependencies, configuration keys, and error handling declarations—extracted by the ExtractFacts pipeline stage. Signatures are normalized to single lines with decorator prefixes stripped, wrapped in collision-resistant inline code spans, and annotated with continuation markers if truncated.

Parameters: * facts (dict | None): A dictionary of verified claims extracted from the source file. If None, empty, or lacking verified claims, an empty string is returned. * doc_paths (dict[str, str]): Mapping of internal module source paths to their corresponding documentation chapter filenames (used to render See Also reference targets).

Returns: * str: Formatted Markdown block ready for prompt interpolation, or an empty string if no valid facts exist.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

docs.title: Guard and Preconditions Check
docs.text:
if not facts or facts.get("claims") is None:
        return ""
    symbols = facts.get("symbols") or []
    modules = list(dict.fromkeys(edge["module"] for edge in facts.get("depends_on") or []))
    config = facts.get("config") or []
    errors = list(dict.fromkeys(item["name"] for item in facts.get("errors") or [] if item.get("role", "raised") != "caught"))
    if not (symbols or modules or config or errors):
        return ""
The routine verifies that the input facts dictionary is non-empty and contains an active claims payload. It extracts symbol lists, deduplicates dependency target module paths using dict.fromkeys(), extracts configuration references, and compiles error entries that represent raised (non-caught) exceptions. If all collections are empty, the method returns "".

docs.title: Formatting and Block Assembly
docs.text:
lines = ["VERIFIED FACTS OF THIS FILE (extracted from it and checked against its source code):"]
    if symbols:
        lines.append(
            "Symbols — document every one; copy each signature as written here (one marked 'start of the declaration' continues in the source: copy it in full from there):"
        )
        for symbol in symbols:
            owner = f"{symbol['parent']}." if symbol.get("parent") else ""
            visibility = f", {symbol['visibility']}" if symbol.get("visibility") else ""
            signature, partial = _fact_signature(symbol)
            marker = " — start of the declaration" if partial else ""
            lines.append(
                f"- {symbol.get('kind') or 'symbol'} {owner}{symbol['name']}{visibility} (line {symbol['line']}): {_code_span(signature)}{marker}"
            )
    if modules:
        lines.append("Project files this file imports — See Also must link each of them:")
        lines.extend(f"- {module} (doc: {doc_paths.get(module, module + '.md')})" for module in modules)
    if config:
        lines.append("Configuration it reads: " + ", ".join(f"{item['name']} ({item.get('kind') or 'config'})" for item in config))
    if errors:
        lines.append("Errors it raises or defines: " + ", ".join(errors))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
The assembly phase structures the extracted components into bulleted sections. Symbols are rendered with their kind, qualified parent ownership, visibility level, declaration line number, and sanitized signature. Target dependencies are mapped against the doc_paths dictionary to supply exact (doc: ...) Markdown link targets. Configuration accessors and raised errors are formatted into comma-delimited summaries.

docs.title: build_facts_focus_note()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_facts_focus_note(lines: list[tuple[int, str]], limit: int = FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT) -> str:

Description: Constructs the {focus_note} prompt segment for follow-up passes of extract_facts.md. When an initial extraction pass fails to account for lines that appear to contain code declarations or import statements, this helper formats up to limit (default 60) uncovered lines with their 1-based line numbers, truncating oversized or minified lines to _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS to instruct the model to report facts specifically on those omitted lines.

Parameters: * lines (list[tuple[int, str]]): Sequence of (line_number, line_text) tuples representing uncovered source lines. * limit (int, optional): Maximum number of lines to explicitly detail before appending an aggregate count of remaining lines. Defaults to FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT (60).

Returns: * str: Formatted follow-up instruction string.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def build_facts_focus_note(lines: list[tuple[int, str]], limit: int = FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT) -> str:
    """The ``{focus_note}`` of an extract_facts.md follow-up: the uncovered lines a first pass left out."""

    def shown_line(text: str) -> str:
        text = text.strip()
        return text if len(text) <= _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS else text[: _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS - 3] + "..."

    shown = "\n".join(f"  {number}: {shown_line(text)}" for number, text in lines[:limit])
    more = f"\n  ... and {len(lines) - limit} more such lines" if len(lines) > limit else ""
    return (
        "FOLLOW-UP: a first pass over this file reported nothing for the lines below, which look like declarations "
        "or imports. Report ONLY the facts on these lines, with the same four lists and rules; a line that is not a "
        "declaration a reader looks up (a local variable, a statement) gets nothing.\n"
        f"Lines:\n{shown}{more}\n"
    )

The nested helper shown_line strips whitespace and clamps lines longer than _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS (200 characters) by appending ellipses (...). The formatted lines are joined with 2-space indentation. If the list exceeds the specified limit, an aggregate trailer (... and N more such lines) is appended, signaling the model that additional uncovered lines exist in the file.

docs.title: parse_facts_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_facts_response(response, keys: tuple = FACTS_KEYS) -> dict:

Description: Parses and validates the structured YAML response emitted by extract_facts.md (or extract_manifest.md). To prevent silent data loss from LLM formatting quirks, the function executes a four-phase parsing and recovery routine: it checks for truncation, extracts the fenced YAML payload, quotes indicator-prefixed identifiers (e.g., @pkg/name, *args), rewrites plain scalar code snippets into block scalars, and falls back to item-by-item chunk recovery via _salvage_yaml_lists() if standard parsing fails. It ensures all scalar values remain raw strings via yaml.BaseLoader to prevent automatic type coercion of strings like "on", "404", or "3.10".

Parameters: * response (str | Any): The model response text or TruncatedResponse object. * keys (tuple, optional): The expected top-level list keys in the payload. Defaults to FACTS_KEYS (("symbols", "dependencies", "config", "errors")).

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing lists of mapping items for each key in keys, plus an "unparsed" integer key indicating the count of lost or invalid items.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the response is flagged as truncated, if no ```yaml fence is detected, or if no valid facts lists can be recovered.

docs.title: Phase 1: Truncation Check and Markdown Fence Extraction
docs.text:
if getattr(response, "truncated", False):
        raise ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed")
    match = _FACTS_BLOCK_RE.search(response) or _FACTS_OPEN_RE.search(response)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Failed to parse YAML: no ```yaml block in the facts reply")
    indent = match.group(1)
    yaml_str = _quote_indicator_values("\n".join(line.removeprefix(indent) for line in match.group(2).split("\n")))
    unparsed = 0
Execution begins by verifying response integrity via getattr(response, "truncated", False). The function then searches for fenced YAML code blocks using _FACTS_BLOCK_RE (closed fence matching the indentation of the opening fence) or _FACTS_OPEN_RE (an open fence extending to end-of-string). Any leading indentation on the opening fence is stripped uniformly across all lines to preserve internal YAML indentation hierarchies.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cascading Deserialization and List Salvaging
docs.text:
try:
        data = _load_strings(yaml_str)
    except Exception:
        try:
            data = _load_strings(_block_quotes(yaml_str))
        except Exception:
            data, unparsed = _salvage_yaml_lists(_block_quotes(yaml_str), keys)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not any(key in data for key in keys):
        raise ValueError("Failed to parse YAML: no fact lists in the facts reply")
The deserialization pipeline applies a three-tiered fallback sequence. It first attempts _load_strings(yaml_str). If that fails (typically due to unescaped colons in signatures), it applies _block_quotes() to convert plain scalars into |- block scalars and retries. If parsing still fails, it invokes _salvage_yaml_lists() to isolate individual lists and salvage items item-by-item, tracking the count of corrupted items in unparsed. If the final result is not a dictionary containing at least one expected key, a terminal ValueError is raised.

docs.title: Phase 3: Structural Validation and Unparsed Metric Calculation
docs.text:
result = {}
    for key in keys:
        items = data.get(key)
        items = items if isinstance(items, list) else []
        result[key] = [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
        unparsed += len(items) - len(result[key])
    result["unparsed"] = unparsed
    return result
In the post-processing phase, the function iterates through the expected keys. Missing or non-list entries default to empty lists. List items are filtered to ensure only dictionary mappings are preserved; any non-dict entries (such as stray strings or incomplete syntax artifacts) are discarded and increment the unparsed counter. The aggregated dictionary, including the final "unparsed" metric, is returned to the caller.

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Constructs the prompt for the DeterministicFileMapper pipeline node in API-reference documentation mode. It formats instructions requesting the LLM to classify repository files into actionable code files (containing APIs, classes, and logic) versus package manifests (such as package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod), while explicitly excluding non-code assets, UI layouts, configs, build scripts, and static documentation.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The display name or identifier of the project being processed. * file_listing (str): Pre-formatted directory tree or indexed file listing generated by utils.files.build_directory_tree.

Returns: * str: The complete prompt string instructing the LLM to return a YAML structure containing code and manifests index lists.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files.

    Used in api-reference mode to identify which files are actual code modules
    (APIs, functions, classes, business logic) vs. UI layouts, configs, assets, and which of the
    others are manifests that declare the names the code imports itself by (ExtractFacts reads those).
    """
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:\n\n"
        f"{file_listing}\n\n"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.\n"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.\n\n"
        f"Separately, list the MANIFESTS among the other files: files that declare a package, module, crate or "
        f"workspace name, or import path aliases, for this project's own code (for example package.json, "
        f"tsconfig.json, go.mod, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, composer.json, pom.xml, build.gradle, "
        f"*.csproj, mix.exs, pubspec.yaml, *.gemspec).\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY YAML with the file indices of both lists:\n\n"
        f"```yaml\ncode:\n  - 0\n  - 1\n  - 3\nmanifests:\n  - 2\n```"
    )

The function interpolates project_name and file_listing into a prompt template that outlines exclusion rules and manifest patterns. It specifies a rigid YAML output schema with code: and manifests: list properties containing integer indices.

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Constructs the prompt used to generate a structured 4-point technical brief of a completed documentation chapter. Summaries produced from this prompt are passed into downstream chapter generation contexts to ensure continuity, prevent redundant explanations, and align architectural cross-references across chapters.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): Positional 1-based index of the chapter. * abstraction_name (str): Title or architectural abstraction topic covered in the chapter. * chapter_content (str): Full Markdown content of the generated chapter. * language (str, optional): Target language for the summary generation. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The complete prompt string specifying the required technical summary format.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    """Build the prompt for generating a technical summary of a written chapter.

    Used after each chapter is generated to create a concise technical summary
    for cross-chapter context. The summary is fed into subsequent chapters'
    prompts so the LLM maintains coherence across the full document.

    The summary captures 4 technical dimensions with 3-5 sentences each:
    1. Component scope & responsibility
    2. Key classes/services/functions and their roles
    3. Implementation patterns & architectural decisions
    4. Inter-component interfaces & dependencies
    """
    lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )

The method injects an optional language directive (Write the entire summary in <Language>.) whenever language is not "english". It frames the prompt around four technical dimensions: Component Scope & Responsibility, Key Technical Elements, Implementation Patterns & Architecture, and System Integration & Dependencies. Each dimension mandates 3 to 5 sentences to maintain consistent information density across chapter briefs.

docs.title: _fact_signature()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fact_signature(symbol: dict) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Normalizes and cleans a symbol's raw signature string for display within prompt context blocks. It strips leading language decorators or attributes (such as @property, #[inline], or [Obsolete]), collapses multiline signatures and internal whitespace into a single line, detects whether the signature was cut short (due to upstream truncation, unbalanced parentheses/brackets, or exceeding _FACT_SIGNATURE_CHARS), and appends a trailing ellipsis if partial.

Parameters: * symbol (dict): The symbol facts dictionary containing keys such as "signature" and "truncated".

Returns: * tuple[str, bool]: A 2-tuple (text, partial) containing the sanitized single-line signature string and a boolean flag indicating whether the signature is truncated or incomplete.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _fact_signature(symbol: dict) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """A verified signature for the prompt: ``(one-line text, cut short)``."""
    lines = str(symbol.get("signature", "")).split("\n")
    while len(lines) > 1 and re.match(r"\s*(?:@|#\[|\[[A-Z])", lines[0]):  # @property, #[inline], [Obsolete]
        lines = lines[1:]
    text = " ".join(" ".join(lines).split())
    code = re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'", "", text)
    partial = bool(symbol.get("truncated")) or code.count("(") > code.count(")") or code.count("[") > code.count("]")
    if len(text) > _FACT_SIGNATURE_CHARS:
        text, partial = text[:_FACT_SIGNATURE_CHARS].rstrip(), True
    return (text + " …" if partial else text), partial

The function splits the signature on line breaks and drops leading lines matching common decorator patterns across Python, Rust, and C#. It collapses internal whitespace sequences via " ".join(" ".join(lines).split()). To detect structural truncation accurately without being misled by brackets inside string literals, it strips quoted literals via re.sub before counting parentheses and square brackets. If brackets are unbalanced, if the symbol is explicitly marked truncated, or if text length exceeds _FACT_SIGNATURE_CHARS (200 characters), partial is set to True and the string is truncated with an appended " …".

docs.title: _code_span()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _code_span(text: str) -> str:

Description: Wraps a given string into a Markdown inline code span such that backticks contained within the string cannot prematurely close the span. It calculates the longest run of consecutive backtick characters present in text, creates a fence delimiter with one additional backtick, and adds padding spaces if the text itself contains backticks.

Parameters: * text (str): The raw text to wrap inside an inline code span.

Returns: * str: The formatted inline code span string.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _code_span(text: str) -> str:
    """*text* as inline code that its own backticks cannot close (a run one longer than any inside, padded)."""
    fence = "`" * (max((len(run) for run in re.findall(r"`+", text)), default=0) + 1)
    return f"{fence} {text} {fence}" if "`" in text else f"{fence}{text}{fence}"

The function uses re.findall(r"+", text)to inspect all contiguous backtick substrings. It determines the maximum run length and constructs an outer fence ofmax_len + 1backticks. Iftextcontains any backticks, CommonMark rules require space padding (f"{fence} {text} {fence}"`) to prevent the boundary backticks from coalescing with internal backticks.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings(text: str):

Description: Deserializes a YAML string using yaml.BaseLoader. Standard YAML parsers automatically convert unquoted tokens such as 404, on, off, yes, no, or version numbers like 3.10 into integers, booleans, or floats. By enforcing BaseLoader, this helper guarantees that all scalar values are parsed purely as raw Python str instances, preventing data corruption when extracting code identifiers, status codes, and configuration keys.

Parameters: * text (str): YAML formatted string.

Returns: * Any: Parsed Python data structure consisting exclusively of str, list, and dict types.

Raises: * yaml.YAMLError: If the YAML string contains syntactic errors.

Example: 

def _load_strings(text: str):
    """YAML with every scalar kept as the reply's text: ``404``, ``on``, ``3.10`` stay strings."""
    return yaml.load(text, Loader=yaml.BaseLoader)  # BaseLoader builds only str / list / dict: safe

This helper wraps yaml.load(text, Loader=yaml.BaseLoader). Because BaseLoader does not resolve scalar tags to arbitrary Python objects or native primitive types (like booleans and numbers), it also provides a security boundary against arbitrary object instantiation during YAML deserialization.

docs.title: _quote_indicator_values()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _quote_indicator_values(text: str) -> str:

Description: Pre-processes raw YAML strings to quote unquoted values led by YAML indicator characters. When models extract symbols or package names such as @acme/api, #db/*, or *args, YAML parsers treat @ as a reserved indicator, # as a comment, and * as an anchor alias. This helper matches target field lines (name, entry, alias, target, base, parent) and safely encloses such values in double quotes.

Parameters: * text (str): Raw YAML text extracted from the LLM response.

Returns: * str: Sanitized YAML string with indicator-led values enclosed in escaped double quotes.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _quote_indicator_values(text: str) -> str:
    return _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE.sub(lambda m: m[1] + '"' + m[2].replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"', text)

The function executes a regular expression substitution using _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE. For matched key-value pairs where the value begins with an indicator character (@, `, #, *, &, !, %), the regex callback preserves the key and leading whitespace (m[1]), escapes existing backslashes and quotes within the value (m[2]), and wraps the sanitized value in double quotes.

docs.title: _block_quotes()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _block_quotes(text: str) -> str:

Description: Converts unquoted or malformed multi-line scalar values on signature: or evidence: lines into YAML literal block scalars (|-). A frequent LLM mistake is outputting code signatures (e.g., signature: def run(self):) or evidence lines containing colons or # characters as plain unquoted scalars, which breaks YAML syntax. This helper detects such occurrences and rewrites them into properly indented block scalars.

Parameters: * text (str): YAML text containing potentially malformed plain scalar lines.

Returns: * str: Transformed YAML string with affected scalar lines formatted as block scalars.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _block_quotes(text: str) -> str:
    return _PLAIN_QUOTE_RE.sub(lambda m: m[0] if _WHOLE_SCALAR_RE.match(m[3]) else f"{m[1]}{m[2]}: |-\n{' ' * (len(m[1]) + 2)}{m[3]}", text)

The regular expression _PLAIN_QUOTE_RE captures signature: and evidence: lines. If _WHOLE_SCALAR_RE matches the value (confirming it is already a fully quoted scalar or a valid block scalar indicator), the match is retained unmodified (m[0]). Otherwise, the value is rewritten as : |-\n followed by the original value indented with two additional spaces relative to the parent key's indentation.

docs.title: _salvage_yaml_lists()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _salvage_yaml_lists(yaml_str: str, keys: tuple) -> tuple[dict, int]:

Description: High-resilience fallback parser for severely malformed YAML payloads. When document-level parsing fails, this helper partitions the YAML text by top-level keys (symbols, dependencies, config, errors). If a list chunk still fails to parse as a whole, it splits the list along item boundary prefixes (-) based on indentation and parses each item individually. Successfully parsed items are retained, while unparseable items increment a lost item counter.

Parameters: * yaml_str (str): The corrupted YAML string. * keys (tuple): Tuple of top-level list keys to look for.

Returns: * tuple[dict, int]: A 2-tuple (parsed, lost) where parsed maps recovered keys to lists of valid dictionary items, and lost is the integer count of discarded items.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def _salvage_yaml_lists(yaml_str: str, keys: tuple) -> tuple[dict, int]:
    """Parse each top-level ``key:`` list of a broken YAML block on its own; a list that still fails is
    parsed item by item (split at its own ``- `` indentation) and keeps the items that parse.
    Returns ``(lists, number of items lost)``."""
    names = "|".join(keys)
    parsed, lost = {}, 0
    for chunk in re.split(rf"(?m)^(?=(?:{names})\s*:)", yaml_str):
        head = re.match(rf"({names})\s*:", chunk)
        if not head:
            continue
        try:
            part = _load_strings(chunk)
        except Exception:
            part = None
        if isinstance(part, dict):
            parsed.update(part)
            continue
        body = chunk[head.end() :]
        first = re.search(r"(?m)^([ \t]*)- ", body)
        if not first:
            continue
        indent = first.group(1)
        items = []
        for piece in re.split(rf"(?m)^(?={re.escape(indent)}- )", body):
            if not piece.startswith(f"{indent}- "):
                continue
            text = "\n".join(line.removeprefix(indent) for line in piece.split("\n"))
            try:
                item = _load_strings(text)
            except Exception:
                lost += 1
                continue
            if isinstance(item, list) and item and isinstance(item[0], dict):
                items.append(item[0])
            else:
                lost += 1
        parsed[head.group(1)] = items
    return parsed, lost

The function splits the text across key names using a multiline positive lookahead (?m)^(?=(?:{names})\s*:). For each chunk, it tests whether the entire section parses via _load_strings(chunk). If parsing fails, it determines the indentation level of the initial list item (first.group(1)). It then splits the body across item boundaries matching (?m)^(?={indent}- ). Each piece has its outer indentation stripped and is parsed individually via _load_strings. Valid mapping entries are appended to the list, while malformed pieces increment lost.

docs.title: Internal Regular Expressions and Constants
docs.text:
The module declares internal constants and compiled regular expressions to support tokenization, fence matching, and syntax normalization:

Identifier Type Value / Pattern Description _INDEX_RE re.Pattern r"^\s*(\d+)\s*(?:#.*)?$" Matches solitary file indices, optionally followed by comments (e.g., 3, "3 # path/to/file.py"). _INDEX_RANGE_RE re.Pattern r"^\s*(\d+)\s*(?:-|\.\.\|–\|to)\s*(\d+)\s*(?:#.*)?$" Matches numeric range syntax (e.g., "0-3", "4..7", "1 to 5"). _FACTS_BLOCK_RE re.Pattern r"(?msi)^([ ]*)```ya?ml[^ ]* (.*?)^\1```[ ]*$" Matches a closed Markdown YAML code block, capturing indentation to ensure closing fence symmetry. _FACTS_OPEN_RE re.Pattern r"(?msi)^([ ]*)```ya?ml[^ ]* (.*)" Matches an unclosed YAML code block extending to the end of the text. _PLAIN_QUOTE_RE re.Pattern r"(?m)^([ ]*(?:- )?)(signature\|evidence):[ ]+(\S.*)$" Captures unquoted scalar values assigned to signature or evidence keys. _WHOLE_SCALAR_RE re.Pattern r"""^(?:"(?:\.\|[^"\])*"\|'(?:''\|[^'])*'\|[\|>][-+0-9]*)[ ]*(?:#.*)?$""" Matches valid quoted strings or block indicators (\|-, >). _INDICATOR_VALUE_RE re.Pattern r"(?m)^([ ]*(?:- )?(?:name\|entry\|alias\|target\|base\|parent):[ ]+)([@#&!%]\S||>\S)(?:[ ]+#.)?$"` Detects values prefixed with YAML indicators requiring defensive quoting. _FACT_SIGNATURE_CHARS int 200 Maximum character length of a signature displayed in a chapter prompt before truncation. _FOCUS_LINE_CHARS int 200 Maximum character length for uncovered source lines rendered in focus notes.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements a strict fail-fast approach for fatal conditions, paired with multi-tiered recovery for recoverable syntax flaws:

  1. Truncation Detection: The parsing functions (parse_yaml_response, parse_grouping_response, and parse_facts_response) inspect incoming response payloads using getattr(response, "truncated", False). When an upstream LLM client (such as llm_anthropic, llm_gemini, or llm_openrouter) emits a TruncatedResponse due to generation token exhaustion, the parser raises an immediate ValueError: 

    if getattr(response, "truncated", False):
    raise ValueError("LLM response was truncated before the YAML block completed")
    This prevents pipeline execution from proceeding with partial data structures that would silently drop modules, symbols, or sections.

  2. Cascading YAML Recovery: In parse_facts_response, parsing errors trigger a multi-stage fallback:

  3. Stage 1 (Strict): Raw extraction using yaml.BaseLoader.
  4. Stage 2 (Scalar Normalization): If Stage 1 fails, _block_quotes() transforms unquoted colons and hash characters on signature: and evidence: lines into |- literal block scalars.
  5. Stage 3 (Item-by-Item Salvage): If Stage 2 fails, _salvage_yaml_lists() splits the payload into individual section chunks and parses items individually along - item boundaries.

  6. Loss Accounting: Dropped items are tallied in the "unparsed" field so upstream validation stages can audit extraction completeness.

  7. Malformed Grouping Recovery: In parse_grouping_response, invalid backtick formatting around section roles (e.g., role:core`) is scrubbed using regex, and section blocks are parsed independently. If the primary"sections"list cannot be constructed, a descriptiveValueError` is raised.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/thinking.py module establishes the configuration and resolution engine for managing reasoning effort ("thinking flows") across all Large Language Model (LLM) invocation sites in the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Tunable reasoning models (including Anthropic Claude 3.7 / Opus, Google Gemini 2.5 and 3.x, and DeepSeek backends exposed via OpenRouter) provide configurable reasoning token allocations. Because reasoning tokens introduce latency and consumption overhead, enforcing a single uniform thinking budget across heterogeneous pipeline tasks is suboptimal. Heavy architectural synthesis operations require extensive cognitive reasoning, whereas mechanical transformations, file filtering, and internationalization tasks require minimal or no reasoning overhead.

This module provides an abstraction that decouples pipeline node identifiers from provider-specific thinking configurations. At its core, the module manages an ordered scale of abstract reasoning tiers (minimal through max) and maps them to pipeline execution call sites (NODE_KEYS). Thinking plans are resolved through a deterministic precedence hierarchy: explicit per-node overrides take precedence over global settings, which in turn override predefined profile matrices (economy, balanced, quality, max). The default auto profile dynamically resolves to balanced when communicating with models capable of fine-grained reasoning control (ANTHROPIC, GEMINI, OPENROUTER), and resolves to off (using provider defaults) when dispatching to local or OpenAI-compatible backends like Ollama.

At runtime, orchestration nodes query their designated thinking level through resolve_thinking_level(), and downstream provider adapters invoke clamp_level() to project abstract levels onto concrete model-supported capabilities (such as Anthropic output effort configurations, Gemini integer budgets or discrete levels, and OpenRouter reasoning fields).

The scale extends from minimal (primarily exposed by select OpenRouter backends) up to max (reserved for intensive architectural synthesis in explicit configurations). Predefined operational profiles reference tiers from low to max, while clamp_level relies on the positional indexing of this tuple to perform nearest-neighbor mathematical distance calculations when negotiating provider capabilities.
